Blog
How We Reduced the Impact of Zombie Clients
By Samantha Frank ·
June 4, 2025
Every night, right around midnight (mainly
UTC
), a horde of zombies wakes up and clamors for … digital certificates!
The zombies in question are abandoned or misconfigured Internet servers and ACME clients that have been set to request certificates from Let’s Encrypt. As our certificates
last for at most 90 days
, these zombie clients’ software knows that their certificates are out-of-date and need to be replaced. What they don’t realize is that their quest for new certificates is doomed! These devices are cursed to seek certificates again and again, never receiving them.
But they do use up a lot of certificate authority resources in the process.
The Zombie Client Problem
Unlike a human being, software doesn’t give up in frustration, or try to modify its approach, when it repeatedly fails at the same task. Our emphasis on automation means that the vast majority of Let’s Encrypt certificate renewals are performed by automated software. This is great when those renewals succeed, but it also means that forgotten clients and devices can continue requesting renewals unsuccessfully for months, or even years.
How might that happen? Most often, it happens when a device no longer has a domain name pointed to it. The device itself doesn’t know that this has changed, so it treats renewal failures as transient even though they are actually permanent. For instance:
An organization may have allowed a domain name registration to lapse because it is no longer needed, but its servers are still configured to request certs for it.
Or, a home user stopped using a particular dynamic-DNS domain with a network-attached storage device, but is still using that device at home. The device doesn’t realize that the user no longer expects to use the name, so it keeps requesting certs for it.
Or, a web hosting or CDN customer migrated to a different service provider, but never informed the old service provider. The old service provider’s servers keep requesting certs unsuccessfully. If the customer was in a free service tier, there might not be invoices or charges reminding the customer to cancel the service.
Or any number of other, subtler changes in a subscriber’s infrastructure, such as changing a firewall rule or some webserver configuration.
At the scale of Let’s Encrypt, which now covers
hundreds of millions of names
, scenarios like these have become common, and their impact has become substantial. In 2024, we noticed that about half of all certificate requests to the Let’s Encrypt ACME API came from about a million accounts that never successfully complete any validations. Many of these had completed validations and issued certificates sometime in the past, but nowadays every single one of their validation attempts fails, and they show no signs that this will change anytime soon.
Unfortunately, trying to validate those futile requests still uses resources. Our CA software has to generate challenges, reach out and attempt to validate them over the Internet, detect and report failures, and record all of the associated information in our databases and audit logs. And over time, we’ve seen more and more recurring failures: accounts that always fail their issuance requests have been growing at around 18% per year.
In January, we mentioned that we had been addressing the zombie client problem
through our rate limit system
. This post provides more detail on that progress.
Our Rate Limit Philosophy
If you’ve used Let’s Encrypt as a subscriber, you may have run into one of our
rate limits
at some point, maybe during your initial setup process. We have eight different kinds of rate limits in place now; as our January post describes, they’ve become more algorithmically sophisticated and grown to address a wider range of problems. A key principle for Let’s Encrypt is that our rate limiting is not a punishment. We don’t think of rate limits as a way of retaliating against a client for misbehavior. Rate limits are simply a tool to maximize the efficient use of our limited resources and prevent people and programs from using up those resources for no constructive purpose.
We’ve consistently tried to design our rate limit mechanisms in line with that philosophy. So if a misconfiguration or misunderstanding has caused excessive requests in the past, we’re still happy to welcome the user in question back and start issuing them certificates again—once the problem has been addressed. We want the rate limits to put a brake on wasteful use of our systems, but not to frustrate users who are actively trying to make Let’s Encrypt work for them.
In addition, we’ve always implemented our rate limits to err on the side of permissiveness. For example, if the Redis instances where rate limits are tracked have an outage or lose data, the system is designed to permit more issuance rather than less issuance as a result.

通过这些措施，Let’s Encrypt有效减少了僵尸客户端带来的影响，确保系统能更好地服务于合法用户。

data.article_summary: Langfuse宣布将其所有产品功能开源，包括LLM-as-a-judge评估、注释队列、提示实验和 playground，所有这些功能现在都可以在MIT许可证下自托管使用。此举旨在加速开发者在其应用中的迭代速度，并获取社区反馈，以进一步改善项目。公司将专注于Langfuse Cloud和企业平台团队的自托管服务，并将商业许可代码限制在企业安全相关功能上。通过开放核心功能，Langfuse希望加深社区信任，加速技术采用，并更快地进行迭代。目前已有超过8000个自托管实例，公司期望此举巩固其在LLMOps领域的首选地位。

44180954.article_content:
June 4, 2025
Doubling Down on Open Source
Today we are open sourcing all remaining Product Features in Langfuse under the MIT license
Marc
Clemens
Max
The LLM landscape is changing rapidly and so are the workflows used to build and improve LLM apps. Today,
we are open sourcing all Product Features in Langfuse
to enable our community to iterate on their applications faster and provide our project with feedback on where to go next.
Newly open sourced features include managed
LLM-as-a-judge evaluations
,
annotation queues
,
prompt experiments
and
the playground
, all of which are now freely available to self-host under the MIT license.
If you are self-hosting Langfuse already today,
upgrade your deployment to the
latest version
. You will find a more powerful version of Langfuse.
Why are we doing this?
Langfuse is building the
open source LLM Engineering Platform
. We are building
the
platform to observe and improve LLM applications.
We are constantly shipping to be the technology of choice for our community. This requires trust, feedback and buy-in from our community.
We re-visited the gated features in our Enterprise Edition. If we want to be the first choice in the market, we need to allow our community to
cover the entire dev cycle in our FOSS version
. Features like LLM-as-a-Judge, Evals, or our Playground are market standard at this point and should be freely available.
But why stop there?
The best platform for developers has to be open at its core. By
removing commercial barriers from our product features
, we’re fostering deeper trust, collaborating on contributions, accelerating adoption, gathering richer community feedback, and iterating faster than ever.
Our Open Source Journey
Langfuse was
launched
as an open source project.
This was based on a few
core beliefs
:
Data captured by Langfuse should be freely accessible
The AI landscape changes every week – Langfuse must integrate agnostically with all models and application stacks
Great teams deserve the flexibility to extend the platform to support custom workflows
This positioning resonates and today we are doubling down on it.
Langfuse has been an open core company from the start.
Our core just expanded significantly
and our periphery shrunk. Commercially licensed code is now limited to features for Enterprise Security and Platform Teams (e.g. SCIM, Audit Logs, Data Retention Policies – regular
SSO
is and continues to be MIT licensed).

As we open source previously commercial features, we are fully investing our commercial focus in Langfuse Cloud and Enterprise platform teams in self-hosting.
Thousands of Langfuse Deployments
There are more than 8,000 monthly active self-hosted instances of Langfuse out in the wild. This boggles our minds.
We expect that today’s changes solidify Langfuse as the first choice for a powerful and truly open source platform in LLMOps.
Today is the day to start self-hosting Langfuse. Head over to
our self hosting docs
and use the new
terraform modules
for deploying Langfuse at production-scale.

data.author: vinhnx
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： prompt工程的有效性和必要性

不同观点：
• **支持prompt工程**：
   - **DebtDeflation**：认为存在三种核心技术：情境学习、思维链和结构化输出，可能还可以加上角色提示。RAG（检索增强生成）则是对模型进行上下文总结。
   - **orochimaaru**：虽然复杂问题不能单靠prompt解决，但可以通过分解任务和示例让模型运行良好。
   - **Kiyo-Lynn**：最初认为模型不够好，后来发现问题在于自己没有清晰思考需求，清晰的prompt有助于模型产生更好结果。

• **质疑prompt工程的价值**：
   - **haolez**：长而复杂的prompt可能给人一种控制感和工程化的错觉，但可能不会显著提升效果。个人经验是使用简单、简约的prompt，并通过几次迭代进行微调。
   - **yuvadam**：认为“过度工程化”，只需粘贴原始代码或错误信息，直接提问，模型足够聪明来理解。

• **反对prompt工程的概念**：
   - **bsoles**：认为“prompt工程”这一说法不成立，写有意义的句子不应被称为工程。
   - **leshow**、**nexoft**：认为用“工程”来形容写prompt显得不严肃，应该称为“常识”。
   - **jwr**：认为“prompt工程”这一名称令人反感，认为没有科学和工程的基础，只是随意尝试。

• **对prompt工程的客观需求**：
   - **ColinEberhardt**：认为目前有很多不必要的prompt指南，熟悉工具后自然会知道该用什么prompt。

• **对prompt工程效果的质疑**：
   - **MontagFTB**：质疑这些prompt修改的效果如何量化，如何确定模型输出了更好的结果。

• **个人经验分享**：
   - **namanyayg**：分享了自己写的prompt，并提供了一个博客链接供参考。

补充讨论：
• **对prompt工程的定义和范围的争议**：一些用户认为写prompt不应被称为“工程”，而另一些用户则认为存在特定的技术和方法。
• **实际应用中的经验分享**：一些用户分享了他们在实际工作中如何有效使用prompt的例子，如分解任务、明确输入输出等。
• **对模型性能的评价**：有用户提到，prompt的质量不仅影响模型的表现，还反映出用户自身对需求的理解。

争议焦点：
• **prompt工程是否是一个有效的概念**：一部分用户认为写prompt是一种工程技术，另一部分用户则认为这只是一个语言表达问题，不应被称为工程。
• **长而复杂的prompt是否有必要**：一些用户认为简单的prompt足够有效，而另一些用户则认为复杂的prompt能提供更好的控制和效果。

data.title: Giant planet discovered orbiting tiny star
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 天文学家发现了一颗围绕极小恒星运行的巨型行星，这一发现挑战了现有的行星形成理论。这颗名为TOI-6894的恒星是一颗质量仅为太阳20%的红矮星，却拥有一颗名为TOI-6894b的巨型气态行星。根据核心吸积理论，低质量恒星周围不易形成如此巨大的行星，因为原行星盘中的物质不足以支持巨行星的形成。然而，TOI-6894b的发现表明现有模型并不完善，可能需要考虑其他形成机制，如中间核心吸积过程或盘的不稳定性。此外，TOI-6894b的大气异常寒冷，为研究巨行星的大气特性提供了宝贵机会。这一发现将帮助科学家更好地理解行星形成过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TOI-6894b行星的特性和其对现有行星形成理论的影响

不同观点：
• [karim79的观点]  
现有行星形成理论无法解释TOI-6894b的存在，让其对当前天文学理解产生质疑。每当遇到这种理论无法解释的现象时，都会感到失望。

• [narag的观点]  
TOI-6894b是一个低密度的气态巨行星，其半径比土星大，但质量只有土星的一半。土星本身密度很低，甚至低于水的密度（可以浮在水上），而TOI-6894b的密度可能更低。这表明这类行星虽然罕见，但并非完全没有 precedent（先例）。

• [mynegation的观点]  
通过快速计算，TOI-6894系统中恒星与行星的质量比约为1400倍，与太阳和木星之间的质量比（1047倍）相比，虽然有差距但并不算过于极端。然而，这个差距可能跨越了某些理论设定的临界值。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：TOI-6894b的存在是否挑战了当前的行星形成理论，特别是关于气体巨行星形成的标准模型。
• 论据：karim79认为这种行星不应存在，指出现有理论的局限性；narag指出土星也有类似的低密度特性，表明这类行星并非完全无法理解；mynegation则通过具体数据比较，指出该系统与已知系统的相似性和可能突破理论阈值的地方。
• 例子：narag提到了土星的低密度特性作为对比，mynegation则通过计算恒星与行星的质量比来说明系统的特殊性。

这些讨论共同围绕TOI-6894b行星的特殊性质及其对天文学理论的影响，展示了不同角度的理解和争议。

44183175.article_content:
Giant planet discovered orbiting tiny star
4 June 2025
Astronomers at UCL and the University of Warwick, as part of a global collaboration including partners in Chile, USA and Europe, have discovered the smallest known star to host a transiting giant planet, which should not exist under leading planet formation theories.
Star TOI-6894 is just like many in our galaxy, a small red dwarf, and only ~20% of the mass of our Sun. Like many small stars, it is not expected to provide suitable conditions for the formation and hosting of a large planet.
However, as published today in
Nature Astronomy
, an international team of astronomers have found the unmistakable signature of a giant planet, called TOI-6894b, orbiting this tiny star.
This system has been discovered as part of a large-scale investigation of TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) data, looking for giant planets around low-mass stars, led by Dr Edward Bryant, who completed this work at UCL’s Mullard Space Science Laboratory and the University of Warwick.
Dr Bryant said: “I was very excited by this discovery. I originally searched through TESS observations of more than 91,000 low-mass red-dwarf stars looking for giant planets.
“Then, using observations taken with one of the world’s largest telescopes, ESO’s VLT, I discovered TOI-6894b, a giant planet transiting the lowest mass star known to date to host such a planet. We did not expect planets like TOI-6894b to be able to form around stars this low-mass. This discovery will be a cornerstone for understanding the extremes of giant planet formation.”
The planet (TOI-6894b) is a low-density gas giant with a radius a little larger than Saturn’s but with only ~50% of Saturn’s mass. The star (TOI-6894) is the lowest mass star to have a transiting giant planet discovered to date and is just 60% the size of the next smallest star to host such a planet.
Dr Vincent Van Eylen, from UCL’s Mullard Space Science Laboratory, said: “It’s an intriguing discovery. We don’t really understand how a star with so little mass can form such a massive planet! This is one of the goals of the search for more exoplanets. By finding planetary systems different from our solar system, we can test our models and better understand how our own solar system formed.”
Dr Daniel Bayliss, based at the University of Warwick said: “Most stars in our galaxy are actually small stars exactly like this, with low masses and previously thought to not be able to host gas giant planets. So, the fact that this star hosts a giant planet has big implications for the total number of giant planets we estimate exist in our galaxy.”
The most widely held theory of planet formation is called the core accretion theory. A planetary core forms first through accretion (gradual accumulation of material) and as the core becomes more massive, it eventually attracts gases that form an atmosphere. It then gets massive enough to enter a runaway gas accretion process to become a gas giant.
In this theory, the formation of gas giants is harder around low-mass stars because the amount of gas and dust in a protoplanetary disc around the star (the raw material of planet formation) is too limited to allow a massive enough core to form, and the runaway process to occur.
Yet the existence of TOI-6894b (a giant planet orbiting an extremely low-mass star) suggests this model cannot be completely accurate and alternative theories are needed.
Dr Bryant added: “Given the mass of the planet, TOI-6894b could have formed through an intermediate core-accretion process, in which a protoplanet forms and steadily accretes gas without the core becoming massive enough for runaway gas accretion.
“Alternatively, it could have formed because of a gravitationally unstable disc. In some cases, the disc surrounding the star will become unstable due to the gravitational force it exerts on itself. These discs can then fragment, with the gas and dust collapsing to form a planet.”
But the team found that neither theory could completely explain the formation of TOI-6894b from the available data, which leaves the origin of this giant planet as an open question for now.
One avenue to shed light on the mystery of TOI-6894b's formation is a detailed atmospheric analysis. By measuring the distribution of material within the planet, astronomers can determine the size and structure of the planet’s core, which can tell us whether TOI-6894b formed via accretion or via an unstable disc.
This is not the only interesting feature of TOI-6894b’s atmosphere; it is unusually cold for a gas giant. Most of the gas giants found by exoplanet hunters are hot Jupiters, massive gas giants with temperatures of ~1000-2000 Kelvin. TOI-6894b, by comparison, is just 420 Kelvin. The cool temperature alongside other features of this planet, such as the very deep transits, makes it one of the most promising giant planets for astronomers to characterise with a cool atmosphere.
Professor Amaury Triaud, University of Birmingham,

data.title: Interactive MissileMap
data.author: Bender
data.article_summary: MISSILEMAP是由史蒂文斯理工学院艺术与文学学院助理教授Alex Wellerstein开发的互动数据可视化工具，旨在展示导弹射程、精度和弹头威力之间的关系，特别用于帮助理解核弹头和远程导弹的威力。用户可以输入坐标或地名来模拟导弹发射，并查看如圆形误差概率（CEP）、单发摧毁概率（SSPK）等数据。该工具还提供了到NUKEMAP的链接，以了解更多关于核武器爆炸威力的信息。该应用由史蒂文斯理工学院 hosting。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于《Nuclear War: A Scenario》一书情节中的导弹轨迹和潜在核战争情景的合理性分析。

不同观点：
• [credit_guy] 认为书中的情节存在缺陷。他具体指出，朝鲜发射的洲际弹道导弹（ICBM）与美国反击的ICBM轨迹在地理上并不重叠，因此美国因为“不用即失”的恐惧而发射大量ICBM的情节不合理。他还提到，美国导弹飞越俄罗斯领土的部分较少，与书中描述的触发俄罗斯全面反应的情节不符。他通过提供具体导弹轨迹链接支持其观点。

• [alkh] 对能够选择发射预设功能表示赞赏，认为这使得模拟更加现实，但没有直接评论书中的情节合理性。

补充讨论：
• [credit_guy] 详细分析了朝鲜导弹与美国导弹的飞行路径，提供了具体的比较数据，并指出了情节中的逻辑问题，特别是涉及到俄罗斯反应的部分。
• [alkh] 的评论更侧重于工具的实用性，即导弹地图的预设功能，而非书中的具体情节。

争议焦点：书中的导弹轨迹和核战争触发条件是否符合现实地理和战略逻辑。

data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：汽车运输船火灾事件，特别是电动汽车（EVs）是否为火灾源头及其潜在风险

不同观点：
• **[linotype]**：认为新闻标题有误导性。指出在3000辆车中只有800辆是电动汽车，且没有证据表明这些电动汽车是火灾源头。
• **[rkagerer]**：提出如果电动汽车使用设计良好的磷酸铁锂电池（LiFePO4），并配备适当的控制器和低温充电保护，是否能降低火灾风险。这暗示了电池技术对安全性的影响。
• **[xnx]**：怀疑这些事件可能是蓄意破坏或保险欺诈，提到2022年和2023年类似船只火灾事件，认为这些船只可能成为特定目标。
• **[benji-york]**：用调侃的语气询问是否是船头掉落了，虽未提供实质性观点，但反映了对事件原因的某种怀疑态度。
• **[t1234s]**：关心船上电动汽车的品牌，可能想了解某些品牌是否更具火灾风险。
• **[jmclnx]**：提供了一个非付费链接，建议避免使用付费墙链接，方便其他讨论者获取信息，强调信息获取的平等性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于电动汽车是否为此次火灾的主要原因，以及如何通过技术手段（如电池改进）降低火灾风险。
• 另一讨论方向是火灾事件是否涉及人为因素，如蓄意破坏或保险欺诈。
• 信息来源的获取问题也被提及，jmclnx提供非付费链接以便讨论者更广泛地参与。

data.title: OpenAI Release ChatGPT Connectors (Remote MCP)
data.author: joshwarwick15
data.article_summary: OpenAI为ChatGPT推出了面向企业用户的新功能，包括与多种云服务（如Dropbox、Box、Google Drive等）的集成，支持会议录音和转录，并可生成带时间戳的笔记和行动建议。此外，新增了深度研究连接器，支持HubSpot、Linear及部分微软和谷歌工具，帮助用户通过这些来源准备详细的研究报告。同时，MCP连接协议支持让用户可以连接其他工具进行深度研究。这些功能面向所有付费用户，Pro、Team和Enterprise用户还可使用MCP支持。这些更新旨在增强ChatGPT在企业工作环境中的应用。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44182893.article_content:
OpenAI’s ChatGPT is adding new features for business users, including integrations with different cloud services, meeting recordings, and MCP connection support for connecting to tools for deep research.
As part of the launch, ChatGPT is gaining connectors for Dropbox, Box, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Google Drive. This allows ChatGPT to look for information across users’ own services to answer their questions. For instance, an analyst could use the company’s slide deck and documents to build out an investment thesis.
OpenAI said that the new feature will follow an organization’s access control hierarchy.
Recording and transcription of meetings, now a table-stakes feature of the productivity suites, is also now available. The feature can generate notes with time-stamped citations and suggest actions. Users will be able to query for information in their meeting notes, as they can with documents and files across the integrated services. Plus, users can convert action items into a Canvas document,
OpenAI’s tool for writing and coding projects
.
The feature competes with ClickUp, Zoom, and, more recently,
Notion
, which have all added some type of transcription and meeting summarization features to their products.
In addition, the company is introducing deep research connectors for HubSpot, Linear, and select Microsoft and Google tools in beta. OpenAI said that users can now prepare detailed research reports through Deep Research using knowledge and data from these sources, along with web information. OpenAI said connectors are available to all paid users.
Customers can also use MCP (model context protocol) to connect to other tools for deep research. MCP support will be available to Pro, Team, and Enterprise users, the company said.

data.title: Meta found 'covertly tracking' Android users through Instagram and Facebook
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: Meta和Yandex被指控通过其应用程序在Android设备上秘密跟踪用户浏览活动。据荷兰Radboud大学和IMDEA Networks的学者研究发现，Meta的Facebook和Instagram，以及Yandex的Yandex Maps等应用，利用脚本绕过Android安全措施，未经用户同意收集浏览器数据，甚至在隐身模式下也能进行跟踪。Google确认此行为违反其安全和隐私原则，并已采取措施缓解这些技术。Meta表示正在调查并与Google协商解决，而Yandex则否认收集敏感信息。Mozilla和DuckDuckGo等公司已采取行动阻止此类跟踪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应用程序通过手机应用获取用户数据和隐私的追踪行为，以及相关的安全和隐私问题。

不同观点：
• [runevault] 认为公司通过奖励积分等方式诱导用户安装应用程序，目的是获取更多用户数据，且安全难以保障。因此，他选择不安装此类应用。
• [m463] 指出，这种行为不仅限于某家公司，iOS系统也存在类似问题，比如通过深层链接拦截URL。此外，位置服务和跨应用追踪技术也广泛使用。最终，他也选择尽量不安装应用。
• [qnleigh] 对应用程序如何追踪浏览器活动感到好奇，尤其是这种行为如何绕过隐私模式，并质疑谷歌是否应承担部分责任，是否属于已知问题但未及时修复。
• [kfkdjajgjic] 以代码形式讽刺一些应用程序在用户拒绝追踪的情况下仍会进行追踪。
• [ethagnawl] 建议使用这些服务的网站版本而非应用程序，以减少使用频率和数据暴露，尽管用户体验可能有所下降。
• [john01dav] 提出这种行为是否违反计算机欺诈和滥用行为法，认为这些应用绕过沙盒获取其他应用数据可能构成违法行为，且大公司这样做带来的危害更大。
• [iammrpayments] 提到Meta的广告管理界面体验极差，且其“代表”提供的策略往往无效，同时账户被封禁后难以找到真人客服解决问题。
• [GiorgioG] 分享个人经历，删除Facebook和Instagram后不再收到基于 verbal conversation 推送的广告，认为这是对隐私的侵犯。
• [Johnny555] 引用谷歌的回应，确认Meta和Yandex滥用Android系统功能进行隐私侵犯，并质疑谷歌为何未立即下架这些应用，同时希望有办法阻止应用在后台运行。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户提到此类追踪行为的广泛性和技术细节，如深层链接和跨应用追踪（[m463]）。
• 部分用户关注法律和责任问题，认为大公司应为侵犯隐私的行为承担法律责任（[john01dav]）。
• 也有用户分享个人经验，表明对隐私侵犯的实际感受和采取的应对措施（[GiorgioG]）。
• 争议焦点在于大公司如何滥用技术能力进行隐私侵犯，以及谷歌和相关平台在监管和处理这些问题上的责任。

44182204.article_content:
Meta found 'covertly tracking' Android users through Instagram and Facebook
Google says Meta and search engine company Yandex used Android capabilities "in unintended ways that blatantly violate our security and privacy principles".
Mickey Carroll
Science and Technology reporter
Wednesday 4 June 2025 16:45, UK
Image:
File pic: AP
Why you can trust Sky News
Meta and search engine company Yandex have been "covertly tracking" Android users in the background of their devices, according to experts.
Academics at the Radboud University in the Netherlands and IMDEA Networks said they discovered Meta and Yandex have been tracking Android users' browser activity without their consent and then using the data in their apps.
Meta said it was looking into the issue, while Yandex denied collecting any sensitive data.
Gunes Acar, assistant professor at Radboud University, said the "covert" data collection was spotted in January.
He said he discovered Meta's apps, including Facebook and Instagram, and Yandex's apps, such as Yandex Maps, were sitting in the background of Android devices and loading a script that sent data locally back to apps on users' phones.
The scripts bypassed Android's security measures and meant that Meta and Yandex could track what users were doing on web browsers, without the user consenting or even knowing, according to the expert.
"They are bridging these two worlds that we think are separate; web browsing and mobile app activities," Dr Acar told Sky News.
"That's very shocking."
The apps were able to track users' browser data on all major Android browsers, even if the user was in incognito mode, the academics said.
"It's really concerning because it negates every privacy control that you have in modern browsers and also in modern mobile platforms like Android," said Narseo Vallina-Rodriguez, associate professor at IMDEA Networks, to Sky News.
Google
, which owns the Android operating system, confirmed the covert activity to Sky News.
It said Meta and Yandex used
Android's
capabilities "in unintended ways that blatantly violate our security and privacy principles".
What have Meta and Yandex said?
Meta told Sky News it was quickly looking into the issue.
"We are in discussions with Google to address a potential miscommunication regarding the application of their policies," said a Meta spokesperson.
"Upon becoming aware of the concerns, we decided to pause the feature while we work with Google to resolve the issue."
Yandex said it "strictly complies with data protection standards", adding: "The feature in question does not collect any sensitive information and is solely intended to improve personalisation within our apps."
Read more science and tech news:

Coffee 'helps women age more healthily'
Get Sky News on WhatsApp
Follow our channel and never miss an update
Tap here to follow
Meta appeared to have been doing the data tracking for around eight months, while Yandex had since 2017, the academics said.
"We found that Facebook was doing it on roughly 16,000 websites when visited from the EU, [...] Yandex was doing this on 1,300 websites," said Tim Vlummens, a PHD student at KU Leuven who worked on the research.
Google told Sky News it had already "implemented changes to mitigate these invasive techniques and have opened our own investigation and are directly in touch with the parties".

Breaking News

The tech giant did not respond when asked what repercussions Meta and Yandex were facing for their conduct.
Firefox, Microsoft Edge and DuckDuckGo browsers were also affected, with Firefox owner Mozilla and DuckDuckGo engineers taking action to stop any future covert tracking.

data.title: AGI is not multimodal
data.author: danielmorozoff
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了生成式AI模型（如大型语言模型，LLMs）在实现人工通用智能（AGI）方面的局限性。尽管这些模型在某些任务上表现出色，但它们缺乏对物理世界的真正理解，仅通过扩展规模和符号预测实现智能，无法解决涉及物理现实的问题，如修理汽车或打结。文章指出，真正的AGI需要具备对物理世界的理解和互动能力，而不仅仅是符号处理。LLMs通过预测下一个符号可能诱导出对世界的表面理解，但缺乏深层次的物理理解。作者主张，AGI应优先考虑具身认知和环境互动，而非简单拼接多模态网络。文章提醒，不应将语言理解与世界理解混为一谈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（人工通用智能）的实现路径、定义及其多模态能力

不同观点：
• **patrickscoleman** 认为很多评论仅针对文章标题做出反应，而没有深入内容。他建议使用更具描述性但较长的标题来澄清文章的核心观点，即AGI需要结合多模态输入输出，并嵌入物理环境，而不是简单依赖单模态模型或通过增加计算资源来解决问题。

• **nsagent** 支持文章的观点，引用了包括DeepMind的David Silver在内的多篇论文和访谈，强调理论上的深思熟虑比单纯依赖计算资源的增加更为重要。

• **skybrian** 质疑“通用智能”的定义，认为真正的AGI必须在所有领域都是通用的，但人类本身也并非在所有方面都有天赋，因此对AGI的这种期望可能不切实际。

• **bufferoverflow** 主张AGI必须是多模态的，认为如果AGI不能理解图像、视频、声音、气味和味道，那么它对世界的理解就是不完整的。

• **waynecochran** 提出将DNA视为一种语言，并认为这可能为构建基于基因序列数据的大语言模型提供了思路。

• **andy99** 对文章中的某些陈述感到困惑，特别是关于追求将身体化（embodiment）和环境互动视为首要因素的AGI路径，质疑这种论述的实际意义。

• **pcwelder** 认为AGI这一术语本身就存在问题，主张不需要所谓的“正确”世界模型，因为人类也没有这种模型。他以飞机发明为例，说明通过近似和实验也能取得成功，AGI只需要有用的模型，而非正确的模型。

• **nexttk** 对文章中“LLM只是下一个词预测器”的观点提出异议，认为这种看法低估了LLM的能力，强调“下一个词预测”只是接口，并不反映内部实现方式，LLM可以通过深远的思考做出预测。

• **pjdesno** 引用了2017年自动驾驶车祸的分析报告，说明当前AI在理解现实世界情境方面存在不足，并指出虽然LLM可能学会这些知识，但缺乏足够的训练数据和适当的词汇来表达。

• **falcor84** 认为当前的AI可能不会直接导致AGI的实现，但可以作为其启动的基础。

• **charcircuit** 强调多模态AGI将比单一模态的AI更有用，人们希望AI能够处理并理解音频、图像、视频等多种信息。

• **ivape** 指出人类思维能够从看似无关的感知中获得洞见，而当前的AI缺乏这种能力，并认为规模的增加将消除专业化。

• **empath75** 以幽默的方式质疑文章的观点，认为AI的“思维”方式不同于人类的思维方式，但这并不妨碍其完成任务，就像飞机飞行不同于鸟类飞行但仍能到达目的地。

• **macinjosh** 以讽刺的方式评论人类对自身智力的怀疑，认为争论机器是否智能可能没有太大意义。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到多模态能力对于AGI的重要性，以及当前AI在理解和处理现实世界情境方面的不足。
• 对“通用智能”的定义和实现路径存在争议，部分评论者质疑理论探讨的实际意义，而另一些评论者则强调深思熟虑的理论方法比单纯增加计算资源更为重要。
• 对LLM的能力和“下一个词预测”的看法存在分歧，部分评论者认为这种看法低估了LLM的实际能力。

44181613.article_content:
"In projecting language back as the model for thought, we lose sight of the tacit embodied understanding that undergirds our intelligence." –Terry Winograd
The recent successes of generative AI models have convinced some that AGI is imminent. While these models appear to capture the essence of human intelligence, they defy even our most basic intuitions about it. They have emerged not because they are thoughtful solutions to the problem of intelligence, but because they
scaled
effectively on
hardware we already had
. Seduced by the fruits of scale, some have come to believe that it provides a clear pathway to AGI. The most emblematic case of this is the multimodal approach, in which massive modular networks are optimized for an array of modalities that, taken together,
appear
general. However, I argue that this strategy is sure to fail in the near term; it will not lead to human-level AGI that can, e.g., perform sensorimotor reasoning, motion planning, and social coordination. Instead of trying to glue modalities together into a patchwork AGI,
we should pursue approaches to intelligence that treat embodiment and interaction with the environment as primary
, and see modality-centered processing as emergent phenomena.
Preface: Disembodied definitions of Artificial General Intelligence — emphasis on
general
— exclude crucial problem spaces that we should expect AGI to be able to solve.
A true AGI must be general across all domains.
Any
complete
definition must at least include the ability to solve problems that originate in physical reality, e.g. repairing a car, untying a knot, preparing food, etc. As I will discuss in the next section,
what is needed for these problems is a form of intelligence that is fundamentally situated in something like a physical world model
. For more discussion on this, look out for
Designing an Intelligence
. Edited by George Konidaris, MIT Press, forthcoming.
Why We Need the World, and How LLMs Pretend to Understand It
TLDR: I first argue that
true AGI needs a physical understanding of the world
, as many problems
cannot be converted into a problem of symbol manipulation
. It has been suggested by some that LLMs are learning a model of the world through next token prediction, but it is more likely that LLMs are learning bags of heuristics to predict tokens. This leaves them with a superficial understanding of reality and contributes to false impressions of their intelligence.
The most shocking result of the predict-next-token objective is that it yields AI models that reflect a deeply human-like understanding of the world, despite having never observed it like we have.
This result has
led to confusion
about what it means to
understand language
and even to
understand the world
— something we have long believed to be a prerequisite for language understanding.
One explanation for the capabilities of LLMs comes from
an emerging theory
suggesting that they induce models of the world through next-token prediction
. Proponents of this theory cite the prowess of SOTA LLMs on various benchmarks, the
convergence of large models to similar internal representations
, and their favorite rendition of the idea that “language mirrors the structure of reality,” a notion that has been espoused at least by Plato, Wittgenstein, Foucault, and Eco. While I’m generally in support of digging up esoteric texts for research inspiration, I’m worried that this metaphor has been taken too literally. Do LLMs really learn implicit models of the world? How could they otherwise be so proficient at language?
One source of evidence in favor of the LLM world modeling hypothesis is
the Othello paper
, wherein researchers were able to predict the board of an Othello game from the hidden states of a transformer model trained on sequences of
legal
moves
. However, there are
many
issues with generalizing these results to models of natural language. For one, whereas Othello moves can
provably
be used to deduce the full state of an Othello board,
we have no reason to believe that a complete picture of the physical world can be inferred by a linguistic description.
What sets the game of Othello apart from many tasks in the physical world is that
Othello fundamentally resides in the land of symbols, and is merely implemented using physical tokens to make it easier for humans to play.
A full game of Othello can be played with just pen and paper, but one can’t, e.g., sweep a floor, do dishes, or drive a car with just pen and paper. To solve such tasks, you need some physical conception of the world beyond what humans can merely
say
about it. Whether that conception of the world is encoded in a formal world model or, e.g., a value function is up for debate, but it is clear that
there are many problems in the physical world that
cannot
be
fully represented by a system of symbols
and solved with mere symbol manipulation.

Melanie Mitchell’s recent piece
and supported
by this paper

• **pcwelder** 认为AGI这一术语本身就存在问题，主张不需要所谓的“正确”世界模型，因为人类也没有这种模型。他以飞机发明为例，说明通过近似和实验也能取得成功，AGI只需要有用的模型，而非正确的模型。

• **nexttk** 对文章中“LLM只是下一个词预测器”的观点提出异议，认为这种看法低估了LLM的能力，强调“下一个词预测”只是接口，并不反映内部实现方式，LLM可以通过深远的思考做出预测。

• **pjdesno** 引用了2017年自动驾驶车祸的分析报告，说明当前AI在理解现实世界情境方面存在不足，并指出虽然LLM可能学会这些知识，但缺乏足够的训练数据和适当的词汇来表达。

• **falcor84** 认为当前的AI可能不会直接导致AGI的实现，但可以作为其启动的基础。

• **charcircuit** 强调多模态AGI将比单一模态的AI更有用，人们希望AI能够处理并理解音频、图像、视频等多种信息。

• **ivape** 指出人类思维能够从看似无关的感知中获得洞见，而当前的AI缺乏这种能力，并认为规模的增加将消除专业化。

• **empath75** 以幽默的方式质疑文章的观点，认为AI的“思维”方式不同于人类的思维方式，但这并不妨碍其完成任务，就像飞机飞行不同于鸟类飞行但仍能到达目的地。

• **macinjosh** 以讽刺的方式评论人类对自身智力的怀疑，认为争论机器是否智能可能没有太大意义。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到多模态能力对于AGI的重要性，以及当前AI在理解和处理现实世界情境方面的不足。
• 对“通用智能”的定义和实现路径存在争议，部分评论者质疑理论探讨的实际意义，而另一些评论者则强调深思熟虑的理论方法比单纯增加计算资源更为重要。
• 对LLM的能力和“下一个词预测”的看法存在分歧，部分评论者认为这种看法低估了LLM的实际能力。

data.author: nabla9

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Reddit将其用户内容出售给AI平台用于模型训练，引发的用户隐私、数据所有权和法律问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **[minimaxir]** 提到Reddit已经与包括OpenAI和Google在内的AI平台达成了利润丰厚的许可协议，暗示用户的内容正在被商业化使用。
• **[linotype]** 表示自己已经不再使用Reddit，并且在十多年前注册时并没有预料到自己的内容会被用作训练数据出售。这反映出用户对数据使用知情权的关注。
• **[4ndrewl]** 认为被出售的是“Reddit的数据”，而不是用户个人的言论，试图区分平台数据和个人言论的所有权。
• **[absurdo]** 持谨慎态度，表示希望听到知识产权律师的意见，以确定Reddit是否有法律依据，还是只是夸大其词，且Google等公司可能已经通过爬取和索引算法获取了这些数据。
• **[oshout]** 关注用户同意的问题，质疑在没有得到用户明确同意的情况下，Reddit是否允许AI使用这些数据进行训练，尤其是对那些在不同版本的用户协议下注册和停止使用的用户。
• **[xhkkffbf]** 引用电影台词，带有讽刺意味，但并未直接表达立场，可能是在暗示对用户权益忽视的现象。
• **[khelavastr]** 提出一个更具哲学性的问题，询问机器人何时会拥有像人类一样的阅读权利，并质疑如果Anthropic通过第三方缓存服务访问Reddit数据，情况是否会有所不同。
• **[mannyv]** 认为Reddit并不拥有用户内容的所有权，因此通过爬取Reddit数据用于AI训练实际上是对资源的不合理使用，暗示平台无权从用户内容中获利。

补充讨论：
• 用户对数据所有权和隐私的关注是核心问题，尤其是在未明确告知或获得用户同意的情况下，将内容用于商业目的。
• 法律层面的争议焦点在于Reddit是否有权将用户生成的内容用于商业用途，特别是当用户协议发生变更时，老用户是否应受新条款约束。
• 讨论中也涉及AI训练数据合法性的问题，包括通过爬取公开网站数据与通过正式授权获取数据之间的区别。
• 哲学性问题如“机器人权利”虽然不是直接的法律问题，但引发了对未来AI使用数据伦理的思考。

争议焦点：Reddit是否有权将其用户的言论内容出售用于AI训练，以及用户在不知情或未同意的情况下，其内容是否应被商业化使用。

data.title: We Are No Longer a Serious Country – Paul Krugman
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各国（尤其是美国）经济衰退的可能性及其原因，以及对当前政治和经济环境的分析与批评。

不同观点：
• **Animats**认为，富裕国家也可能走向失败，并列举了委内瑞拉、阿根廷、葡萄牙和罗马帝国衰落的例子，警示美国也可能正走上这条道路。这些例子显示了从繁荣到衰退的可能性，并强调了历史教训。
  
• **nabla9**指出，债券市场比股票市场更重要，因此当前的担忧是可以理解的，尤其是对债券市场的担忧。

• **wagwang**认为，许多美国人对经济问题漠不关心，无论是股市大跌还是债券违约，他们都不关心，因为他们根本不认同当前的系统。

• **w10-1**强调了利率与美元走势之间的历史性背离，认为这对投资者和企业建设者来说是一个不好的预兆。他还讨论了美国在技术和信息服务领域的转型，以及美国是否失去了应对挑战的严肃性。该观点提到了美国债务问题可能与少数主要玩家（如中东、中国、俄罗斯）的干预有关。

• **Macha**对"beard"一词在特定语境下的使用感到困惑，并寻求澄清。

• **tunesmith**表达了对当前经济分析中过度政治化和危言耸听的担忧，认为很难区分哪些紧急情况是真实的，哪些是被夸大的。该评论提到了克鲁格曼的分析，认为其中一些内容是无意义的抱怨，而非严肃的分析。

• **wodenokoto**认为，克鲁格曼指出的资本市场对当前形势的乐观预期是有道理的，但也指出，跟随特朗普的政策可能带来短期投资机会。该观点认为市场波动可能符合某些人的利益，而非仅仅是政府不严肃。

• **vessenes**同意政策变化会导致市场波动，但对抱怨法案名称等表面问题持批评态度，认为更应关注谁从中受益及受益时间。

• **Herring**将经济问题与政治倾向联系起来，认为共和党的政策导致了经济和社会的困境，并指出红州长期以来对共和党的支持令人不解，认为 dysfunction 比任何单一政府更深层次。

• **BuckRogers**批评保罗·克鲁格曼更像是一个政治操盘手而非经济学家，认为低曝光率的经济学家可能提供更有价值的分析。

• **selivanovp**认为，美国的问题不仅仅是特朗普造成的，而是源于美国精英阶层自认为“特殊”并推行所谓的“基于规则的秩序”，导致外交失效，其他国家不再信任美国。

• **pfortuny**对克鲁格曼的批评持怀疑态度，认为其抱怨可能只是出于对市场变化的不满。

补充讨论：
- 经济衰退的历史案例被用来警示当前的美国可能面临类似的问题。
- 债券市场和利率变化被视为经济健康的重要指标。
- 美国公众对经济问题的漠不关心被认为是潜在问题。
- 克鲁格曼的分析被一些评论者认为过于政治化或表面化，缺乏深度分析。
- 政治倾向与经济政策效果之间的关联被深入讨论，尤其是共和党政策的影响。
- 对美国精英阶层和外交政策的批评指向了更深层次的结构性问题。

data.title: You Will
data.author: cainxinth
data.article_summary: "You Will"是AT&T于1993年推出的一系列由大卫·芬奇导演的广告，由汤姆·塞莱克配音。广告展示了多个 futuristic 场景，例如智能个人助理、视频会议、GPS导航等，并以"你将会，而实现这一切的公司是AT&T"结尾。尽管这些广告准确预测了许多未来技术，但实现这些技术的公司大多是新兴的硅谷企业，而非AT&T。该广告活动赢得了多个奖项，并包括了一些创新概念，如RFID、远程医疗、智能手表和家庭自动化等。广告还在1994年推出了首批网络横幅广告之一。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对科技广告的历史回忆与不同视角的解读

不同观点：
• [jgrahamc] 回忆了微软以前制作的恶搞广告，特别提到了一则由貌似汤姆·塞勒克（Tom Selleck）配音的广告。他还具体描述了其中一个场景，一个女人在海边收到了一封从她的草帽里传出来的传真。这表明他对这些幽默广告印象深刻，并认为这些广告具有独特创意。

• [duxup] 对广告中传达的积极与乐观的科技前景表示赞赏，认为那个时代的科技广告充满了对未来的美好期望与信心。他通过分享一个YouTube链接（视频内容为乐观的科技广告）来支持他的观点，表明他对这种积极情感的认同和怀念。

• [sandspar] 则通过指出一个常见的错误，即很多人会混淆互联网技术作家Timothy B. Lee和万维网发明者Tim Berners-Lee。他以一种幽默的方式暗示，Timothy B. Lee可能已经习惯了因为这种误解而让观众失望。这一观点偏向于调侃和幽默，但也指出了名人效应带来的潜在误解。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点似乎并不明显，但不同评论者对广告的记忆和解读有所不同。[jgrahamc] 侧重于广告的幽默和创意，[duxup] 强调广告传达的乐观科技情绪，而[sandspar] 则通过调侃一个常见的错误引发了对名人效应的思考。

• 评论之间的讨论关系较为松散，主要围绕对科技广告的记忆和评价展开，但每个评论者从不同的角度切入，包括广告的具体内容、情感基调以及相关的名人混淆问题。

44182114.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
AT&T marketing campaign
For other uses, see
You Will (disambiguation)
.
"You Will"
was an
AT&T
marketing campaign that launched in 1993, consisting of commercials directed by
David Fincher
.
[
1
]
[
2
]
Each ad presented a futuristic scenario beginning with "Have you ever…" and ending with "…you will. And the company that will bring it to you: AT&T."
The ads were narrated by
Tom Selleck
.
[
1
]
The creative team that created the ad campaign at N.W. Ayer & Partners were Copy Supervisor Gordon Hasse, Art Supervisor Nick Scordato and Producer Gaston Braun.
One of the first
web banner
ads ever sold was part of an AT&T campaign that ran on
HotWired
starting October 27, 1994, asking "Have you ever clicked your mouse right HERE? You Will".
[
3
]
In 2016, technology writer Timothy B. Lee commented that "overall, the ads were remarkably accurate in predicting the cutting-edge technologies of the coming decades. But the ads were mostly wrong about one thing: the company that brought these technologies to the world was
not
AT&T. At least not on its own. AT&T does provide some of the infrastructure on which the world's communications flow. But the gadgets and software that brought these futuristic capabilities to consumers were created by a new generation of Silicon Valley companies that mostly didn't exist when these ads were made."
[
4
]
The ads won a few different awards at the time, notably the first annual David Ogilvy Award for the most effective campaign supported by research, the 1994 PCIA (Personal Communications Industry Award), and two
ADDY Awards
.
[
5
]
Innovations
[
edit
]
The proposed innovations included:
[
6
]
Grocery checkout machines that would process an entire cart at a time without the groceries needing to be removed, presumably via
RFID
or something similar ("Have you ever checked out at the supermarket, a whole cart at a time?")
[
7
]
Telemedicine
("[Have you ever] put your heads together, when you're not together?")
[
7
]
Intelligent personal assistants
("Have you ever had an assistant who lived in your computer?")
Videoconferencing
("Have you ever shown up for a meeting in your bare feet?")
GPS
navigation systems
with automatic rerouting based on live traffic ("Have you ever crossed the country without stopping to ask directions?")
Wi-Fi
/
WAN
,
tablet computing
and portable
pen computing
("Have you ever sent a fax from the beach?")
Smartwatches
("[Have you ever] gotten a phone call, on your wrist?")
Self-service kiosks

Illustration: David Parkins
The problem
Dear
Nature
,
I am a postdoc working at an academic institute. I admire my principal investigator (PI) and am working on a project that fits my skill set and interests. However, before this position, I had two difficult experiences in consecutive postdoc jobs that led me to leave both labs. During my interviews, the PIs and I discussed working on projects that I was passionate about, but when I joined each lab, I was assigned to other projects that didn’t align with my interests. The PIs were also unclear about where my funding came from. For instance, after working in my first postdoc position for several months, I found out that my salary was being paid by another PI in the department. At the time, I felt misled. These positions weren’t what I signed up for.
I tried to discuss my concerns with both PIs, but ultimately felt that my only option was to look for new positions. I’m now in my third postdoc role in three years, which doesn’t look great for job applications. My new PI has been transparent about funding, and the projects I’m working on are what I expected, but I’m still having a hard time trusting him. How does someone choose the right PI?
—
An uncertain computer scientist
The advice
Nature
’s careers team reached out to two academics and two career coaches for advice.
“You did exactly the right thing by moving on,” says Emma Williams, founder of the Nerd Coach, an academic coaching business in Cambridge, UK. The relationship between a PI and postdoc “is so key to everything in your career going forwards”.
In terms of choosing the right PI for a postdoc, all four said the first step is self-reflection. “Start by identifying what you want to get out of your postdoc,” says LaShan Hendrix, a biomedical engineer at the University of Cincinnati in Ohio. “Do you want to get more papers? Do you want to take on a new role? Do you want teaching or grant-writing experience?”
Nine books to help shape your science career in 2025
Then, Hendrix suggests, explore what mentoring style you like. Do you prefer a mentor who is hands-on, or someone who is less involved? If you had issues with your PhD adviser, Hendrix recommends looking for a PI for your postdoc who can provide you with a different personality and mentoring style.
Next, consider what laboratory environment you need to thrive. For instance, in a large lab group, you might have the opportunity to take on a leadership role and collaborate with graduate students. In a smaller lab, it might just be you and the PI working closely on a project. “It can feel quite claustrophobic, or the two of you could be a brilliant team,” Williams says.
Navigating interviews
Understanding what you want as a researcher isn’t enough on its own, however. The next step is interviewing potential PIs. Keep in mind that this process isn’t just about the PI questioning you — you’re also interviewing them to see whether they will be the right fit. All of the specialists
Nature
spoke to said that it’s important to discuss ongoing research projects as well as where the funding comes from and what the PI expects of you. Williams suggests asking for written documentation about the project you’ll be working on, and for a copy of the grant that will support your work. If the PI is unwilling to provide those documents, that could be a warning sign, she says.
Williams also says that the way you phrase your questions can affect the type of information you receive. For instance, instead of asking a hypothetical question about how the PI will support your career, ask how they have supported their postdocs’ careers in the past, which encourages them to provide you with evidence of their previous efforts. Looking into how long researchers have stayed in the lab for can also be helpful. “If people are only staying six months, that would be a big red flag for me,” says Williams.
Hendrix says it’s crucial to clarify which intellectual ideas from your postdoc research you will be able to take with you after you move on, and which aspects will stay with the lab. For example, if your PI works on the 3D microenvironment in breast cancer, maybe you can go on to study the 3D microenvironment in lung cancer instead. Another example could be examining different pathways in the same disease.
How do I tell someone that I can't write them a strong letter of recommendation?
“A red flag would be if they make it clear that they don’t want you to take anything,” she says. “Another thing to look out for is whether your future research interests are exactly what that PI is working on, because then they might see you as competition. You want to have some separation in your research interests.”
If you want to do independent research, it’s important to ask whether you can work on it during the postdoc. “I usually encourage young fellows or postdocs to look for their own small grant

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了Go语言中关于错误处理的冗长问题，尤其是频繁的`if err != nil`检查使代码显得繁琐。自2018年起，Go团队尝试解决此问题，最早提出了基于"check"和"handle"机制的方案，但被认为过于复杂。随后在2019年提出了简化的"try"方案，尽管进行了大量讨论和工具测试，但由于控制流不清晰和社区反对，该方案也被放弃。文章反思了过程中的失误，指出应更早引入新关键字并给予社区更多反馈空间。此后，社区不断提出新的错误处理建议，但尚未有新进展。总体而言，Go团队仍在探索如何简化错误处理，同时保持语言的简洁性和可读性。

44171677.article_content:
The Go Blog
[ On | No ] syntactic support for error handling
Robert Griesemer
3 June 2025
One of the oldest and most persistent complaints about Go concerns the verbosity of error handling.
We are all intimately (some may say painfully) familiar with this code pattern:
x, err := call()
if err != nil {
// handle err
}
The test
if err != nil
can be so pervasive that it drowns out the rest of the code.
This typically happens in programs that do a lot of API calls, and where handling errors
is rudimentary and they are simply returned.
Some programs end up with code that looks like this:
func printSum(a, b string) error {
x, err := strconv.Atoi(a)
if err != nil {
return err
}
y, err := strconv.Atoi(b)
if err != nil {
return err
}
fmt.Println("result:", x + y)
return nil
}
Of the ten lines of code in this function body, only four (the calls and the last two lines) appear to do real work.
The remaining six lines come across as noise.
The verbosity is real, and so it’s no wonder that complaints about error handling have topped
our annual user surveys for years.
(For a while, the lack of generics surpassed complaints about error handling, but now that
Go supports generics, error handling is back on top.)
The Go team takes community feedback seriously, and so for many years now we have tried to
come up with a solution for this problem, together with input from the Go community.
The first explicit attempt by the Go team dates back to 2018, when Russ Cox
formally described the problem
as part of what we called the Go 2 effort at that time.
He outlined a possible solution based on a
draft design
by Marcel van Lohuizen.
The design was based on a
check
and
handle
mechanism and was fairly comprehensive.
The draft includes a detailed analysis of alternative solutions, including comparisons with
approaches taken by other languages.
If you’re wondering if your particular error handling idea was previously considered,
read this document!
// printSum implementation using the proposed check/handle mechanism.
func printSum(a, b string) error {
handle err { return err }
x := check strconv.Atoi(a)
y := check strconv.Atoi(b)
fmt.Println("result:", x + y)
return nil
}
The
check
and
handle
approach was deemed too complicated and almost a year later, in 2019,
we followed up with the much simplified and by now
infamous
try
proposal
.
It was based on the ideas of
check
and
handle
, but the
check
pseudo-keyword became
the
try
built-in function and the
handle
part was omitted.
To explore the impact of the
try
built-in, we wrote a simple tool
(
tryhard
)
that rewrites existing error handling code using
try
.
The proposal was argued over intensively, approaching 900 comments on the
GitHub issue
.
// printSum implementation using the proposed try mechanism.
func printSum(a, b string) error {
// use a defer statement to augment errors before returning
x := try(strconv.Atoi(a))
y := try(strconv.Atoi(b))
fmt.Println("result:", x + y)
return nil
}
However,
try
affected control flow by returning from the enclosing function in case of an error,
and did so from potentially deeply nested expressions, thus hiding this control flow from view.
This made the proposal unpalatable to many, and despite significant investment
into this proposal we decided to abandon this effort too.
In retrospect it might have been better to introduce a new keyword,
something that we could do now since we have fine-grained control over the language version
via
go.mod
files and file-specific directives.
Restricting the use of
try
to assignments and statements might have alleviated some
of the other concerns. A
recent proposal
by Jimmy Frasche, which essentially
goes back to the original
check
and
handle
design and addresses some of that design’s
shortcomings, pursues that direction.
The repercussions of the
try
proposal led to much soul searching including a series of blog
posts by Russ Cox:
“Thinking about the Go Proposal Process”
.
One conclusion was that we likely diminished our chances for a better outcome by presenting an almost
fully baked proposal with little space for community feedback and a “threatening” implementation
timeline. Per
“Go Proposal Process: Large Changes”
:
“in retrospect,
try
was a large enough change that the new design we published […] should have
been a second draft design, not a proposal with an implementation timeline”.
But irrespective of a possible process and communication failure in this case, the user sentiment towards
the proposal was very strongly not in favor.
We didn’t have a better solution at that time and didn’t pursue syntax changes for error handling for several years.

44171677.article_summary: 文章讨论了Go语言中关于错误处理的冗长问题，尤其是频繁的`if err != nil`检查使代码显得繁琐。自2018年起，Go团队尝试解决此问题，最早提出了基于"check"和"handle"机制的方案，但被认为过于复杂。随后在2019年提出了简化的"try"方案，尽管进行了大量讨论和工具测试，但由于控制流不清晰和社区反对，该方案也被放弃。文章反思了过程中的失误，指出应更早引入新关键字并给予社区更多反馈空间。此后，社区不断提出新的错误处理建议，但尚未有新进展。总体而言，Go团队仍在探索如何简化错误处理，同时保持语言的简洁性和可读性。

data.title: Sid Meier's Pirates – In-depth (2017)
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 《Sid Meier's Pirates!》是MicroProse于1987年推出的经典游戏，最初在Commodore 64上发布，1990年移植到Amiga平台。该游戏在不同平台上都有独特改编，Amiga版本被视为最佳之一。游戏背景设定在17世纪加勒比海，玩家可选择不同年代开始冒险，参与海战、城镇袭击及剑斗等。游戏融合了动作、冒险与策略元素，具有高度开放性，玩家可自行设定目标，如私掠或寻宝。尽管画面被误认为使用了64色模式，实际为32色，但通过技术处理达到出色视觉效果。游戏手册提供了详尽的历史背景和玩法指导，增强了沉浸感。总体而言，该作在独特性和可玩性上表现出色，是不可错过的经典。

While there may be many games that we love and come back to time and again, how often do we appreciate the different versions of a game? We usually find ourselves playing the version we grew up with, perhaps even ignoring the best version in favor of nostalgia. If we had no prior experience with said game, we'll ignore the lesser looking versions, even if that might be the original, completely missing out on their charm. How often do we love a game so much that we want to experience as many versions as possible? Sid Meier's Pirates! (referred hereafter as Pirates) is a game I have to have for every system it supports, and I truly love all of the many ports and remakes of this game.
^Starting up the game and some options
The original Pirates came out in 1987, written by Sid Meier for the Commodore 64, using the BASIC programing language. The game received ports for just about every system imaginable at the time, and I could not characterize any of them as "straight ports". They were all quite unique for each system, and indeed this Amiga version, released a few years later in 1990, is an obvious loving port. It was rewritten for the Amiga in-house at MicroProse USA, another example of a fine American Amiga product that the European Amiga scene these days almost refuse to acknowledge.
The ports based off the original Pirates peek with this Amiga version. The game is so beautiful that some magazines falsely claimed the game used 64 color Extra Half Bright Mode. I tested this out by taking actual screen captures from my Amiga, and found the game was always in a 320x200 32 color mode. However, there are certain screens like the title that do not capture quite right using my screen capture program, seemingly missing colors. Rather than use EHB mode I believe they were manipulating certain areas of the screen in order for some areas to get a fresh 32 color palette, a practice used in several games to pull off hundreds of colors on the Amiga. When the game was remade in the mid-90's as Pirates! Gold for several platforms, it could be debated on if even that version looked better than this.
^Descriptions of various time periods from the manual
Upon loading, the game offers you several choices of play. You can dive straight into the game, which will automatically put you into the 1660's, the most prosperous pirating period. You can select from several other periods of time as well, offering a range of different challenges and situations. Finally you can partake in several special scenarios involving historical events with actual pirates. The manual is a tremendous resource for information regarding these time periods,  and an overall excellent read at nearly 100 pages. While the game is fairly intuitive on its own, I do believe people will be missing out if they ignore the top notch manual.
^The game usually starts you off at a "lovely seaside town"
Pirates was made during a time when a game could defy characterization. This is a truly unique game in its own genre. The cover of the manual describes it as the "action adventure simulation" and the worlds first swashbuckling simulation. Microprose was already famous for their simulations at this point. While the game successfully combines quite a few categories together, simulation might be the least of these. The manual itself more than makes up for a game that is largely the Hollywood tale of the pirating life, but indeed the game itself is taking you on an adventure of the best movie elements of that life, not simulating the actual truth of the life. There's plenty of action elements here, including a very fun sword fighting sequence, but there's even strategy elements during the various ship and town attack sequences.
^The Caribbean, finding our way using the sun, and attacking a ship
It's an open ended game during a time when those games did not exist, originally being released before SimCity had been. You decide your goals with this game. There is eventually an ending in retirement, which age will force upon you at some point, and even a high score, but there's nothing but personal goals for you to achieve before you reach that ending. Retire in the first town you come across if you want, game over. The later Pirates Gold remake would attempt to steer you toward some goals in the form of listed quests, but all of those quests can be completed (or not) right here in the original game. You decide how to have your fun with Pirates.
^Swordplay on ship and sinking one
During the 1660's you could have quite a successful career privateering for various countries aga

data.title: Tesla shows no sign of improvement in May sales data
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 特斯拉CEO马斯克将重心转回面临困境的汽车业务。尽管全球电动车销量上升，特斯拉今年一季度销量同比减少数万辆，尤其在欧洲和中国市场销量大幅下滑。德国、英国和意大利的数据显示特斯拉在这些国家的销售疲软，尽管整体电动车市场在增长。中国市场竞争激烈，本土品牌以更低价格和更多功能抢占市场。此外，美国工厂仍受特朗普时期进口汽车零部件关税的影响。特斯拉在向NACS充电接口转型中遇到挑战，超级充电站被替换。同时，特斯拉在奥斯汀推出的自动出租车服务因商标问题受阻。马斯克还公开反对共和党预算提案，引发政治争议。

Tesla CEO Elon Musk's big government adventure appears to be at an end.
As promised in April
, Musk has returned his attention to his car company, which is facing serious headwinds. In the first quarter of the year, Tesla sold tens of thousands fewer electric vehicles than it did the year before, despite a rise in worldwide EV sales. Data from April looked even worse, with
substantial sales declines in Europe
and China. May's numbers don't look much better.
Although Tesla only publishes its global production and sales numbers—and only at the end of each quarter—some countries provide monthly new car registration information, making it possible to track sales on a national level. And according to Germany's KBA, in May, Tesla sales fell by just over 36 percent year over year, even as overall EV registrations increased by 45 percent. At least that's a few hundred more cars than it managed in April.
Similar trends
were seen in the UK and Italy. In the UK, Tesla sales decreased by 45 percent, even as overall EV sales increased by 28 percent. In Italy, EV sales increased by almost 41 percent, but Tesla's deliveries dropped by 20 percent.
The slide isn't quite as bad in China, where Tesla faces stiff competition from local brands that undercut it with low prices while providing a wealth of features that are either unavailable in Teslas or cost extra.
According to Reuters
, Tesla's Shanghai factory delivered 15 percent fewer vehicles in May than it did last year, a number that includes both exports to Europe and local sales.
A rare spot of good news is that Norway—which has one of the highest adoption rates of EVs in the world—has seen a huge 213 percent increase year over year.
Turning around shrinking sales is just one of Musk's challenges at Tesla. Even though much of the company's production is vertically integrated, its US factories are
still exposed to increased costs due to the Trump tariffs
on imported auto parts, which make up about 20 percent of a Tesla's content. Allegedly, Musk was unaware of this impact
on a recent visit to Tesla HQ
.
The industry-wide shift from CCS1 to Tesla-style NACS charging plugs is
progressing so slowly that the New Jersey Turnpike is
replacing Superchargers
with machines that can service both types
. Will others follow suit?
Now that we're into June, the clock is ticking on the rollout of Tesla's autonomous taxi service in Austin, Texas, which suffered a branding setback when the company
was denied a trademark
on the word "robotaxi."
And finally, the CEO appears to be at odds with his political allies, taking to social media to express his hostility toward the proposed Republican budget and promising to "fire all politicians who betrayed the American people."

data.title: Morgan Stanley's AI parsed 9M lines of code, saving 15K devs 280K hours
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: Morgan Stanley开发了一款名为DevGen.AI的AI工具，帮助开发人员将旧编程语言（如Perl）的代码转换为英文描述，进而重写为更现代的语言（如Python）。该工具基于OpenAI的GPT模型，自1月份推出以来，已为公司15,000名开发人员节省了280,000小时的工作时间。由于市面上的商业工具无法满足其特定需求，摩根士丹利选择自行开发该工具。尽管AI能处理部分代码转换，但仍需人工开发人员参与以确保效率和质量。公司预计不会因该工具而裁减软件工程人员。此外，摩根士丹利还推出了其他AI应用，帮助员工提高工作效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在代码转换和重构中的实际应用，特别是从Perl到Python的转换。

不同观点：
• throwaway843认为AI可以通过阅读Perl代码，为Python开发者节省时间，提供了一个非夸大宣传的实际应用案例，展示了AI在开发中的具体好处。
• buttrpopcorn指出，尽管AI工具可以将代码从旧语言转换为新语言，但AI并不擅长像人类开发者那样高效地编写新代码。他们建议使用非AI的扫描器、解析器、翻译器来处理Perl代码库，然后让AI进行重构，最后由人类开发者优化和修复问题。
• GuB-42提到，尽管Perl和Python是同一代的语言，并且都有最新的版本发布，但Python如今更受欢迎。Perl难以阅读，但拥有庞大的代码库，因此是AI解析的一个好目标。

补充讨论：

'Building It Ourselves': Morgan Stanley Created an AI Tool to Fix the Most Annoying Part of Coding. Here's How It Works.
Morgan Stanley first introduced the AI tool in January, and it has since saved developers 280,000 hours of work.
By
Sherin Shibu
Edited by
Melissa Malamut
Jun 3, 2025
Share
Copy
Key Takeaways
Morgan Stanley’s new AI tool translates code in older languages into plain English.
The bank’s developers can then use the English specs to rewrite the code into a newer language.
The tool has helped Morgan Stanley's 15,000 developers save time.
Morgan Stanley built its in-house AI tool to tackle a difficult
coding
problem: reworking old legacy code into more updated
coding
languages.
Morgan Stanley introduced the AI tool, which is based on OpenAI's GPT models, in January, per
The Wall Street Journal
. The tool, called DevGen.AI, translates code in older languages, such as Perl (released in
1987
), into plain English, which developers can then use as a basis for rewriting the code into newer languages like Python.
Related:
Amazon Cloud CEO Predicts a Future Where Most Software Engineers Don't Code — and AI Does It Instead
Mike Pizzi, Morgan Stanley's global head of technology and operations, told
WSJ
that in the five months since its launch, DevGen.AI has worked through nine million lines of code, saving the firm's 15,000 developers roughly 280,000 hours of work.
Pizzi said that Morgan Stanley opted to build the tool itself because tech companies didn't have any solutions that could fit Morgan Stanley's exact specifications. Commercial tools lacked expertise in deciphering older coding languages, especially those specific to a company.
"We found that building it ourselves gave us certain capabilities that we're not really seeing in some of the commercial products," Pizzi told
WSJ
. "We saw the opportunity to get the jump early."
Related:
Morgan Stanley Plans to Lay Off 2,000 Workers, Replacing Some with AI
Morgan Stanley trained DevGen.AI on languages within its own code base, including languages customized for the company. However, the AI tool still has growing to do when it comes to full translation. Though the tool can, in theory, rewrite code from an older language to a newer one, it doesn't know how to write the new code efficiently or as well as a human developer, Pizzi said.
That's why Morgan Stanley is keeping human developers involved in the process of translating old or legacy code to new languages. Pizzi disclosed that the firm will not be reducing its software engineering workforce as a result of the AI tool, though the company did lay off 2,000 of its
80,000-person
workforce in March.
Morgan Stanley has released several
AI apps
for employees, including one that helps them summarize video meetings and another that quickly finds information for them from the company's body of research.
Morgan Stanley CEO Ted Pick told investors last year that the AI tools could save employees up to 15 hours per week and be "potentially really game-changing," per
Reuters
.

data.author: gregorywegory
data.article_summary:
**cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider** 是一个用于 Cloudflare Workers 的 OAuth 2.1 提供者库，用 TypeScript 编写，支持 PKCE。该库作为 Worker 代码的包装器，自动处理令牌管理，并为 API 端点添加授权功能。其主要特点包括：

1. 自动管理所有令牌。
2. API 处理程序接收已认证的用户信息，无需自行验证。
3. 不限定用户管理和认证方式。
4. 不限定 UI 框架，可自由实现授权流程。
5. 存储不包含任何秘密信息，仅存储哈希值。

使用示例中，需配置 API 路由、处理程序、默认处理程序以及授权和令牌交换端点等。该库仍处于测试阶段，API 可能会变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用AI辅助编码的实践、效果、安全性及版权问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• rienbdj 指出AI生成的代码中存在安全隐患，特别是加密密钥的处理可能破坏端到端加密。他强调了对AI生成的代码进行安全审查的重要性，并怀疑非专业人员是否能发现和解决此类问题。
• paxys 支持AI辅助编码的方向，认为AI能帮助有经验的工程师快速生成代码片段，但强调工程师仍需仔细审查和测试代码。他还质疑了完全不用AI是否会更快完成任务。
• c-linkage 分享了自己在使用LLM生成非网页代码时的挫折经验，认为LLM在处理复杂或不常见的编码任务时表现不佳，可能因为这些问题过于 obscure 或 novel。
• mtlynch 对评论中提到的"I (@kentonv)"表示困惑，质疑该用户是否是另一个用户的别名，并指出了可能的误解。
• jes5199 基于个人经验，认为使用AI工具（如Claude）可以显著提高生产力，但也指出这种方法对认知要求更高。他还提到AI工具在短时间内有了显著改进。
• infinitebattery 分享了自己在使用AI工具时的类似经历，AI工具能完成部分任务，但在解决复杂问题时表现不佳，最终需要手动修复AI的错误。
• aeneas_ory 对AI在安全相关代码中的应用表示担忧，认为使用经过多年迭代和安全测试的工具更为可靠。他将AI辅助编码视为一种反模式，类似于“自造加密”的复生。
• vaidhy 提出阅读他人代码比编写代码更费脑力，认为AI工具可能更适合生成短代码片段，而非从头开始的项目。
• jauntywundrkind 和 simonw 提供了具体的AI生成代码提交历史链接，展示了AI在早期提交中的明确指导和手把手提示。
• declan_roberts 对出现“请求过多”错误表示调侃，认为这是与所涉及公司不匹配的尴尬情况。
• Luker88 对AI生成代码的版权问题表示关注，询问在大量使用AI生成代码的情况下如何处理版权问题，特别是在手动修改代码的情况下。
• _tqr3 分享了自己在使用LLM构建Web应用时的挫败经历，指出AI在解决无限循环和保持上下文方面表现不佳。
• qsort 认为虽然AI生成代码的过程中需要大量指导，但仍可能节省大量时间，整体上持谨慎乐观态度。
• kentonv 作为该库的作者，分享了自己从AI怀疑论者转变为支持者的个人经历。他认为AI辅助编码与人工编码审查有显著不同，特别是在反馈循环短和AI擅长处理样板代码方面。但他同时也指出AI在复杂代码重构方面的局限性。

补充讨论：
- AI工具在生成代码时的表现和局限性是讨论的核心，特别是在复杂问题、上下文保持和安全性方面。
- 版权问题和AI生成代码的法律归属也是用户关注的重点之一。
- 手动审查和修改AI生成代码的必要性被多次提及，强调了人类工程师在AI辅助编码中的重要作用。

OAuth 2.1 Provider Framework for Cloudflare Workers
This is a TypeScript library that implements the provider side of the OAuth 2.1 protocol with PKCE support. The library is intended to be used on Cloudflare Workers.
Beta
As of March, 2025, this library is very new, prerelease software. The API is still subject to change.
Benefits of this library
The library acts as a wrapper around your Worker code, which adds authorization for your API endpoints.
All token management is handled automatically.
Your API handler is written like a regular fetch handler, but receives the already-authenticated user details as a parameter. No need to perform any checks of your own.
The library is agnostic to how you manage and authenticate users.
The library is agnostic to how you build your UI. Your authorization flow can be implemented using whatever UI framework you use for everything else.
The library's storage does not store any secrets, only hashes of them.

• paxys 支持AI辅助编码的方向，认为AI能帮助有经验的工程师快速生成代码片段，但强调工程师仍需仔细审查和测试代码。他还质疑了完全不用AI是否会更快完成任务。
• c-linkage 分享了自己在使用LLM生成非网页代码时的挫折经验，认为LLM在处理复杂或不常见的编码任务时表现不佳，可能因为这些问题过于 obscure 或 novel。

• jes5199 基于个人经验，认为使用AI工具（如Claude）可以显著提高生产力，但也指出这种方法对认知要求更高。他还提到AI工具在短时间内有了显著改进。
• infinitebattery 分享了自己在使用AI工具时的类似经历，AI工具能完成部分任务，但在解决复杂问题时表现不佳，最终需要手动修复AI的错误。
• aeneas_ory 对AI在安全相关代码中的应用表示担忧，认为使用经过多年迭代和安全测试的工具更为可靠。他将AI辅助编码视为一种反模式，类似于“自造加密”的复生。
• vaidhy 提出阅读他人代码比编写代码更费脑力，认为AI工具可能更适合生成短代码片段，而非从头开始的项目。
• jauntywundrkind 和 simonw 提供了具体的AI生成代码提交历史链接，展示了AI在早期提交中的明确指导和手把手提示。
• declan_roberts 对出现“请求过多”错误表示调侃，认为这是与所涉及公司不匹配的尴尬情况。
• Luker88 对AI生成代码的版权问题表示关注，询问在大量使用AI生成代码的情况下如何处理版权问题，特别是在手动修改代码的情况下。
• _tqr3 分享了自己在使用LLM构建Web应用时的挫败经历，指出AI在解决无限循环和保持上下文方面表现不佳。
• qsort 认为虽然AI生成代码的过程中需要大量指导，但仍可能节省大量时间，整体上持谨慎乐观态度。
• kentonv 作为该库的作者，分享了自己从AI怀疑论者转变为支持者的个人经历。他认为AI辅助编码与人工编码审查有显著不同，特别是在反馈循环短和AI擅长处理样板代码方面。但他同时也指出AI在复杂代码重构方面的局限性。

补充讨论：
- AI工具在生成代码时的表现和局限性是讨论的核心，特别是在复杂问题、上下文保持和安全性方面。
- 版权问题和AI生成代码的法律归属也是用户关注的重点之一。
- 手动审查和修改AI生成代码的必要性被多次提及，强调了人类工程师在AI辅助编码中的重要作用。

The iPhone 15 Pro's Depth Maps
Since 2017, Apple have supported depth maps in the images its iPhones capture either via LiDAR scanners, 3D
time-of-flight
scanner-less LIDAR or
structured-light
3D scanning.
These depth maps, along with other imagery, are stored in High Efficiency Image File Format (HEIF) container files. These files can contain multiple images and vast amounts of metadata. This format was originally designed between 2013 and 2015 and Apple adopted its HEIC variant in 2017.
Since then, HEIC files are the default storage container format for images captured on the iPhone. But with that said, it is possible to use the JPEG format instead if things like depth maps and HDR are not of interest.
Finn Jaeger, who is the head of VFX at Replayboys, a film production firm in Hamburg, Germany,
posted
a screenshot a few weeks ago showing how multiple depth maps were being produced by his iPhone.
He announced he was working on a project called
HEIC Shenanigans
. This project contains scripts to separate out images and their metadata from HEIC containers as well as convert them into EXR Files. As of this writing, the project contains 374 lines of Python.
In this post, I'll walk through Finn's codebase with an example image from an iPhone 15 Pro.
My Workstation
I'm using a 5.7 GHz AMD Ryzen 9 9950X CPU. It has 16 cores and 32 threads and 1.2 MB of L1, 16 MB of L2 and 64 MB of L3 cache. It has a liquid cooler attached and is housed in a spacious, full-sized Cooler Master HAF 700 computer case.
The system has 96 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 4,800 MT/s and a 5th-generation, Crucial T700 4 TB NVMe M.2 SSD which can read at speeds up to 12,400 MB/s. There is a heatsink on the SSD to help keep its temperature down. This is my system's C drive.
The system is powered by a 1,200-watt, fully modular Corsair Power Supply and is sat on an ASRock X870E Nova 90 Motherboard.
I'm running Ubuntu 24 LTS via Microsoft's Ubuntu for Windows on Windows 11 Pro. In case you're wondering why I don't run a Linux-based desktop as my primary work environment, I'm still using an Nvidia GTX 1080 GPU which has better driver support on Windows and ArcGIS Pro only supports Windows natively.
Installing Prerequisites
I'll use Python 3.12.3 and a few other tools in this post.

sudo
add-apt-repository
ppa:deadsnakes/ppa

update

install

python3.12-venv
Note, the
libimage-exiftool-perl
package installs
exiftool
version 12.76+dfsg-1 which was released at the end of January 2024. Since then, there have been at least ten releases that have addressed issues or enhanced exiftool's HEIC support.
The above version should work fine for the steps in this post but be mindful that any issues you encounter going forward might be resolved with a more up to date version of exiftool.
I'll be using
JSON Convert
(jc) to convert the output of various CLI tools into JSON.

https://github.com/kellyjonbrazil/jc/releases/download/v1.25.2/jc_1.25.2-1_amd64.deb

I'll set up a Python Virtual Environment and install a few dependencies.

install

OpenImageIO
I'll use
DJV
v2.0.8 to view EXR imagery produced in this post.
An iPhone 15 Pro Image
Joel Joseph
, a subject matter expert on the ArcGIS Desktop Products Suite in Mumbai, India, was kind enough to send me an HEIC-contained image he took on his iPhone 15 Pro. I'll use this image in this post. Below is a screenshot.
Extracting the Gain Map
The HEIC file Joel provided is 1.57 MB.

~/heic-shenanigans/gain_map_extract.py

data.author: picture
data.article_summary: 2025年4月，荷兰代尔夫特理工大学（TU Delft）的科学家和学生团队在阿布扎比举行的A2RL无人机锦标赛中获得冠军。他们的全自主无人机在比赛中击败了13架其他自主无人机和多名人类无人机竞速冠军，创造了人工智能发展的新里程碑。该无人机仅依靠一个前置摄像头，通过深度神经网络进行高性能控制，最终在曲折赛道上达到了95.8公里/小时的速度。与以往在虚拟环境中击败人类冠军的突破不同，这次胜利发生在现实世界中，展示了人工智能在极端时间压力和有限资源下的潜力。这项技术将对自动驾驶汽车和人形机器人等机器人应用产生重要影响。

Back to (previous) overview
TU Delft's latest news
Autonomous drone from TU Delft defeats human champions in historic racing first
News
-
15 April 2025
A team of scientists and students from TU Delft has taken first place at the A2RL Drone Championship in Abu Dhabi - an international race that pushes the limits of physical artificial intelligence, challenging teams to fly fully autonomous drones using only a single camera. The TU Delft drone competed against 13 autonomous drones and even human drone racing champions, using innovative methods to train deep neural networks for high-performance control. The gained knowledge on highly-efficient robust AI  will contribute to many robotics applications, from self-driving cars to humanoid robots.
The TU Delft team: Anton Lang, Quentin Missine, Aderik Verraest, Erin Lucassen, Till Blaha, Robin Ferede, Stavrow Bahnam, Christophe De Wagter and Guido de Croon.
Beating human pilots
For the first time, a drone has beaten human pilots in an international drone racing competition, marking a new milestone in the development of artificial intelligence. On Saturday April 14, 2025, two drone racing events took place simultaneously: The Falcon Cup Finals for human pilots and the A2RL Drone Championship for AI-powered, autonomous drones. As a climax, the best AI drones also competed against the best human pilots. The AI drone developed by TU Delft first won the A2RL Grand Challenge. It then went on to win the knockout tournament against human pilots, beating three former DCL world champions and reaching flight speeds up to 95.8 km/h on the very winding track.
The team of scientists and students from TU Delft achieved this by developing an efficient and robust AI system, capable of split-second, high-performance control. Whereas earlier breakthroughs, like AI defeating world champions at chess or Go, have taken place in virtual settings, this achievement happened in the real world. Two years ago, the Robotics and Perception Group at the University of Zürich was the first to beat human drone racing champions with an autonomous drone. However, that impressive achievement occurred in a flight lab environment, where conditions, hardware, and the track were still controlled by the researchers – a very different situation from this world championship, where the hardware and track were fully designed and managed by the competition organisers.
The drone designed by the organizers, A2RL and DCL for use by the AI teams and human pilots.
Pushing the frontiers of physical AI
The goal of the 2025 A2RL Drone Championship in Abu Dhabi was to push the frontier of physical AI, by stimulating research on robotic AI under extreme time pressure and with very limited computational and sensory resources. The drone had access to just one forward-looking camera, a major difference from previous autonomous drone races. This is more similar to how human FPV pilots fly, and leads to additional perception challenges for the AI.
The AI that won against the three former DCL world champions was developed by a team of scientists and students from the MAVLab at TU Delft’s Faculty of Aerospace Engineering. Team lead Christophe De Wagter is both exhausted and exhilarated.
I always wondered when AI would be able to compete with human drone racing pilots in real competitions. I’m extremely proud of the team that we were able to make it happen already this year. I hope that this achievement and this type of competition in general forms a springboard for real-world robot applications.
Christophe De Wagter
Timelapse of the TU Delft drone flying through a gate of the racing track.
AI that directly commands the motors
One of the core new elements of the drone’s AI is the use of a deep neural network that doesn’t send control commands to a traditional human controller, but directly to the motors. These networks were originally developed by the Advanced Concepts Team at the European Space Agency (ESA) under the name of “Guidance and Control Nets”. Traditional, human-engineered algorithms for optimal control were computationally so expensive that they would never be able to run onboard resource-constrained systems such as drones or satellites. ESA found that deep neural networks were able to mimick the outcomes of traditional algorithms, while requiring orders of magnitude less processing time. As it was hard to test whether the networks would perform well on real hardware in space, a collaboration was formed with the MAVLab at TU Delft.
“We now train the deep neural networks with reinforcement learning, a form of learning by trial and error. ”, says Christophe De Wagter. “This allows the drone to more closely approach the physical limits of the system. To get there, though, we had to redesign not only the training procedure for the control, but also how we can learn about the drone’s dynamics from its own onboard sensory data.”

data.title: A proposal to restrict sites from accessing a users’ local network
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由Chrome安全网络团队提出的提案，旨在限制公共网站未经用户许可访问其本地网络。目前，公共网站可以探测用户的本地网络并可能发动针对脆弱设备的跨站请求伪造（CSRF）攻击。为解决此问题，提案建议废除公共网站直接访问私有IP地址的能力，要求网站在获得用户许可后才能连接其本地网络设备。该方案基于Chrome之前暂停的“私有网络访问（PNA）”工作，但通过权限控制而非预检请求来增强用户控制。其目标是防止驱动式网页对本地设备的利用，同时允许在用户明确许可的情况下进行合法通信。提案不打算破坏现有工作流程，也不解决本地网络HTTPS问题。主要用例包括普通用户和需要通过公共网站控制本地设备的用户（如IoT设备设置）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：浏览器是否应该允许网站访问用户的本地网络资源，以及如何在安全性和用户体验之间取得平衡。

不同观点：
• mystifyingpoi认为，浏览器默认允许网站访问本地IP是严重的安全隐患，建议通过弹窗提示让用户自行决定是否允许访问，这样可以平衡安全性和灵活性。
• pacifika提到，Internet Explorer以前通过分区系统解决了这一问题，暗示可以借鉴这种做法。
• paxys指出，浏览器默认允许网站访问本地网络服务是安全隐患，尤其在开发环境中容易被忽视，建议加强默认的安全措施。
• sroussey认为，这一改变可能有助于阻止Meta等公司通过本地通信绕过隐私限制。
• skybrian指出，即使需要这种权限的网站，通常也只需要访问一个特定的本地服务器，全面开放本地网络权限违反了最小权限原则。
• ronsor提醒，由于NPAPI插件的移除，一些本地软件依赖于运行在localhost的HTTP服务器，改变这种行为可能会影响这些软件的使用。
• rerdavies担心IPv6环境下，难以区分站点本地的IP地址，这可能导致提案在IPv6网络中出现问题，并提到本地网络地址使用私有证书的必要性。
• AdmiralAsshat提到，像uBlock / uMatrix这样的工具已经默认阻止这种行为，并指出一些知名网站试图探测localhost。
• zajio1am认为，在IPv6过渡期间，使用公共地址的本地网络使得这种解决方案显得不合适。
• nickcw指出，这种改变可能会影响依赖localhost进行OAuth的机制，但认为合理的权限提示可以解决问题。
• phkahler坚决认为，这种访问根本就不应该存在，用户同意只是让问题变得更可以接受，而不是解决它。
• thesdev离题地讨论了标题中的语法问题。
• AshamedCaptain不理解为何要基于IP地址范围扩展保护，认为同源策略应该已经能防止这些问题。
• profmonocle指出，RFC1918地址代表的是私有网络，而非本地网络，建议通过客户端自身的子网掩码来判断IP是否为本地。
• foota提到，虽然替代方案因设备支持问题被暂停，但希望未来可以通过设备选择机制避免权限提示。

补充讨论：
1. 关于IPv6环境下如何判断本地地址的争议，以及私有证书在本地网络中的使用问题。
2. 关于浏览器默认行为和用户教育之间的讨论，如何在不影响用户体验的情况下提升安全性。
3. 对于企业环境中的特殊需求，例如大型企业内部网络的访问需求，如何在方案中进行考虑。

Explainer for Local Network Access
This proposal is an early design sketch by the Chrome Secure Web and Network team to describe the problem below and solicit feedback on the proposed solution. It has not been approved to ship in Chrome.
Proponents
Chrome Secure Web and Network team
Participate
https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/local-network-access/issues
Introduction
Currently public websites can probe a user's local network, perform CSRF attacks against vulnerable local devices, and generally abuse the user's browser as a "confused deputy" that has access inside the user's local network or software on their local machine. For example, if you visit
evil.com
it can use your browser as a springboard to attack your printer (given an HTTP accessible printer exploit).
Local Network Access aims to prevent these undesired requests to insecure devices on the local network. This is achieved by deprecating direct access to private IP addresses from public websites, and instead requiring that the user grants permission to the initiating website to make connections to their local network.
Note:
This proposal builds on top of Chrome's previously paused
Private Network Access (PNA) work
, but differs by gating access on a permission rather than via preflight requests. This increases the level of user control (at the expense of new permissions that have to be explained to the user) but removes the explicit "device opt-in" that the preflight design achieved. We believe this simpler design will be easier to ship, in order to mitigate the real risks of local network access today. Unlike the previous Private Network Access proposal, which required changes to devices on local networks, this approach should only require changes to sites that need to access the local network. Sites are much easier to update than devices, and so this approach should be much more straightforward to roll out.
Goals
Stop exploitation of vulnerable devices and servers from the drive-by web.
Allow public websites to communicate to private network devices when the user expects it and explicitly allows it.
An adjacent goal is that we want a path for browsers to be good stewards of OS-level local network access permissions. These OS-level permissions are increasingly common (
on iOS, and more recently on macOS
) -- simply because the
browser
has been granted the permission (for legitimate browser functionality the user may want to use, like mirroring the contents of a tab on a local device) should not expose users' local devices to the risks of the open web.
Non-goals
Break existing workflows and services that rely on a public web frontend that can control local network devices.
As long as there is
some
path forward we should be okay with breaking some use cases (e.g., iframe and HTML subresources that aren't explicitly sourced from local hostnames), but overall we want to minimize breakage.
Solve the local network HTTPS problem.
As stated in the
original Private Network Access explainer
:
Provide a secure mechanism for initiating HTTPS connections to services running on the local network or the user's machine. This piece is missing to allow secure public websites to embed non-public resources without running into mixed content violations, with the exception of
http://localhost
which is embeddable. While a useful goal, and maybe even a necessary one in order to deploy Private Network Access more widely, it is out of scope of this specification.
Use cases
Use case 1
The most common case is for users who don't have any services or devices on their local network that expect connections from websites. Today, browsers freely allow JavaScript and subresource requests to these devices without any indication to the end user. Unless this behavior is expected by the user, users should not be exposed to this risk by default.
Use case 2
Public web frontend for controlling or setting up local devices (such as an IoT device, home router, etc.).
Device manufacturers want to be able to give users an easy process for setting up a new device, and one method that is used is to have a page hosted on the manufacturer's public website which then communicates with the device via the user's browser, explicitly relying on the

data.title: Redesigned Swift.org is now live
data.author: lawgimenez
data.article_summary: Swift是一款强大、灵活、多平台的编程语言，具有快速、表达力强和安全的特点。它可以从嵌入式设备和内核扩展到应用程序和云基础设施。Swift编译成原生代码，提供可预测的内存管理，支持面向对象、函数式和泛型编程模式。其设计注重内存安全，消除多种bug和漏洞。Swift与C和C++具有出色的互操作性，允许逐步将现有代码库迁移到Swift。该语言适用于从微控制器到服务器的各种环境，并且是开源的，欢迎贡献和参与。

不同观点：

data.title: Apple Notes Expected to Gain Markdown Support in iOS 26
data.author: danso
data.article_summary: 据传闻，Apple的Notes应用将在iOS 26和macOS 26中加入Markdown支持（来源：9to5Mac）。这一功能将允许用户使用简单语法进行文本格式化，而无需依赖现有的富文本控件。对习惯键盘操作的用户而言，这将是一个重大升级，可以直接输入**加粗**或#标题等标记符号。此举将使Apple Notes与Obsidian、Notion和Bear等支持Markdown的笔记应用看齐，并方便那些在GitHub或Reddit上熟悉Markdown的用户，无需切换应用。该功能可能会在下周的全球开发者大会上与iOS 26的其他改进一同发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iOS Notes应用的Markdown支持及其相关功能争议

不同观点：
• [lurk2] 不推荐在iOS Notes生态中投资，因为无法在不使用iCloud的情况下导出包含元数据和媒体的笔记。他建议使用Joplin，因为它支持Markdown、多平台客户端以及自托管同步。
• [tlhunter] 提到Microsoft Notepad也正在增加Markdown支持，并对Markdown快速成为主流表示惊讶。
• [mdeeks] 希望Markdown支持是可选的，因为人们在Markdown和富文本之间有强烈的偏好。他个人不喜欢Markdown，并提到Bear笔记现在支持隐藏Markdown，认为这是一个很好的折中方案。
• [RollingRo11] 对仅支持Markdown导出而不支持编辑功能表示失望，并希望有LaTeX支持。
• [andy_xor_andrew] 猜测Markdown支持可能与未来Apple的智能功能和LLM相关，因为Markdown易于LLM处理。
• [DevKoala] 表示现在使用ChatGPT做笔记，并认为传统笔记应用显得原始，不再使用。

补充讨论：
• [afavour] 和 [promiseofbeans] 对通过此讨论得知Apple新操作系统版本命名系统表示惊讶。
• [ale42] 和 [zamadatix] 提到对Apple新版本号和Markdown支持功能的误解和信息更正。
• [cyberge99] 分享了他从Evernote切换到Upnote并找到满意的笔记解决方案的经历。
• [puttycat] 提供了关于iOS 26的文章链接以帮助不了解版本号来源的人。
• [htk] 希望Apple修复笔记应用中存在多年的光标跳动问题。
• [paxys] 对Markdown支持表示欢迎，但希望Notes应用保持简单，不要引入LLM相关功能。

争议焦点：
• 用户对Markdown支持的看法不一，部分用户希望Notes应用保持简单，而另一些用户则希望有更多高级编辑功能如Markdown和LaTeX支持。
