44187777.article_content:
SQL is a declarative language; only the result of the query is specified. The exact steps to produce the result must be determined by the DBMS. Often, multiple ways exist to calculate a query result. For example, the DBMS can choose to use an index or perform a sequential scan on a table to find the needed tuples.
The query optimizer is responsible for finding the most efficient plan for a given query. The plan generator creates possible plans, which are then evaluated based on their costs. Afterward, the cheapest plan is chosen and executed. When the DBMS expects to return a large portion of the table, a full table scan can be more efficient than following the pointers in an index structure. However, it is hard to determine when the DBMS prefers one plan over another and when the switch between plans occurs.
In a few evenings of vibe coding,
I implemented the plan explorer
for PostgreSQL. It iterates over a search space and generates visualizations that show when the plan changes and how many tuples are expected versus the actual number returned. This blog post examines the “art” of query optimization. It discusses the plan explorer tool, the images the tool generates, and the insights the tool provides into the decisions made by the PostgreSQL query optimizer.
Plan Explorer
Plan Explorer is a tool that iterates over a two-dimensional search space and executes a given SQL query for each parameter combination. Based on the returned query plans (and actual query executions), various diagrams are generated. These diagrams have an artistic aspect, but they also provide valuable insights into the workings of the query optimizer and visually represent the decisions made (i.e., at which point PostgreSQL considers using a specific index).
The tool is based on the ideas of
Picasso
, but implemented as a modern web application.
The Picasso database query optimizer visualizer, Jayant R. Haritsa, Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, Volume 3, Issue 1-2, September 2010
Server Mode
Initially, the tool was developed as a standalone website that does not require any server component. The WebAssembly build of PostgreSQL,
PGlite
, is used to run PostgreSQL within the user’s browser and extract the needed query plans.
In the most recent version of the tool, an optional server mode was added. Using this server mode, queries are sent to a
REST
endpoint on a web server. On the web server, a script can take the requested queries and forward them to an actual PostgreSQL server. The server component acts as a proxy for query execution. This is necessary because, due to security constraints, JavaScript running in a browser cannot open network connections to other hosts. So, to communicate with a real PostgreSQL server, the proxy component is needed. However, when an actual PostgreSQL server is queried, large datasets can be preloaded or custom extensions can be integrated into the database server. This allows the tool to run in these environments as well (e.g., a PostgreSQL extension developer could check their custom cost models and whether PostgreSQL picks up the desired query plans).
The architecture of the plan explorer is shown in the diagram below:
flowchart LR
subgraph **Browser**
UI["WebUI"]
PGLite["PGlite (WebAssembly PostgreSQL)"]
UI -- "SQL, Parameters" --> PGLite
PGLite -- "Query Results, Plans" --> UI
end
subgraph "**Proxy Mode** (Optional)"
Proxy["Proxy Server"]
PG["PostgreSQL Database"]
UI -- "HTTP (SQL/Params)" --> Proxy
Proxy -- "SQL" --> PG
PG -- "Results" --> Proxy
Proxy -- "Results" --> UI
end
A further feature of the server mode is that the queries can also be executed (
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)
) instead of only being planned (
EXPLAIN
). When only the planning of the query is performed, the tool operates much faster and can quickly iterate over the given search space. On the other hand, if the query is actually executed, PostgreSQL provides further information, such as the actual number of returned tuples or the execution time.
Generated Drawings
The plan explorer tool creates several different drawings from one query. These drawings are:
The used query plans
The expected costs of the query
The actual execution time of the query
The estimated number of result tuples
The actual number of result tuples
The difference between the estimated and actual number of result tuples
For a database administrator, the different query plans and their distribution might be the most interesting output of the tool. For a developer who has implemented custom scan nodes and cost models, the other outputs may also be of interest. They enable database developers to determine if the cost models function as expected.
Example Query Discussion

data
on the attribute
key
. Two predicates in the
WHERE
clause define filter conditions. The exact values for these conditions are determined by the search space. In this example, the

data.title: Air Lab – A portable and open air quality measuring device
data.author: 256dpi
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：空气质量监测设备的选择与评价

不同观点：
• **支持AirGradient设备**：voxlax认为AirGradient设备价格更便宜、测量精度高，且硬件和软件都是开源的，可以自行刷机。他认为这对于关注准确性的人来说是一个不错的选择，并提供了自己使用该设备的体验链接。
• **强调产品诚实和设计**：hereme888赞赏AirGradient的网站设计简洁、产品真实，没有过度营销和复杂界面，认为这体现了产品背后的用心。
• **关注价格和可负担性**：homebrewer指出，对于生活在空气污染严重但经济条件有限的地区的人来说，200美元以上的设备过于昂贵，建议推出价格更低的基础版本。他强调，NO₂测量功能是该设备的一大亮点。
• **对Air Lab项目的反馈**：256dpi介绍了自己开发的Air Lab设备，该设备功能全面且开源，旨在让空气质量监测更易于定制和扩展。用户反馈中有人（如poisonborz）指出该设备的动画界面不实用，建议直接展示传感器数据。还有人（如ronakjain90）建议增加仅显示数据模式，以便用户自行选择展示方式。

补充讨论：
• **与其他产品的比较**：tigrezno认为Air Lab价格偏高，尤其是与具备空气净化功能的设备相比。neves询问是否有价格低于100美元的空气质量监测设备，特别是可以在AliExpress上购买的。
• **关于硬件选择的讨论**：部分用户对Air Lab的ESP32微控制器选择提出质疑，认为在功耗方面可能不如其他选择（如red523）。还有人关注设备是否支持Zigbee等集成系统（如xvfLJfx9）。
• **功能需求和改进建议**：一些用户提到对特定功能的需求，如PM2.5监测（savrajsingh）和Zigbee支持（xvfLJfx9）。此外，finnjohnsen2提到市场缺乏可用于自行组装的氡传感器模块。
• **开源社区和基础设施**：zevon提到sensor.community项目，该项目提供开源传感器设计和公共数据聚合基础设施。

争议焦点：
• **设备价格 vs. 功能性**：部分用户认为高价设备不具备空气净化功能，性价比不高。
• **界面设计 vs. 实用性**：一些用户认为Air Lab的动画界面不必要，更倾向于直接展示传感器数据。
• **可负担性 vs. 功能全面性**：价格较高的设备功能全面，但低收入地区用户更需要价格低廉的基础版本。

data.title: A Case for Feminism in Programming Language Design (2024)
data.author: smitty1e
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言（PL）设计中的性别视角和多样性，特别是女性在PL领域的体验和贡献。

不同观点：
• [andsoitis的观点] 作者以自身经历讲述了她对编程的热爱以及在编程语言领域中的成长，但同时也指出，PL研究和设计往往优先考虑机器而非人的需求。她认为当前的PL社区标准往往以男性化视角为主，注重形式化和技术评估，而忽视了用户研究和定性研究。她提出，通过引入女性主义视角，可以更好地审视PL的价值观和优先事项，并从多样化的视角改进编程语言设计。

• [MichealCodes的观点] 他引用了Grace Hopper的维基百科链接，暗示女性在编程历史中已有重要贡献，可能不需要特别强调性别视角，因为历史上已有女性做出了杰出贡献（如Grace Hopper）。

• [dismalaf的观点] 他认为作者不应仅仅批评现有编程语言缺乏女性视角，而应亲自去设计一种编程语言来证明自己的观点。

• [imgreen的观点] 他列举了多个由男性主导开发的编程语言，认为编程语言的设计历史上确实主要由男性主导，但质疑女性主义是否能真正推动PL设计的多样性和包容性。

• [iliti22的观点] 他讽刺地指出，女性可能更关注于衣服和TikTok舞蹈等活动，而不是像男性那样以编程为乐，暗示性别偏好可能影响了女性在编程领域的参与度。

• [tines的观点] 他认为某些PL设计者对错误信息的设计不够重视，而这种设计往往反映了设计者的生活经验和价值观。他特别提到，对于那些在编程世界中感到自己不属于该领域的人（如女性），不清晰的错误信息可能会带来负面影响。然而，tines也批评作者对成年用户的不尊重，认为不应该假设用户无法处理直接的错误信息。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于编程语言设计是否应该以及如何引入女性主义视角，特别是在错误信息设计和用户体验方面。一些人认为女性主义可以促进多样性和包容性，而另一些人则质疑其必要性或有效性。

• 对于如何在PL设计中体现多样性和包容性，有观点认为实际行动（如设计新的编程语言）比单纯批评现有设计更为有效。

• 对错误信息设计的讨论揭示了PL设计中一个具体而实际的改进方向，即更具可读性和用户友好的错误信息可能对所有用户都有帮助。

data.title: Binary Wordle
data.author: eh8
data.article_summary: 《Binary Wordle》是一款基于二进制数字（0和1）的猜词游戏，玩法类似于经典的Wordle。玩家通过键盘输入（0、1、Enter、Backspace）或使用按钮来参与游戏，目标是猜出正确的二进制序列。文章还包含了赞助商链接，推荐了一项名为altodial.com的电话服务，以及一个个人网站chengeric.com，提供更多有趣的内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基于Wordle的二进制及数字变体游戏的玩法、难度和改进建议

不同观点：
• **对二进制版游戏的简单性提出质疑**：
  - [AmsterErdo] 认为二进制版游戏因为只有两个可能的值，因此很容易在两次尝试中猜中。
  - [umvi] 认为二进制确实简单，但十六进制版本更具挑战性，并分享了自己在编程游戏中的十六进制Wordle变体"dwordle"。
  - [abotsis] 也认为二进制版过于简单，建议改为“猜数字”的二进制形式，提供“太高”或“太低”的提示，并提议将猜测次数限制为5次以增加难度。

• **对游戏改进的建议**：
  - [NotAnOtter] 建议通过增加字符串长度和匹配子字符串的条件来提升游戏难度，使游戏更具挑战性。
  - [NoSalt] 和 [mulmen] 分享了自己的游戏结果，分别在两次和十次猜测中完成游戏，表明游戏对部分玩家来说可能过于简单。
  
• **其他数字变体游戏的分享**：
  - [zck] 分享了自己设计的多种基于Wordle的数字变体游戏，如"numberdle"、"rationerdle"、"factordle"和"formuladle"，并解释了每个变体的玩法和挑战性。
  - [James-Livesey] 提供了自己设计的十六进制版本链接，并提到之前的二进制版本因过于简单而不太受欢迎。

• **对游戏创意的赞赏与技术反馈**：
  - [Aissen] 赞赏游戏创意的趣味性，鼓励继续创新。
  - [bitwrangler] 对游戏的UI和动画表示赞赏，并指出游戏可以帮助学习二进制运算。
  - [thehours] 提供了技术反馈，指出输入时遇到的问题，无法用键盘输入除'0'以外的字符。

• **幽默和调侃**：
  - [tylerchr] 引用妻子的幽默评论，指出二进制版不应称为Wordle，而应叫"Digitle"。
  - [patrakov] 分享了一个简单的二步猜测策略，进一步强调了游戏的简单性。
  - [asimovDev] 提到另一个类似的游戏"Horsle"，引发对更多变体的联想。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于二进制版游戏的难度过低，玩家们提出了多种增加挑战性的建议。
- 玩家们分享了自己设计的各种Wordle变体游戏，展示了创造性和对游戏机制的深入理解。
- 技术反馈和幽默评论为讨论增添了趣味性和实用性。

  - [James-Livesey] 提供了自己设计的十六进制版本链接，并提到之前的二进制版本因过于简单而不太受欢迎。

- 技术反馈和幽默评论为讨论增添了趣味性和实用性。

data.title: DiffX – Next-Generation Extensible Diff Format
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了传统Unified Diffs在现代软件开发中的局限性，并提出了一种新的可扩展差异格式——DiffX。Unified Diffs仅标准化了一部分差异信息，如文件标识、差异块偏移和增删行，但在编码、版本控制、元数据和文件路径表示等方面缺乏统一标准，导致解析和处理困难。文章指出，Unified Diffs无法表示提交列表、二进制补丁、文本编码，且缺乏标准的元数据格式。为解决这些问题，文章提出了DiffX格式，它完全向后兼容现有工具，具备未来适应性，且保持人类可读性。DiffX通过定义结构化和标准化格式，解决了Unified Diffs的不足，使得工具能更可靠地处理差异文件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Diff格式的设计及其在不同工具中的应用和问题

不同观点：
• laserbeam认为当前的层次化格式（带有"..meta"和"…meta"）不易读，建议使用具有不同名称的结构以提高可读性，并质疑为何使用JSON和key=value两种格式。他还提到格式对分割diff的影响，以及对修订版本作为文件属性的困惑。
• HelloNurse指出提议中存在不必要的功能扩展，如单个diff表示多个提交列表和二进制补丁表示，认为这些功能过于复杂且不必要。
• blacklion批评当前格式混合了自定义头和JSON有效载荷，认为这种结构混乱且需要两个解析器，同时对扩展diff添加元数据的想法表示认可，但对其具体实现持批评态度。
• ed认为现有的patch格式已经解决了这些问题，并引用了git-format-patch文档作为支持。
• bawolff质疑是否真的需要这些新功能，认为多diff表示多个提交更自然，且元数据主要在单个系统内部有用。
• xyzzy_plugh认为文档难以阅读，指出diff和patch的区别，并质疑新格式是否真正解决了问题，建议如果元数据必须是JSON会更合理。
• redleader55质疑新格式试图解决的问题及其目标用户。
• itake提到diff工具对新行属性的依赖问题，认为长行变化的审查困难。
• tlb认为最通用和明确的diff表示方式是直接包含两个文件的内容，并指出diff格式在人类可读性上的不足。
• koiueo认为JSON不适合作为元数据的通用格式，过于复杂。
• greatgib不支持使用多行JSON或YAML，认为这会使格式变得复杂，并强调diff文件的单行命令特性。
• signa11推荐difftastic，认为其使用tree-sitter提供更好的diff信息。
• chipx86（DiffX作者之一）解释了DiffX的背景和目标，强调其解决工具在处理不同SCM系统的diff文件时遇到的问题，包括元数据、编码、二进制文件处理等，并指出新格式的必要性和设计决策。
• xiphias2认为新格式向后兼容但向前不兼容，建议通过文档化现有git diff源代码来解决问题，而非创建新格式。
• b0a04gl认为这是在过度工程化一个并不紧迫的问题，开发人员更需要不会因文件重命名或行结束符变化而崩溃的工具。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于新格式的必要性和复杂性，一些人认为现有工具和格式已经足够，而另一些人则强调新格式在处理不同SCM系统的元数据和二进制文件方面的优势。
• 对JSON作为元数据格式的适用性存在分歧，一些人认为其过于复杂，而另一些人认为其通用性和易解析性是优势。
• 对新格式中引入的多层次结构和混合格式表示不满，认为这会增加解析和理解的难度。
• 实际使用中的问题，如长行变化的审查困难、文件重命名和行结束符变化带来的工具问题，也被提及并讨论。

44176737.article_content:
DiffX - Next-Generation Extensible Diff Format
¶
If you’re a software developer, you’ve probably worked with diff files. Git
diffs, Subversion diffs, CVS diffs.. Some kind of diff. You probably haven’t
given it a second thought, really. You make some changes, run a command, a
diff comes out. Maybe you hand it to someone, or apply it elsewhere, or put it
up for review.
Diff files show the differences between two text files, in the form of
inserted (
+
) and deleted (
-
) lines. Along with this, they contain some
basic information used to identify the file (usually just the name/relative
path within some part of the tree), maybe a timestamp or revision, and maybe
some other information.
Most people and tools work with
Unified Diffs
. They look like this:
--- readme    2016-01-26 16:29:12.000000000 -0800
+++ readme    2016-01-31 11:54:32.000000000 -0800
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or this:
Index: readme
===================================================================
RCS file: /cvsroot/readme,v
retrieving version 1.1
retrieving version 1.2
diff -u -p -r1.1 -r1.2
--- readme    26 Jan 2016 16:29:12 -0000        1.1
+++ readme    31 Jan 2016 11:54:32 -0000        1.2
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or this:
diff --git a/readme b/readme
index d6613f5..5b50866 100644
--- a/readme
+++ b/readme
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or even this:
Index: readme
===================================================================
--- (revision 123)
+++ (working copy)
Property changes on: .
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Modified: myproperty
## -1 +1 ##
-old value
+new value
Or this!
==== //depot/proj/logo.png#1 ==A== /src/proj/logo.png ====
Binary files /tmp/logo.png and /src/proj/logo.png differ
Here’s the problem
¶
Unified Diffs themselves are not a viable standard for modern development.
They only standardize parts of what we consider to be a diff, namely the
---
/
+++
lines for file identification,
@@
...
@@
lines for
diff hunk offsets/sizes, and
-
/
+
for inserted/deleted lines.
They
don’t
standardize encodings, revisions, metadata, or even how
filenames or paths are represented!
This makes it
very
hard for patch tools, code review tools, code analysis
tools, etc. to reliably parse any given diff and gather useful information,
other than the changed lines, particularly if they want to support multiple
types of source control systems. And there’s a lot of good stuff in diff files
that some tools, like code review tools or patchers, want.
You should see what GNU Patch has to deal with.
Unified Diffs have not kept up with where the world is going. For instance:
A single diff can’t represent a list of commits
There’s no standard way to represent binary patches
Diffs don’t know about text encodings (which is more of a problem than you
might think)
Diffs don’t have any standard format for arbitrary metadata, so everyone
implements it their own way.
We’re long past the point where diffs should be able to do all this. Tools
should be able to parse diffs in a standard way, and should be able to modify
them without worrying about breaking anything. It should be possible to load a
diff, any diff, using a Python module or Java package and pull information out
of it.
Unified Diffs aren’t going away, and they don’t need to. We just need to add
some extensibility to them. And that’s completely doable, today.
Here’s the good news
¶
Unified Diffs, by nature, are
very
forgiving, and they’re everywhere, in
one form or another. As you’ve seen from the examples above, tools shove all
kinds of data into them. Patchers basically skip anything they don’t
recognize. All they really lack is structure and standards.
Git’s diffs are the closest things we have to a standard diff format (in that
both Git and Mercurial support it, and Subversion pretends to, but poorly),
and the closest things we have to a modern diff format (as they optionally
support binary diffs and have a general concept of metadata, though it’s
largely Git-specific).
They’re a good start, though still not formally defined. Still, we can build
upon this, taking some of the best parts from Git diffs and from other
standards, and using the forgiving nature of Unified Diffs to define a new,
structured Unified Diff format.
DiffX files
¶
We propose a new format called Extensible Diffs, or DiffX files for short.
These are
fully backwards-compatible with existing tools
, while also being
future-proof
and remaining
human-readable
.
#diffx:
encoding=utf-8, version=1.0
#.change:
#..preamble:
indent=4, length=319, mimetype=text/markdown
Convert legacy header building code to Python 3.
Header building for messages used old Python 2.6-era list comprehensions
with tuples rather than modern dictionary comprehensions in order to build
a message list. This change modernizes that, and swaps out six for a
3-friendly `.items()` call.
#..meta:
format=json, length=270
{
"author"
:
"Christian Hammond <christian@example.com>"
,
"committer"
:
"Christi

data.title: An Arrow Flight SQL Server with DuckDB or SQLite back-end execution engines
data.author: tanelpoder
data.article_summary:
GizmoSQL 是由 GizmoData™ 开发的 Apache Arrow Flight SQL 服务器实现，支持 DuckDB 或 SQLite 作为后端数据库。它支持通过中间件进行身份验证，并允许通过 TLS 进行加密连接。该项目最初是从 Voltron Data 的开源项目 sqlflite 分支而来，并在 Apache 2.0 许可证下独立扩展为 GizmoSQL。

用户可以通过发布的 Docker 镜像运行 GizmoSQL，并可选择启用或禁用 TLS。运行时可以挂载自定义的 DuckDB 数据库文件，该文件需使用 DuckDB 1.3.0 版本创建。此外，用户可在容器启动时执行初始化 SQL 命令，但选择查询结果不会显示，且失败的命令将导致服务器退出。最后，GizmoSQL 支持通过 JDBC 连接到服务器。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

Description
This is the GizmoSQL core repo - used to build an Apache Arrow Flight SQL server implementation using DuckDB or SQLite as a backend database.
It enables authentication via middleware and allows for encrypted connections to the database via TLS.
For more information about Apache Arrow Flight SQL - please see this
article
.
It is originally
forked from
sqlflite
, an open-source project developed by Voltron Data. I contributed to
sqlflite
while employed at Voltron Data, and have since independently extended and evolved the project into GizmoSQL under the Apache 2.0 License.
Option 1 - Running from the published Docker image
Open a terminal, then pull and run the published Docker image which has everything setup (change: "--detach" to "--interactive" if you wish to see the stdout on your screen) - with command:
#
Pull and run the Docker image
docker run --name gizmosql \
--detach \
--rm \
--tty \
--init \
--publish 31337:31337 \
--env TLS_ENABLED=
"
1
"
\
--env GIZMOSQL_PASSWORD=
"
gizmosql_password
"
\
--env PRINT_QUERIES=
"
1
"
\
--pull missing \
gizmodata/gizmosql:latest
The above command will automatically mount a very small TPC-H DuckDB database file.
Note
: You can disable TLS in the container by setting environment variable:
TLS_ENABLED
to "0" (default is "1" - enabled).  This is not recommended unless you are using an mTLS sidecar in Kubernetes or something similar, as it will be insecure.
Optional - open a different database file
When running the Docker image - you can have it run your own DuckDB database file (the database must be built with DuckDB version: 1.3.0).
Prerequisite: DuckDB CLI
Install DuckDB CLI version
1.3.0
- and make sure the executable is on your PATH.
Platform Downloads:
Linux x86-64
Linux arm64 (aarch64)
MacOS Universal
In this example, we'll generate a new TPC-H Scale Factor 1 (1GB) database file, and then run the docker image to mount it:
#
Generate a TPC-H database in the host's /tmp directory
pushd
/tmp
duckdb ./tpch_sf1.duckdb
<<
EOF
.bail on
.echo on
SELECT VERSION();
INSTALL tpch;
LOAD tpch;
CALL dbgen(sf=1);
EOF
#
Run the gizmosql docker container image - and mount the host's DuckDB database file created above inside the container
docker run --name gizmosql \
--detach \
--rm \
--tty \
--init \
--publish 31337:31337 \
--env TLS_ENABLED=
"
1
"
\
--env GIZMOSQL_PASSWORD=
"
gizmosql_password
"
\
--pull missing \
--mount type=bind,source=
$(
pwd
)
,target=/opt/gizmosql/data \
--env DATABASE_FILENAME=
"
data/tpch_sf1.duckdb
"
\
gizmodata/gizmosql:latest
Running initialization SQL commands
You can now run initialization commands upon container startup by setting environment variable:
INIT_SQL_COMMANDS
to a string of SQL commands separated by semicolons - example value:
SET threads = 1; SET memory_limit = '1GB';
.
Here is a full example of running the Docker image with initialization SQL commands:
#
Pull and run the Docker image
docker run --name gizmosql \
--detach \
--rm \
--tty \
--init \
--publish 31337:31337 \
--env TLS_ENABLED=
"
1
"
\
--env GIZMOSQL_PASSWORD=
"
gizmosql_password
"
\
--env PRINT_QUERIES=
"
1
"
\
--env INIT_SQL_COMMANDS=
"
SET threads = 1; SET memory_limit = '1GB';
"
\
--pull missing \
gizmodata/gizmosql:latest
You can also specify a file containing initialization SQL commands by setting environment variable:
INIT_SQL_COMMANDS_FILE
to the path of the file containing the SQL commands - example value:
/tmp/init.sql
.  The file must be mounted inside the container.
Note
: for the DuckDB back-end - the following init commands are automatically run for you:
SET autoinstall_known_extensions = true; SET autoload_known_extensions = true;
Note
: Initialization SQL commands which SELECT data will NOT show the results (this is not supported).
Note
: Initialization SQL commands which fail will cause the Flight SQL server to abort and exit with a non-zero exit code.

用户可以通过发布的 Docker 镜像运行 GizmoSQL，并可选择启用或禁用 TLS。运行时可以挂载自定义的 DuckDB 数据库文件，该文件需使用 DuckDB 1.3.0 版本创建。此外，用户可在容器启动时执行初始化 SQL 命令，但选择查询结果不会显示，且失败的命令将导致服务器退出。最后，GizmoSQL 支持通过 JDBC 连接到服务器。

data.title: Show HN: Controlling 3D models with voice and hand gestures
data.author: getToTheChopin
data.article_summary: "3D Model Playground" 是一个开源网页应用，允许用户通过手势和语音命令实时控制3D模型。该项目使用 Three.js 进行3D渲染，MediaPipe 进行手势追踪，Web Speech API 进行语音识别。用户可以通过说 "drag"（拖拽）、"rotate"（旋转）、"scale"（缩放）或 "animate"（动画）来改变互动模式，并通过捏合手指控制3D模型。此外，用户还可以拖放 GLTF 格式的3D模型到页面进行导入。该项目需要现代浏览器支持 WebGL，并访问摄像头和麦克风。项目代码可在 GitHub 获取，并遵循 MIT 许可证。

data.title: Track Errors First
data.author: GarethX
data.article_summary: 文章强调了在构建可观察性系统时，应首先关注错误（errors），因为错误是系统出现问题时最直接、最有价值的信号。作者指出，尽管传统的可观察性模型包括日志、指标和追踪三个支柱，但它们无法直接指出代码出错的具体位置。相比之下，错误提供了明确的堆栈轨迹、本地变量、请求数据和用户上下文等关键信息。文章建议，在系统出错时应尽可能多地收集上下文信息，而不是仅仅收集分散的日志或指标数据。此外，作者提醒开发者，虽然许多应用性能监控（APM）工具声称跟踪错误，但往往仅限于计数或简单汇总，未能提供完整的错误细节。作者强调，错误应被视为首要关注点，而非次要的数据点。文章最后提到，作者是错误跟踪工具Bugsink的创始人，并基于这一理念构建了该工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：程序开发中的错误处理与日志记录方法，以及不同工具和平台（如Sentry、Bugsink等）的使用体验和评价。

不同观点：
• [arnsholt] 认为在开发过程中应该大量抛出错误，以提醒开发者注意未保持的不变量。在生产环境中，错误越接近源头处理越容易，避免错误状态被持久化后引发更复杂的问题。
• [edelbitter] 强调错误不仅仅是另一个事件，它带有特定的上下文。所有的日志事件都应该带有上下文，以便更容易追踪问题。对随机出现的警告日志感到困扰，因为它们缺乏必要的上下文信息。
• [marcosdumay] 指出可观察性社区中日志充满了无用信息，导致错误信息容易被淹没，认为这是该社区发展过程中必然的结果，但已经到了可以忽视这些信息的阶段。
• [jensenbox] 喜欢使用Sentry，但认为它变得过于复杂，欢迎市场上有更多竞争者出现。
• [bheesink] 测试了Bugsink，并对其在Django项目中的表现感到满意，尤其看重其数据隐私保护特性，确保数据留在欧盟境内。
• [rco8786] 依赖Sentry进行错误跟踪，乐见市场上有新的竞争产品出现。
• [arp242] 认为日志在生产问题调试中很少有用，而错误信息则几乎总是有帮助。批评了许多组织在日志中产生大量“噪音”，使得错误信息被忽略。
• [jtwaleson] 期待有一个自托管的Sentry替代方案，因为数据过滤总是滞后，容易泄露用户隐私。

补充讨论：
• [MattSayar] 提出MELT（Metrics, Errors, Logs, Traces）的概念，认为这些元素都是有用的。
• [18172828286177] 回应MELT，认为良好的日志能够指出代码出错的位置。
• [827a] 询问当前大家使用的错误报告工具。
• [bugsense] 简单提到“传递火炬”，暗示可能是在告别或转型。

争议焦点：
• 错误与日志在开发和生产环境中的作用与重要性。部分开发者认为日志信息缺乏上下文，难以追踪问题，而错误信息则更加直接和有用。
• Sentry等工具的复杂性与隐私保护问题，部分开发者欢迎更多简单和自托管的替代方案。

Track Errors First
Klaas van Schelven;
June 4 - 5 min read
Observability usually means collecting dashboards, traces, metrics, and logs — or at least, that’s how it’s sold.
What’s often missing from that conversation is
the most valuable signal
of all:
errors.
When an exception is raised, your code is telling you:
this was not supposed to happen
. Not just that something is
slow, or that usage is spiking — but that
your assumptions, as a programmer, just failed
.
That makes an exception — a real, raised error — the single most useful event you can track.
If you’re building out observability, whether for the first time or revisiting an existing setup,
start with that
.
The three pillars of observability
The standard model splits observability into three pillars:
logs, metrics, and traces
. They’re helpful, but something
is missing — and if you only follow this model, you’ll miss it too.
Logs
tell you what the system thought was worth noting.
Metrics
show trends over time: request duration, error rates, cache hit ratios.
Traces
give a sense of flow: what did this request call, and how long did it take?
All of those are useful. But none of them tell you
where the code broke
. For that, you need proper error tracking.
Signal Over Noise
There’s nothing more direct than a thrown exception. You don’t have to guess whether it’s important.
It’s the system saying:
this should not have happened, and here’s the line where it went wrong.
Right to the heart of the problem: a stacktrace with local variables
And because exceptions are so rare – so high-signal – it’s worth going deep when they happen. You want to capture:
The full stacktrace
— readable, with line numbers and source references
Local variables
— so you know what was actually passed in
Request data
— like URL paths, headers, or session info
User context
— who was affected, what were they doing?
You can’t get this from a metric. And you usually don’t get it from a log line unless you’ve done a
lot of extra
work
.
So instead of collecting a little information about everything that works — one trace here, one log line there — you’re
better off collecting
as much context as possible
at the moment your system breaks.
As one developer put it:
“One exception is worth a thousand logs.”
Missing from the Diagram
The canonical “three pillars” of observability are logs, metrics, and traces.
But
error tracking isn’t even mentioned
.
If you believe exceptions are your highest-signal events — and you probably should — then this model doesn’t just feel
incomplete.
It’s actively misleading.
It reflects what’s easy to generalize, easy to collect, and easy to sell — not necessarily what’s most useful when your
code breaks.
The Temple of Observability, with Errors fallen to the side
Technically Covered
In most observability platforms, errors are not missing — just abstracted.
They show up in logs, get counted in metrics, or appear as failed spans in traces. Some platforms file them under
generic “events,” alongside cache misses, deployments, and GC pauses.
This flattening makes implementation easier. Everything becomes a stream of telemetry — uniform, processable, and easy
to route.
But that abstraction comes at a cost. An exception isn’t just another event.  It’s your code
telling you it failed
,
in a specific place, with a specific context. If the system treats that like just another row in a data pipeline, you’ll
likely get the minimum: a message string, maybe a timestamp, maybe a partial trace.
Error tracking requires collecting more.
Stack traces, local variables, request metadata, user context — details
that rarely make it into standard logs or metric counters.
So yes, errors are technically covered. But they’re not treated as meaningful failures. Just another data point, in a
sea of unrelated ones.
You’re (probably) not Google
You’re probably not Google. And even if you are,
errors should come first — APM second.
Exceptions give you the clearest, most actionable signal when something breaks. You want full context, not a red dot on a
dashboard.
Plenty of APM tools claim to track errors — but often that just means counting them.
You get a spike on a chart, maybe a summary, rarely the full story. If exceptions are your highest-signal events, that
shouldn’t be an afterthought.
And watch out even with dedicated error tracking tools. Some of them started strong, fast, focused, developer-first,
but have since drifted into full observability platforms. Dashboards got added, then tracing, then metrics pipelines.
More tabs, more noise, more clicks.
So take a moment to check: Are errors still first-class in your stack? Or just another checkbox on a sales sheet?
Not your Neutral Observer
So who’s your friendly author? I’m Klaas,
the founder of
Bugsink
: an error tracking tool.
So yes, I have a stake in this – but not by accident.
I built a tool around this belief, not the other way around. And I think the current ecosystem, with its emphasis on
full-stack APM suites and dashboard-driv

data.article_summary: 《Privacy At Risk: Government Buries Lawful Access Provisions in New Border Bill》一文指出，加拿大政府在《强边境法》(Bill C-2)中暗藏了允许无证访问互联网用户信息的条款。这些条款涉及无证访问互联网用户数据、制定新的全球生产命令以及加强对电子服务提供商数据的访问，旨在扩大执法部门的权限。自1999年以来，加拿大执法机构一直试图通过各种法案获取互联网用户数据，但多次因公众和法院的反对而失败。2014年，最高法院在Spencer案中裁定用户信息受隐私保护。尽管如此，执法部门仍试图通过将无证访问与边境安全等问题挂钩来推动立法。文章批评了这种将无关网络数据访问条款纳入边境安全法案的过度行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加拿大法律和政治体系中的问题及相关争议

不同观点：
• **redm的观点**：认为政客经常通过在不同时间以略微不同的语言重复提交类似的法律条款，直到这些条款最终通过。这种做法被视为一种不正当的“法律闹剧”，且往往会成功。这种评论反映了对于立法过程中的漏洞和政客操纵手法的批评。

• **transcriptase的观点**：指出了加拿大司法系统中存在的一些问题，包括找到和起诉犯罪分子后，由于保释制度和法院积压案件，犯罪分子可能会很快被释放或者案件被撤销。具体提到加拿大最高法院对审理时间的严格限制，导致案件可能因为无法及时审理而被撤销，或者因为辩护律师提出的系统性问题作为辩护理由而被释放。这一观点反映了对于刑事司法系统效率和公平性的质疑。

• **petermcneeley的观点**：引用了CTV News的文章，指出为了打击洗钱和资助恐怖主义，加拿大对超过1万加元的现金交易和一人存入他人账户的现金存款施加了新的限制。这个评论更像是在提供信息，指出政府为应对特定问题所采取的法律措施。

• **dismalaf的观点**：批评了加拿大的选民和政客，特别是对前加拿大央行行长卡尼（Carney）的转变表示不满。评论认为卡尼在竞选时表现得像一个保护国家和民族主义的角色，但当选后却回归到全球主义和权威主义的立场。这个评论反映了对政客言行不一以及选民判断能力的质疑。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：不同评论对加拿大法律和政治体系的有效性和公正性存在争议。例如，redm和transcriptase对立法和司法过程中的漏洞和不公提出批评，而petermcneeley则引用了政府为应对特定问题所采取的措施。dismalaf的评论则更多地关注政客的言行不一和选民的判断能力。

• **论据和例子**：评论中提到了具体的法律条款、司法案例和政客的背景（如卡尼的例子），这些都被用来支持各自的观点和批评。

• **讨论关系**：redm和transcriptase的观点在批评法律和司法体系的漏洞上有相似之处，而petermcneeley提供了具体的法律措施作为背景信息。dismalaf的评论则更像是一种对政客和选民的综合性批评，与其他评论形成对比。

44190832.article_content:
Welcome Mat by Bruce Bortin https://flic.kr/p/dZGkk CC BY-NC 2.0
News
Privacy At Risk: Government Buries Lawful Access Provisions in New Border Bill
June 4, 2025
The government yesterday introduced the
Strong Border Act (Bill C-2)
, legislation that was
promoted
as establishing new border measure provisions presumably designed to address U.S. concerns regarding the border. Yet buried toward the end of the bill are lawful access provisions that have nothing to do with the border. Those provisions, which raise the prospect of warrantless access to information about Internet subscribers, establish new global production orders of subscriber information, and envision new levels of access to data held by electronic service providers, mark the latest attempt in a longstanding campaign by Canadian law enforcement for lawful access legislation. Stymied by the Supreme Court of Canada (which has ruled that there is a
reasonable expectation of privacy in subscriber data
) and by repeated failures to present a compelling evidentiary case for warrantless access, law enforcement has instead tried to frame lawful access as essential to address everything from
organized crime
to
cyber-bullying
to (now)
border safety
. Much like the government’s overreach last year on online harms, Bill C-2 overreaches by including measures on Internet subscriber data that have nothing to do with border safety or security but raise privacy and civil liberties concerns that are bound to spark opposition. This post provides the background on lawful access and an overview of some Bill C-2’s provisions with more details on key elements to come.
Lawful Access Background
The pressure from Canadian law enforcement for access to Internet subscriber data dates back to 1999, when government officials began crafting proposals that included legal powers to access surveillance and subscriber information. What followed were a series of lawful access bills that sparked opposition – both in the public and effectively in the courts. For example, a 2010 lawful access bill included mandated the disclosure of Internet provider customer information, including customer name, address, phone number, email address, Internet protocol address, and a series of device identification numbers without court oversight.
That bill stalled, but in February 2012, then-Public Safety Minister Vic Toews introduced Internet surveillance legislation that once again sparked widespread criticism from across the political spectrum. Toews
infamously
said to Francis Scarpaleggia, now the Speaker of the House but then a critic of the bill, that he “could stand with us or with the child pornographers.” The comment did not help his case and the overwhelming negative publicity pressured the government to quickly backtrack by placing it on hold.
In 2013, then-Justice Minister Rob Nicholson announced that the bill was dead,
confirming
“we will not be proceeding with Bill C-30 and any attempts that we will continue to have to modernize the Criminal Code will not contain the measures contained in C-30.” Nicholson’s commitment lasted less than a year. By 2014, Peter MacKay, then the new federal justice minister, unveiled Bill C-13, which was marketed as an effort to crack down on cyber-bullying. Yet the vast majority of the bill brought back many (though not all) lawful access provisions found in the earlier proposal.
The lawful access campaign was effectively derailed for a decade by the Supreme Court of Canada. In the 2
014 Spencer decision
, the Court ruled that there was a reasonable expectation of privacy in Internet subscriber information:
in the totality of the circumstances of this case, there is a reasonable expectation of privacy in the subscriber information. The disclosure of this information will often amount to the identification of a user with intimate or sensitive activities being carried out online, usually on the understanding that these activities would be anonymous. A request by a police officer that an ISP voluntarily disclose such information amounts to a search.
There were some efforts to revive lawful access, but in 2017 the House of Commons Standing Committee on Public Safety and National Security r
ecommended against introducing reforms
:
That at this time, and following the Supreme Court of Canada’s decision in R. v. Spencer, no changes to the lawful access regime for subscriber information and encrypted information be made, but that the House of Commons Standing Committee on Public Safety and National Security continue to study such rapidly evolving technological issues related to cyber security.
Last year, the Supreme Court expanded the privacy safeguards in the
Bykovets decision
, ruling that “if section 8 of the Charter is to meaningfully protect the online privacy of Canadians in today’s overwhelmingly digital world, it must protect their IP addresses. An IP address is the crucial link between an Internet user and their online activity.” The case is discussed in th

data.title: Sodern launches Astradia, a star tracker for GNSS-denied navigation
data.author: sorenjan
data.article_summary: Sodern annonce le lancement d'Astradia, un viseur d'étoiles pour la navigation aéronautique civile et militaire. Couplé à une centrale inertielle, il assure une navigation précise, robuste et non dépendante des signaux GNSS, fonctionnant de jour comme de nuit grâce aux étoiles. Astradia est particulièrement résistant au brouillage et à la désinformation, et ne détecte aucune onde, garantissant la discrétion. Avec un poids inférieur à 3 kg et une grande précision de pointage, il est conçu pour une variété de porteurs aériens, y compris les drones et les avions de surveillance. Sa commercialisation débutera en juin 2025 au prix de 250 000 € HT.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：天文导航技术在现代应用中的可行性、优缺点以及与现有技术的比较。

不同观点：
• [perihelions] 认为可以在太空中设置光学导航信标，与仅依赖惯性导航的现有解决方案相比，通过人工“星星”可以获得额外的视差测量，从而得到更完整的坐标系。这种方法可以弥补仅依靠星体追踪进行方向参考的不足。

• [blacklion] 对技术进步表示赞赏，认为技术已经形成了闭环，表明对这种技术进步持积极态度。

• [contingencies] 对该技术的实际应用持怀疑态度，认为3公斤的重量在GNSS denied环境下提供的可靠性性价比不高。他提出通过气压计、惯性测量单元（IMU）、数字高程模型（DEM）等技术也能获得类似的定位精度。因此，他认为该技术更像是一个针对“已知风险”的快速修复方案，而不是一个高效的解决方案，尤其对于无人机等需要高效率的设备来说。

• [AStonesThrow] 对该技术的实现细节感兴趣，特别关注该星体追踪器使用的波长，表明对技术细节有深入了解的意愿。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该天文导航技术的实际应用价值，尤其是在现代如无人机等需要轻便和高效的设备中是否值得采用。

• [contingencies] 提出了其他技术如气压测高、惯性导航和地形模型的组合使用，认为这些技术可能提供更具性价比的解决方案，从而削弱了天文导航技术的市场吸引力。

• [perihelions] 提出的光学导航信标的想法引发了关于如何进一步完善现有天文导航系统的讨论，提出了通过增加人工信标来提升测量精度的可能性。

44190498.article_content:
< Retour
Posté le
27 Mai 2025
Évènements
Optronique spatiale
Sodern annonce la commercialisation d’Astradia, un viseur d’étoiles qui, combiné à une centrale inertielle, permet une navigation plus précise, robuste et non leurrable.
Spécialement conçu pour les porteurs aéronautiques civils et militaires, Astradia
fonctionne de jour comme de nuit
grâce aux étoiles, quel que soit l’endroit sur Terre.
Astradia sera présenté au salon SIAE du Bourget 2025 sur le stand de Sodern.
Le 27 mai 2025 – Sodern a le plaisir de lancer la commercialisation d’Astradia :
un viseur diurne
capable d’épauler les systèmes de navigation pour les rendre non tributaires des signaux GNSS de radionavigation.
Après plusieurs années de recherche et développement, Sodern a mis au point Astradia, un viseur céleste endoatmosphérique qui, couplé à une centrale inertielle, fournit de jour et de nuit une mesure d’attitude afin de garantir une information de géolocalisation embarquée précise, robuste et fiable.
Ce viseur de haute performance est donc autonome, non tributaire de signaux de radionavigation et vise à contrer la dérive naturelle des centrales inertielles. De plus, il présente l’avantage de n’émettre aucune onde qui rendrait le porteur détectable.
Contrairement aux systèmes de géolocalisation par satellite, un système de navigation couplé « inertie-viseur » offre une mesure absolue fiable et sûre.
Aujourd’hui, la plupart des systèmes de géolocalisation présentent l’inconvénient d’être extrêmement vulnérables car ils utilisent une technologie basée sur les signaux de radionavigation par satellite (GPS, Galileo, etc.). Ces services de géolocalisation peuvent être non seulement brouillés ou temporairement indisponibles mais aussi facilement leurrés en générant de fausses données. Avec Astradia, Sodern propose une toute nouvelle technologie aux porteurs de types aéronefs civils ou militaires, qui ont besoin d’un système fiable ou qui souhaitent rester discrets en n’émettant aucune onde.
Astradia bénéficie de tout l’héritage en vol des viseurs d’étoiles et de moyens performants comme les bancs de calibration certifiés.
Astradia est à la fois le fruit du savoir-faire de Sodern et d’une technologie de pointe qui a fait ses preuves. Astradia bénéficie, en effet, de l’héritage de plusieurs milliers de viseurs d’étoiles déjà en vol dans l’espace ainsi que d’un catalogue d’étoiles et d’algorithmes de détection éprouvés.
Par ailleurs, cette technologie a déjà bénéficié d’essais en vol concluants.
«
Chez Sodern, nous sommes fiers de concevoir des technologies duales, qui exigent à la fois précision et robustesse pour répondre à un besoin spécifique des armées et une conception industrielle pour une meilleure optimisation des coûts. Astradia en est un très bon exemple et intéressera aussi bien des porteurs militaires que des avions civils
» affirme Sandra Feilles, Directrice de l’Innovation et des Programmes.
Astradia, un viseur spécialement conçu pour répondre aux besoins des porteurs aéronautiques.
Avec un encombrement réduit (176 mm x 185 mm x 207 mm) et un poids inférieur à 3 kg, Astradia a été spécialement conçu pour s’intégrer facilement à tous types de porteurs aéronautiques. Cette conception optimisée rend Astradia idéal pour un large éventail d’applications, y compris les drones et les avions de surveillance. Sa conception monobloc et sa facilité d’intégration en font un
choix polyvalent et efficace pour diverses missions aéronautiques.
Une capacité de pointage d’une grande précision.
Astradia offre une capacité de pointage de quelques secondes d’arc près, équivalente à 1 mètre pour une distance de 70 km. Cette fonctionnalité très utile pour l’alignement et le recalage des systèmes de navigation inertiels ouvre aussi la porte à de futures autres applications particulièrement exigeantes en pointage.
Chaque seconde et sans interruption, de jour comme de nuit, ce capteur délivre des mesures à l’aéronef avec une capacité opérationnelle à tout endroit sur Terre, y compris sur les océans, et sans aucune servitude de mise à jour de cartes pour exécuter sa mission.
Ce capteur concourt à réduire efficacement les dérives de navigation des longs vols, et plus généralement à améliorer la sécurité de localisation en vol.
Astradia sera commercialisé dès juin 2025 au prix HT d’environ 250 000€.

data.title: 10 Years of Betting on Rust
data.author: K0nserv
data.article_summary: 本文回顾了作者使用Rust编程语言十年的经历和感受。作者在2015年首次接触Rust，尽管早期存在版本兼容性差、编译时间长等问题，但Rust的独特优势如内存安全和高效能逐渐显现。随着时间推移，Rust的生态系统日益成熟，编译和升级变得更加可预测，错误提示更友好，依赖关系更稳定。如今，Rust已成为许多领域的可靠选择，尤其在系统和后端开发中表现出色。作者认为，Rust的成功归功于社区的贡献和志愿者的努力，他们塑造了Rust的独特魅力和长期价值。Rust不仅是一种技术选择，更体现了对编程体验的深刻理解和改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust语言的异步编程复杂性、技术工具（如博客平台）的使用体验、以及具体技术问题（如X11的中键功能）

不同观点：
• Arch-TK认为博客平台的实时编辑功能是个噱头，导致了意外的文本编辑问题，特别是影响了X11中键选择缓冲区的使用，这对他们的生产力至关重要。他们明确表示不喜欢这种设计。
• weinzierl对文章中提到的Rust异步编程的高复杂性表示认同，并提到Rust过去通过libgreen实现并发性的尝试，尽管因为性能和维护成本被移除，但认为值得重新审视这种方案，以简化语言的异步部分。

44190190.article_content:
10 years of betting on Rust
and what I’m looking forward to next.
By Alec Mocatta, Founder
1 Jun, 2025
I wrote my first line of Rust in June 2015,
a month after the buzz of Rust 1.0 landing
. Coming from C, Python, and JavaScript, I never looked back. Two Rust-based startups and 500k lines of Rust later, here are some reflections on the milestone.
The early days were painful
Version compatibility was poor—both between crates and with the compiler itself. A bug-fix update could force a compiler bump, which in turn dragged in unstable crates like
syntex
(
once
a key
serde
dependency) and their dependents. In practice we “updated the world” and temporally pinned when a critical bug fix or feature demanded it—early on this was as often as every 6-week compiler release cycle. An awful lot of time was wasted binary-searching for compatible version combinations.
“Fighting the borrow checker” was real for me. Traits came naturally given background in C++, Java and Objective-C, but lifetimes and the idea of “proofs” that (
*mostly
) don’t affect codegen took a while to grok. Patient friends and colleagues made this easier!
After a couple years of our codebase and team growing, compile times became painful. Large types were a
recurring
issue (and
still are
, occasionally), requiring diagnosis and mitigation. Investments brought it down for us, but iteration cycles still took a hit and rapid prototyping generally required effort to set up.
The people were and are exceptional
The Rust ecosystem has an impressive amount of programming “taste”, manifesting in dependencies with relatively simple builds, elegant implementations, and fast and robust performance. Reaching for TypeScript or Python is a relative exercise in frustration. There’s a reason Rust has taken the
“most loved/admired language”
title for nine years now!
“What went right” is an essay in itself, but the evolving cadre of dedicated, opinionated and earnest volunteers, with strong mores around saying “no” and “not yet”, are I think the crux of it.
I reaped the benefits as an employer. We’ve been fortunate to be one of few Rust opportunities in London, with a pipeline of talented engineers keen to work in their favourite language. That your average Rust programmer is better than your average <most other languages> programmer has been a bonus.
Rust has become a safe bet (in some domains)
The early days necessitated a lot of
yak shaving
. Omissions in
std
, for example, led to our evolving a library of workarounds, hacks and extensions: code that simplified or optimised our application code but wasn’t ready or wasn’t justifiable to merge upstream. Over time the rate of additions to it has slowed, and we regularly find ourselves now removing from it.
Our
custom
implementations
begone
! Nowadays being able to rely upon
std
’s primitives having even relatively
uncommon
or
abstract
implementations, and them be well-optimised, is a joy.
This reliability now extends to much of the Rust experience. Building and upgrading is wildly more predictable, with fewer non-Rust dependencies, ~no surprise compiletime/codegen/inlining blowups, less ecosystem reliance on nightly features and greater respecting of semver.
Inference
improvements
have made the borrow checker friendlier to newcomers. And far fewer ICEs on nightly! We used to see new ICEs or link errors almost weekly, now it’s quarterly at most.
The crate ecosystem is more predictable too: newer crates like
jiff
,
polars
and
tauri
build on the hard-won lessons of earlier projects, while stalwarts like
tokio
,
hyper
and
regex
have earned robustness through years of heavy production use.
Ten years ago choosing Rust for production opted you into reinventing wheels and working around known and unknown issues. While still the case for some domains—namely Rust in the browser for us—for general systems and backend engineering that is a thing of the past. Rust empowers us to focus on business logic while producing remarkably fast and robust applications.
Rust today feels like what programming should be
More than a safe bet, Rust has a degree of programmer empathy that is unprecedented in large software projects: simple and robust builds, the best
error messages
and linting around, great docs and IDE integration, and strong
CI
and
regression testing
. Rust feels like a passion project, a labour of love by and for programmers.
10 years ago could we have predicted this? Well, I think some did. Pained by the status quo, some saw the potential of a language, an ecosystem, designed
well
by people like them. They volunteered their time and made Rust what it is. As Graydon Hoare, one of Rust’s original authors,
puts it
:
Rust today is the result of significant investments made by forward-looking institutions and the efforts of thousands of individuals who shared a belief in the long-term payoff of what they were building.
I bet my time and (my investors’) money on Rust 10 years ago because I believed in this payoff. The enthusiasm wa

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: DNS4EU是一个由欧盟开发的公共DNS服务，旨在为个人提供快速、安全、注重隐私的网络浏览体验。该服务提供五种解析选项，包括基础保护、儿童保护、广告拦截等功能，用户可根据需求选择合适的方案。DNS4EU专为欧盟公民设计，不适用于通信提供商或政府。该服务通过多种安全标准如DNSSEC来防御网络攻击，并严格遵循GDPR等隐私保护法规。其服务器分布于欧盟各地，确保高效可靠。用户可以根据指南轻松配置DNS，享受安全、灵活的网络浏览体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟资助的DNS4EU项目的成本、网站设计、用户体验、安全性和技术实现等方面的问题。

不同观点：
• 对项目成本的质疑：[olieidel]指出该项目的预算为€3M，已经使用了€1M，其中大部分资金流向了一家名为"Whalebone sro"的公司。他还提到之前分析和重建的欧盟医疗设备数据库项目，该项目已经花费了€45M，并且有一个50人的团队在维护一个只有500k条目（约10GB）的数据库，质疑DNS4EU的高成本。

• 网站设计的批评：[olieidel]和[ahofmann]都对DNS4EU网站的设计表示不满。[ahofmann]特别强调用户体验，指出需要减少用户操作摩擦，认为DNS4EU网站在提供关键信息（如IP地址）方面做得不够直接。相比之下，Cloudflare和Google的DNS服务在这方面做得更好。

• 对安全保护的疑惑：[falcor84]对项目所声称的"增强保护"表示困惑，质疑大多数用户是否真的需要这些额外的保护。

• 对国家控制DNS服务的看法：[sph]认为由国家支持和控制的DNS服务是有益的，但也暗示那些有隐私顾虑或反体制倾向的人可能会选择非官方的软件。

• IP地址记忆问题：[tigrezno]提到DNS4EU的IP地址不如Cloudflare或Google的DNS那么简单易记。

• 技术实现问题：[teddyh]指出DNS4EU解析器未正确设置反向DNS，且主机名没有AAAA记录指向IPv6地址。

• 替代服务的提及：[throw0101b]提到加拿大有一个类似的服务CIRA，提供给加拿大人使用。

• 自建DNS服务器的讨论：[louwrentius]指出如果用户愿意设置自己的DNS服务器，就不需要使用转发DNS服务，并提到DNS4EU可能在提供额外过滤功能方面有其价值。

• 广告过滤的技术细节：[AStonesThrow]分享了关于Pi-hole和IP地址0.0.0.0的技术经验。

• 网站内容的错误：[bsenftner]发现"下载威胁情报白皮书"链接返回404错误。

• 对现代DNS安全要求的建议：[sneak]指出任何现代公共DNS都需要支持DoH（DNS over HTTPS），并认为设置指南应该指导用户这样配置，以防止ISP对未加密DNS请求的嗅探、阻止和重写。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到Cloudflare（1.1.1.1）的用户体验和技术实现，作为对比DNS4EU的参考。
• 对欧盟资助项目的一般性怀疑态度，尤其是在成本和团队规模方面。
• 强调用户体验设计中的"不要让我思考"原则，即直接提供用户所需的关键信息，减少不必要的操作。

总体来看，讨论主要围绕DNS4EU项目的成本效益、技术实现和用户体验展开，并对欧盟资助项目的透明度和效率提出质疑。

data.title: Phptop: Simple PHP ressource profiler, safe and useful for production sites
data.author: kadrek
data.article_summary: PHPtop 是由 Bearstech 开发的一个开源 PHP 资源分析工具，适用于生产环境。它能够监控和显示每个查询的 CPU 时间（用户、系统和总时间）及内存使用情况，支持 PHP 5.2.0 及以上版本，已在多个生产服务器上长期稳定运行。使用方法简单，只需在 `php.ini` 或 `.user.ini` 中添加一行配置，重启服务器后即可收集数据。示例输出显示了每个 URL 的命中次数、时间消耗和内存使用等信息，有助于性能优化。该工具基于 GPL-3.0 协议发布，由多名贡献者开发维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于某性能监控工具的实用性、功能性及兼容性的讨论

不同观点：
• [nchmy] 认为该工具的输出过于泛泛，不太清楚"query"是否指代"request"。他对工具的功能如wpdb机制的报告内容（总查询时间、最慢查询）表示质疑，认为类似Query Monitor的工具更强大。他还推荐了php-spx作为性能分析工具，并指出xhgui虽然类似但不如php-spx精准。
• [basilgohar] 认为该工具对WordPress站点可能更有用，但对非WordPress环境（如PDO查询的拦截和分析）帮助有限。不过，他认为免费提供代码本身仍有价值，不应完全贬低其作用。

补充讨论：
• 工具的功能实现细节存在争议，尤其是"query"的定义和wpdb机制是否足够实用。

• 工具的适用场景和兼容性问题也是讨论的焦点之一，尤其是其在不同技术栈（如nginx+php-fpm）上的可行性。

data.title: FDA rushed out agency-wide AI tool—it’s not going well
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）在特朗普政府时期积极采用人工智能工具，推出了名为Elsa的大型语言模型（LLM），旨在加速临床协议审查和科学评估，并识别高优先级的检查目标。然而，据NBC News和Stat新闻报道，FDA工作人员测试Elsa时发现其提供的总结存在完全或部分错误，工具显得仓促且不准确。工作人员认为Elsa的能力被过度宣传，目前仅适用于行政任务，而非科学工作。此外，FDA未能为该工具的使用制定完善的政策和防护措施。Elsa基于Anthropic的Claude LLM，由咨询公司Deloitte开发，耗资数百万美元。此前，各中心独立进行AI试点，但在削减成本后，FDA选择将CDER-GPT扩展为全局版本并重命名为Elsa。

Under the Trump administration, the Food and Drug Administration is eagerly embracing artificial intelligence tools that staff members are reportedly calling rushed, buggy, overhyped, and inaccurate.
On Monday, the FDA publicly announced the
agency-wide rollout of a large language model (LLM) called Elsa
, which is intended to help FDA employees—"from scientific reviewers to investigators." The FDA said the generative AI is already being used to "accelerate clinical protocol reviews, shorten the time needed for scientific evaluations, and identify high-priority inspection targets."
"It can summarize adverse events to support safety profile assessments, perform faster label comparisons, and generate code to help develop databases for nonclinical applications," the announcement promised.
In a statement, FDA Chief AI Officer Jeremy Walsh trumpeted the rollout, saying: "Today marks the dawn of the AI era at the FDA[. W]ith the release of Elsa, AI is no longer a distant promise but a dynamic force enhancing and optimizing the performance and potential of every employee."
Meanwhile, FDA Commissioner Marty Makary highlighted the speed with which the tool was rolled out. "I set an aggressive timeline to scale AI agency-wide by June 30," Makary said. "Today’s rollout of Elsa is ahead of schedule and under budget, thanks to the collaboration of our in-house experts across the centers."
Rushed and inaccurate
However, according to
a report from NBC News
, Elsa could have used some more time in development. FDA staff tested Elsa on Monday with questions about FDA-approved products or other public information, only to find that it provided summaries that were either completely or partially wrong.
FDA staffers who spoke with Stat news, meanwhile,
called the tool "rushed"
and said its capabilities were overinflated by officials, including Makary and those at the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), which was headed by controversial billionaire Elon Musk. In its current form, it should only be used for administrative tasks, not scientific ones, the staffers said.
"Makary and DOGE think AI can replace staff and cut review times, but it decidedly cannot," one employee said. The staffer also said that the FDA has failed to set up guardrails for the tool's use. "I’m not sure in their rush to get it out that anyone is thinking through policy and use," the FDA employee said.
According to Stat, Elsa is based on Anthropic's Claude LLM and is being developed by consulting firm Deloitte. Since 2020, Deloitte has been paid $13.8 million to develop the original database of FDA documents that Elsa's training data is derived from. In April, the firm was awarded a $14.7 million contract to scale the tech across the agency. The FDA said that Elsa was built within a high-security GovCloud environment and offers a "secure platform for FDA employees to access internal documents while ensuring all information remains within the agency."
Previously, each center within the FDA was working on its own AI pilot. However, after cost-cutting in May, the AI pilot originally developed by the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, called CDER-GPT, was selected to be scaled up to an FDA-wide version and rebranded as Elsa.
FDA staffers in the Center for Devices and Radiological Health told NBC News that their AI pilot, CDRH-GPT, is buggy, isn't connected to the Internet or the FDA's internal system, and has problems uploading documents and allowing users to submit questions.

data.title: A new Pitt study has upended decades-old assumptions about brain plasticity
data.author: XzetaU8
data.article_summary: 一项来自匹兹堡大学的新研究颠覆了神经科学中关于大脑可塑性的长期假设。传统观点认为， spontaneous（自发）和evoked（诱发）神经传导使用相同的突触位点和分子机制，但这项研究发现，大脑实际上使用不同的传输位点来调节这两种活动模式。研究团队聚焦于初级视觉皮层，发现视觉输入后，evoked传导增强，而spontaneous传导保持稳定。通过化学实验，他们证明这两种传导模式通过功能不同的突触位点运作。该发现揭示了大脑如何在保持稳定的同时实现灵活学习和适应，并可能有助于理解自闭症、阿尔茨海默病等神经和精神疾病的机制。

主要讨论点：音乐学习与大脑处理问题的关系

不同观点：
• [randomcarbloke] 认为，将音乐学习的机制正式编纂成文虽然不错，但这不应该是什么新鲜事。对于任何花时间学习过乐器的人来说，这都是显而易见的常识。

• [davydm] 则从另一个角度出发，将这一现象与大脑的"后台线程"模型联系起来。他认为，大脑一直在后台处理问题，解决方案常常会在之后出现，给人一种似乎是随机的感觉。

A new Pitt study has upended decades-old assumptions about brain plasticity
June 3, 2025
A new study from Pitt researchers challenges a decades-old assumption in neuroscience by showing that the brain uses distinct transmission sites — not a shared site — to achieve different types of plasticity. The findings,
published in Science Advances
, offer a deeper understanding of how the brain balances stability with flexibility, a process essential for learning, memory and mental health.
Neurons communicate through a process called synaptic transmission, where one neuron releases chemical messengers called neurotransmitters from a presynaptic terminal. These molecules travel across a microscopic gap called a synaptic cleft and bind to receptors on a neighboring postsynaptic neuron, triggering a response.
Traditionally, scientists believed spontaneous transmissions (signals that occur randomly) and evoked transmissions (signals triggered by sensory input or experience) originated from one type of canonical synaptic site and relied on shared molecular machinery. Using a mouse model, the research team — led by Oliver Schlüter, associate professor of neuroscience in the Kenneth P. Dietrich School of Arts and Sciences — discovered that the brain instead uses separate synaptic transmission sites to carry out regulation of these two types of activity, each with its own developmental timeline and regulatory rules.
“We focused on the primary visual cortex, where cortical visual processing begins,” said Yue Yang, a research associate in the Department of Neuroscience and first author of the study. “We expected spontaneous and evoked transmissions to follow a similar developmental trajectory, but instead, we found that they diverged after eye opening.”
As the brain began receiving visual input, evoked transmissions continued to strengthen. In contrast, spontaneous transmissions plateaued, suggesting that the brain applies different forms of control to the two signaling modes.
To understand why, the researchers applied a chemical that activates otherwise silent receptors on the postsynaptic side. This caused spontaneous activity to increase, while evoked signals remained unchanged — strong evidence that the two types of transmission operate through functionally distinct synaptic sites.
This division likely enables the brain to maintain consistent background activity through spontaneous signaling while refining behaviorally relevant pathways through evoked activity. This dual system supports both homeostasis and Hebbian plasticity, the experience-dependent process that strengthens neural connections during learning.
“Our findings reveal a key organizational strategy in the brain,” said Yang. “By separating these two signaling modes, the brain can remain stable while still being flexible enough to adapt and learn.”
The implications could be broad. Abnormalities in synaptic signaling have been linked to conditions like autism, Alzheimer’s disease and substance use disorders. A better understanding of how these systems operate in the healthy brain may help researchers identify how they become disrupted in disease.
“Learning how the brain normally separates and regulates different types of signals brings us closer to understanding what might be going wrong in neurological and psychiatric conditions,” Yang said.
This work was supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health, the Whitehall Foundation, the Alzheimer’s Association and the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft, and under Germany's Excellence Strategy.

data.author: cyberplaid
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种免费、无需登录的在线AI老照片修复服务。用户可以上传损坏、褪色或有划痕的老照片，AI将自动修复并增强照片的色彩和清晰度，最后提供高分辨率的下载。该服务具有快速、高质量、隐私保护等特点，利用先进的机器学习算法，能够修复裂缝、撕裂、缺失部分，并提升对比度和分辨率。许多用户对修复结果表示满意，称赞其专业和出色的效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图片修复工具的有效性和准确性，尤其是在处理旧照片时的表现。

不同观点：
• [ralphdas] 认为工具在修复照片时缺乏用户的控制权。他提到上传的一张父亲幼年时的照片被修复后，结果展现的是一个中年男人的形象，与实际年龄不符。他希望能够指定某些修复细节。
• [karpour] 对工具的修复方式持批评态度，认为它生成了一个全新的图像，而不是修复原图。他以爱因斯坦的照片为例，指出明显的 facial features 被移除，认为结果虽然美观但并不准确。
• [banner520] 也表示了对修复结果的不满，提到在修复过程中丢失了一些原图的元素，认为算法需要更新。
• [camtarn] 支持 [karpour] 的观点，并进一步指出工具在处理男性照片时无故增加了胡茬，且在爱因斯坦的照片中移除了原有的痣，显示出不准确的问题。

data.title: From Tokens to Thoughts: How LLMs and Humans Trade Compression for Meaning
data.author: ggirelli
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了大型语言模型（LLMs）与人类在语义压缩和意义保持之间的差异。人类通过语义压缩将知识组织成紧凑的类别，在保留意义的同时将不同实例映射到抽象表示。文章引入了一个信息理论框架，比较LLMs和人类的压缩策略。研究发现，虽然LLMs能形成与人类判断相符的广泛概念类别，但在捕捉细粒度的语义区别上存在困难。此外，LLMs倾向于激进的统计压缩，而人类系统则更注重适应性的细微差别和情境丰富性。这些发现揭示了当前AI与人类认知架构的关键差异，为开发更符合人类概念表示的LLMs提供了指导。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对大型语言模型（LLMs）及其分析方法的有效性和研究方法的争议

不同观点：
• [johnnyApplePRNG] 认为该论文只是重申了LLMs是统计工具而非认知系统，尽管使用了信息论框架，但并没有实质性改变这一事实。

• [valine] 对论文的方法论提出强烈质疑，认为论文分析的是输入嵌入模型（EMatrix），而非LLMs本身。他们指出，作者在没有进行前向传播的情况下，仅通过一个静态的嵌入查表来得出结论，且未使用注意力机制（如点积计算），因此质疑作者如何能够对LLMs的内部运作做出声明。此外，他们认为模型大小的比较在此情境下没有意义，因为根本没有激活模型参数。

• [andoando] 表示对研究中的计算方法感到困惑，并认为研究的范围可能过于局限，例如仅限于名词分类（如“知更鸟是鸟”）。

• [fusionadvocate] 提出语言的多义性和复杂性，可能在更广泛的语境下（如不同词语在不同情境中的使用）对LLMs的分析带来挑战。

补充讨论：
• [valine] 特别指出论文中的一张图表，显示模型大小与对齐分数的相关性，认为这是尤其荒谬的，因为根本没有激活任何模型参数。
• 争议的焦点在于研究方法的有效性和合理性，特别是静态嵌入查表是否能够代表LLMs的内部运作，以及在没有进行前向传播和注意力计算的情况下，如何能得出关于LLMs的有效结论。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对研究范围的质疑，特别是研究是否仅限于简单的名词分类任务，从而限制了其对更广泛的语言理解问题的适用性。

Title:
From Tokens to Thoughts: How LLMs and Humans Trade Compression for Meaning
Authors:
Chen Shani
,
Dan Jurafsky
,
Yann LeCun
,
Ravid Shwartz-Ziv
View a PDF of the paper titled From Tokens to Thoughts: How LLMs and Humans Trade Compression for Meaning, by Chen Shani and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Humans organize knowledge into compact categories through semantic compression by mapping diverse instances to abstract representations while preserving meaning (e.g., robin and blue jay are both birds; most birds can fly). These concepts reflect a trade-off between expressive fidelity and representational simplicity. Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable linguistic abilities, yet whether their internal representations strike a human-like trade-off between compression and semantic fidelity is unclear. We introduce a novel information-theoretic framework, drawing from Rate-Distortion Theory and the Information Bottleneck principle, to quantitatively compare these strategies. Analyzing token embeddings from a diverse suite of LLMs against seminal human categorization benchmarks, we uncover key divergences. While LLMs form broad conceptual categories that align with human judgment, they struggle to capture the fine-grained semantic distinctions crucial for human understanding. More fundamentally, LLMs demonstrate a strong bias towards aggressive statistical compression, whereas human conceptual systems appear to prioritize adaptive nuance and contextual richness, even if this results in lower compressional efficiency by our measures. These findings illuminate critical differences between current AI and human cognitive architectures, guiding pathways toward LLMs with more human-aligned conceptual representations.

data.title: American Science and Surplus is fighting for its life. Why Should You Care?
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 美国科学与 surplus 商店成立于1937年，最初以销售镜头和摄影设备起家，现已成为一家多元化的实体店，出售实验室设备、军用剩余物资、工具、电子产品、玩具等。然而，受新冠疫情和成本上涨影响，这家拥有近90年历史的老店正面临生存危机，并发起了一项20万美元的众筹活动。店主帕特·迈耶表示，面对大盒零售商和在线巨头的竞争，小型零售商处境艰难，银行也不愿提供贷款。迈耶希望通过众筹挽救这个深受顾客喜爱的社区机构。尽管部分商品区域缩减，如望远镜区，但店内仍充满各种电机、开关、工具等，体现了创客精神。迈耶在店里工作了41年，对这家店有着深厚感情，不愿看到它消失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国科学面临的生存挑战

不同观点：
• 观点一：美国科学正面临严峻挑战，可能正在“为生存而战”。支持者认为科研资金削减、政治干预以及对科学的不信任正在威胁科学的发展。例子包括环保政策和气候变化研究受到的限制，以及政府对科学机构的预算削减。
  
• 观点二：美国科学依然具有强大的韧性和创新能力，认为其“为生存而战”过于悲观。支持者指出美国仍然是全球科研的领导者，拥有世界一流的大学和研究机构，以及大量的私人资金支持。例子包括美国在生物技术、人工智能等领域的持续突破和创新。

补充讨论：
• 有人指出科学的政治化是当前美国科学面临的主要问题之一，尤其是政府对特定科学领域（如气候变化和公共卫生）的政策影响。
• 另一个讨论点是国际竞争，认为来自中国等国家的科技竞争对美国科学构成威胁，需要更多的政策支持和资金投入以保持领先地位。
• 还有人提到公众对科学的不信任和反智主义倾向是美国科学面临的内在挑战，需要加强科学教育和科普工作来改善这一状况。

争议焦点：美国科学是否真的在“为生存而战”或者只是面临短期挑战，以及如何有效应对这些挑战以保持其全球领导地位。

It was shortly after moving into Chicago's Jefferson Park neighborhood that I saw the sign for the first time: American Science & Surplus. My curiosity piqued, I pulled into the strip mall and walked into a store filled with an unimaginable variety of lab equipment, military surplus, tools, electronics, toys, and so much more.
Now, nearly 90 years after its launch selling "reject lenses" as American Lens & Photo,
American Science & Surplus
is facing an existential threat. The COVID-19 pandemic and increased costs hit the business hard, so the store has launched a
GoFundMe campaign looking to raise $200,000
from customers and fans alike. What's happening in suburban Chicago is a microcosm of the challenges facing local retail, with big-box retailers and online behemoths overwhelming beloved local institutions. It's a story that has played out countless times in the last two-plus decades, and owner Pat Meyer is hoping this tale has a different ending.
American Science & Surplus owner Pat Meyer holds the two most popular items in the store: $4 solenoid switches that are used to repair a well-known brand of single-cup coffee makers.
Credit:
Eric Bangeman
American Science & Surplus owner Pat Meyer holds the two most popular items in the store: $4 solenoid switches that are used to repair a well-known brand of single-cup coffee makers.
Credit:
Eric Bangeman
Launching a fundraiser was a tough choice for Meyer. "I don't like asking people for money," he said.
With his voice catching, he continued: "It's hard for me to talk about sometimes, because the more I'm in the store, the more I see how much people care about it and don't want it to go away."
And the current environment is tough for small business owners. "Banks… are real hesitant [about lending] money," Meyer told Ars. "Interest rates are high, too. So we decided that we were going to try and reach out to the community that we built over the last 88 years."
Walk into any of the three American Science & Surplus' stores in the Illinois-Wisconsin area—two in Illinois, Park Ridge and Geneva, and one in Milwaukee—and it's easy to see why it has such a devoted following. Each aisle could be a store of its own. One has stationery and office supplies. Another has military surplus. The next one over has tools. I head over there regularly just to wander the aisles and see what's in stock. Other times I go looking for a particular oddball item—and I usually find it there.
A long history
Old catalogs from the American Lens & Photo days.
Credit:
American Science & Surplus
Old catalogs from the American Lens & Photo days.
Credit:
American Science & Surplus
American Science & Surplus got its start in 1937 and has expanded its inventory and reach ever since. And Meyer has been a part of the story for the last four decades. "I've done everything in the company that there is to do," he said. "I started off literally scraping floors and Windexing, driven our trucks. I've done warehouse sales, I've done tent sales. I've been store manager, assistant manager, I've done—there isn't anything in this company that I haven't—and it's been my life for 41 years."
Over time, the store has moved far beyond lenses and lab equipment. There's a science toy section and an aisle devoted to Etsy-style craft supplies. But other, once-thriving areas of the business have suffered. When I first discovered American Science & Surplus in the early 2000s, I would always linger at the massive telescope section. The store staff was always more than happy to answer my questions and explain the differences between the scopes. Now, telescopes are just a small corner of the store, and sales are infrequent. "People come in to ask questions and then buy the telescopes online," Meyer explained.
One of the display cases in the Park Ridge store.
Eric Bangeman
One of the display cases in the Park Ridge store.
Eric Bangeman
My kids loved to search through the fossils and minerals when they were younger.

data.title: Statement on California State Senate Advancing Dangerous Surveillance Bill
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: 加州参议院通过S.B. 690法案后，电子前沿基金会（EFF）、TechEquity、加州消费者联合会、加州科技监督组织和ACLU加州行动发布联合声明，警告该法案将严重威胁数百万加州人的隐私和安全。S.B. 690允许公司获取敏感个人信息，如移民状态或医疗记录，且未限制这些信息如何被使用或分享，可能被提供给数据中介、移民官员或限制生殖和性别确认护理州的执法部门。在联邦机构基于政治信仰、宗教 affiliations或健康决定 targeting个人的背景下，该法案将使更多敏感信息落入政府手中，立法机构应保护而非危害加州人隐私。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加州的危险监控法案（SB 690）是否真的如电子前沿基金会（EFF）所描述的那样对隐私和安全构成威胁，还是只是为了保护使用追踪像素（tracking pixels）的人免受无谓的诉讼。

不同观点：
• **phendrenad2的观点**：该法案实际上是在保护使用追踪像素的人，尤其是那些用于投放定向广告的人，使他们免受无谓的法律诉讼。他认为EFF并没有具体说明法案的内容，而是戏剧性地夸大了法案的危害性，声称该法案会导致“反乌托邦式的大科技监控行为”，危及加州人的隐私和安全。phendrenad2认为EFF已经变成了“反派”，暗示EFF失去了中立性和客观性。

• **EFF的观点（推测）**：从phendrenad2的评论中可以推测出，EFF认为SB 690法案是对隐私和安全的重大威胁，可能会导致大科技公司滥用监控技术，从而侵犯用户的隐私权。EFF将该法案描述为“危险”且可能导致“反乌托邦”后果。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：法案的真实影响和EFF的描述是否准确。phendrenad2质疑EFF没有提供具体的法案内容，而是通过戏剧化的语言来引发公众恐慌。EFF则可能认为该法案确实存在严重的隐私和安全风险。

• **重要论据**：
  - phendrenad2认为追踪像素广泛用于定向广告，法案只是为了防止无谓诉讼。
  - EFF则可能利用“反乌托邦”和“侵犯隐私”等词汇强调法案潜在的负面影响。

• **讨论的深度**：phendrenad2认为EFF没有提供具体的法案条文，仅凭其描述无法准确判断法案的实际效果。而EFF的支持者可能会认为，即便法案的表面目的是保护某些技术使用者，但其潜在的负面影响不可忽视。

44189442.article_content:
In the wake of the California State Senate’s passage of S.B. 690, the
Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF)
,
TechEquity
,
Consumer Federation of California
,
Tech Oversight California
, and
ACLU California Action
issued a joint statement warning that the bill would put the safety and privacy of millions of Californians at serious risk:
“SB 690 gives the green-light to dystopian big tech surveillance practices which will endanger the privacy and safety of all Californians. SB 690 would allow companies to spy on us to get our sensitive personal information, such as our immigration status or what healthcare we’ve received. And once they have our sensitive personal information, SB 690 places no limits on how that business can use or share that information, allowing them to share it with data brokers, immigration officials, or law enforcement officials in states that restrict reproductive or gender-affirming care.
“At a time where agencies of the federal government are actively targeting individuals based on information collected from businesses about their political beliefs, religious affiliations, or health decisions, we cannot risk sharing even more sensitive information with them. The legislature should be doing all it can to protect Californians, not make it easier for the federal government to secretly obtain our sensitive information.”

Take Action Against SB 690

data.title: Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Launched for 1.6TbE Generation
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: Broadcom推出了新一代Tomahawk 6系列交换机ASIC，包括BCM78910和BCM78914两款型号。该系列支持高达102.4Tbps的带宽，能够处理64个1.6TbE端口，标志着"Terabit以太网"时代的到来。Tomahawk 6旨在通过提供不同的SerDes选项和配置（如512x 200G或1024x 100G PAM4），实现扩展性和灵活性，满足大规模AI集群的需求。新功能包括Global Load Balancing 2.0和Cognitive Routing 2.0，提升了负载平衡和数据传输智能。此外，Tomahawk 6还通过减少交换层数和光学器件使用，降低了成本和功耗。尽管面临NVIDIA的竞争，Broadcom在AI网络领域仍具有重要影响力。

44189967.article_content:
Networking
Facebook
Twitter

Linkedin

Copy URL
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 200G BCM78914
Today Broadcom is launching its next-generation of switch ASICs with the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 series. This is a new 102.4Tbps switch that can handle up to 64 ports of 1.6TbE. Yes, we are now replacing the “Gigabit” with the “Terabit” Ethernet port era. The two new ASICs, the Broadcom BCM78910 and BCM78914 offer two different configurations for different applications.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Launched for 1.6TbE Generation
In addition to the higher bandwidth, the new switch chips need SerDes to power the ports and improve load balancing and telemetry. We have Broadcom’s launch deck that generally highlights these points.
Broadcom Tomahawk 5 To Tomahawk 6
The idea behind these new switches is that they can be used to scale up or scale out. Scale up, providing massive bandwidth between a smaller number of nodes is one option. The other is to scale out connecting massive numbers of accelerators and nodes.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Scale Up And Scale Out
On the scale-up side, here is the scary one showing HBM4 to switch bandwidth.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Memory Sharing Across XPUs
On the scale-up side there is a need to scale to hundreds of thousands of accelerators and beyond.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 AI Scaling
One of the neat features of the new chips is the option for co-packaged optics as well as either 512x 200G PAM4, or 1024x 100G PAM4.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Built For AI Scale
Using the 200G PAM4 option, the idea is that one can configure up to 512 XPUs on a single switch. (512 x 200G = 102.4Tbps.)
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 512 XPUs In A Scale Up Cluster
On the scale-out side, if you were only using 200GbE, that means that you have a bigger radix and thus can use fewer network switch layers.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Two Tier Scale Out
The advantage of using fewer switches and switch tiers is not the cost per switch. Usually the cost of new switches is higher than older switches. The savings comes from using fewer of them and fewer optics, cables, power, and so forth. It also saves on latency by having fewer hops.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Two Tier Vs Three Tier Networks
With Tomahawk 6, we get a new Global Load Balancing 2.0.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Global Load Balancing 2.0
The new Cognitive Routing helps balance load across the full network path. A simple model here is that as we get more devices operating at high speed, the network needs to get smarter on how it moves data around.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Cognitive Routing
We will let you read through this slide on Cognitive Routing 2.0.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Cognitive Routing 2.0
In addition, operators such as cloud providers constantly push for better telemetry.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Telemetry And Diagnostics
Broadcom also has a number of options for connecting devices that it had a slide on in the launch deck.
Broadcom 3 Pronged Approach To AI Interconnect Cost And Power
The company makes not just switches, but also NICs and more.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Full Stack Ethernet Innovation
Here is the Scale-Up Ethernet diagram for folks.
Broadcom Open Scale Up Innovation With Scale Up Ethernet SUE
Broadcom’s switches and NICs are used all over.
Broadcom Ethernet Switch NIC Ecosystem
The summary is basically that Tomahawk 6 is a 102.4Tbps switch that supports up to 1.6Tbps links and has different SerDes options.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Summary
Along with that there are also several new features to handle the higher speeds.
Final Words
Over the past few weeks I have seen three different Tomahawk 6 switches. These have been listed simply as 102.4T switches before this announcement. For a lot of folks, 102.4Tbps is an arbitrary number. We have seen numbers in the 1200-1700Tbps of global Internet bandwidth in recent years just to put that number into some perspective. To be clear, the move toward UltraEthernet and faster switching is great, as is the ability to scale out to larger network topologies with fewer layers of switching. In a world of growing AI clusters, networking is a significant cost, and consumers a notable amount of power. Broadcom now has the big switch ASIC in the market.
Broadcom Tomahawk 6 100G BCM78910
A major challenge Broadcom is facing more generally is that NVIDIA is effectively closing its accelerator ecosystem to non-NVIDIA NICs and PCIe switches. Broadcom also makes many custom XPUs and AI accelerators, so it is a heavyweight in the AI space. It feels a bit like the market is starting to bifurcate.
NVIDIA Just Ended Broadcom’s Chances in a Traditional AI Segment with This by Patrick Kennedy
$4000+ of BOM Opportunity Locked Out
Read on Substack
Hopefully we will get to take apart a Tomahawk 6 switch soon. The last Tomahawk one we did was in the Tomahawk 4 era:
In the 51.2T switch era, we took apart a
Marvell Teralynx 10
switch if you want to see inside a current generation switch.

data.author: june3739
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应对PayPal账户上的信用卡测试和欺诈交易问题

不同观点：
• **[patio11]** 认为攻击者的动机可能是测试信用卡/凭证是否有效，以便将来进行更大规模的欺诈。攻击者通过小额交易筛选出有效的信用卡，然后转卖或进行更大金额的盗刷。他建议通过增加 heuristics（启发式方法）检测异常行为，并主动退款或审查可疑交易。

• **[cookiengineer]** 提出这可能是洗钱计划，利用PayPal API的漏洞在不同子域之间混合交易。他还强调PayPal支持团队的效率问题，建议通过封锁已知恶意ASN、虚拟化软件环境和强化安全措施（如禁用SSH密码认证）来防御攻击。

• **[tyingq]** 提供了一个简单的解决方案，建议配置PayPal账户以拒绝未验证的买家，从而减少欺诈交易的可能性。

• **[Foofoobar12345]** 认为攻击者是在测试被盗的PayPal账户，可能会在未来进行更大金额的交易。他分享了自己的经验，指出与PayPal支持交涉无果后最终关闭了PayPal支付。

• **[abxyz]** 强调手动审查和账户批准的重要性，建议联系PayPal的账户经理而非前线支持，以获得更有效的解决方案。此外，提出如果依赖的服务商无法提供直接支持，应考虑更换服务商。

• **[imdavidsantiago]** 认为这是自动化退单滥用，建议通过浏览器指纹识别、行为跟踪、引入轻量级CAPTCHA等技术手段来减缓攻击。

• **[noodlesUK]** 警告PayPal对风险账户的严格处理，建议迅速解决问题或准备切换到其他支付服务商。

• **[dabinat]** 通过增加指纹识别和限速成功缓解了问题，认为减缓攻击者的攻击速度是有效的策略。

• **[Huxley1]** 通过添加CAPTCHA和监控可疑IP地址来阻止攻击，并指出联系PayPal的商户服务团队有助于减少欺诈。

• **[Beijinger]** 除了建议拒绝未验证买家外，还提出应考虑长期依赖PayPal的风险，建议通过法律手段和ICANN举报恶意域名。

• **[aga98mtl]** 建议将订单设为"待定"，并要求通过SMS验证以阻止攻击者。

data.title: UK tech job openings climb 21% to pre-pandemic highs
data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary: 根据Accenture的研究，英国科技职位空缺增加了21%，达到疫情前的高峰，尤其在人工智能（AI）领域需求激增，AI相关职位需求同比增长近200%。伦敦占据了全国AI职位发布的80%，而近三分之二的科技职位空缺也在伦敦。尽管有169万人自称具备科技技能，但区域间AI技能提升的差距引发对数字鸿沟的担忧。伦敦公司计划将五分之一的科技预算用于AI，而其他地区如英格兰东北部、苏格兰和威尔士的投入较少。PwC的研究显示，AI应用较多的行业，如软件行业，实现了更高的生产率和工资增长。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国技术岗位的就业市场情况，特别是薪资水平和就业机会的质量。

不同观点：
• [tetris11] 认为虽然开放的岗位在增加，但薪资和长期合同并没有相应增长。他指出，同样的职位会在LinkedIn上反复出现，可能是虚假的招聘信息，或者这些工作变成了临时合同。对于入门级技术人员来说，职位要求仍然很高，求职者可能需要夸大自己的能力或接受降薪才能获得工作。

• [rgavuliak] 同意英国的技术岗位薪资较低，尤其是在伦敦的公司，考虑到生活成本后，薪资显得更加不理想。

• [jpgvm] 指出英国拥有深厚的AI和数学人才储备，以及大量的硬件和FPGA人才。他认为相对于湾区的薪资水平，更多AI专注的公司应该在伦敦设立卫星办公室，但目前这种情况并不多见。

• [dyl000] 则认为英国的技术岗位市场相对美国要好得多，并表示美国的情况更糟糕，对美国的求职者表示同情。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于英国技术岗位市场的真实状况，特别是薪资水平和就业机会的质量。一些评论者（如[tetris11]和[rgavuliak]）认为薪资较低且合同不稳定，而另一些评论者（如[jpgvm]和[dyl000]）则认为英国市场拥有良好的发展潜力和相对较好的就业机会。

• 对于入门级技术人员来说，职位要求高和薪资不匹配是一个主要问题，这使得新进入市场的求职者面临更大的挑战。

• 讨论还涉及国际比较，特别是与美国和湾区的比较，表明英国技术岗位市场的表现可能在国际背景下有不同的评价。

44190120.article_content:
AI + ML
2
UK tech job openings climb 21% to pre-pandemic highs
2
Accenture points to AI hiring spree, with London dominating demand
Lindsay Clark
Thu 5 Jun 2025
//
09:48 UTC
UK tech vacancies are up by 21 percent to hit their highest levels since before the pandemic, according to research from Accenture.
... regions outside of London will also need to compete for talent and infrastructure
The global consultancy found a surge in demand for AI skills, which increased nearly 200 percent in a year. London accounted for 80 percent of AI-related job postings across the UK, while nearly two-thirds of technology vacancies as a whole were in London.
Accenture collected data from LinkedIn in the first and second week of February 2025, and supplemented the results with a survey of more than 4,000 respondents conducted by research firm YouGov between July and August 2024.
The research found a 53 percent annual increase in those describing themselves as having tech skills, amounting to 1.69 million people reporting skills in disciplines including cyber, data, and robotics.
Accenture tech lead Emma Kendrew commented: "The UK has a golden opportunity to establish itself as a global AI leader, and London is at the epicenter. The UK is seeing hotspots of tech talent emerge which we expect to grow as AI is more widely adopted.
"However, to fully capitalize on the economic potential of AI, regions outside of London will also need to compete for talent and infrastructure to achieve sustainable growth and unlock opportunities. The disparity in regional upskilling in AI raises concerns about a growing digital divide in the UK and could hurt long-term competitiveness."
AI hype fuels pay rise – but only if you're in the right gig
What will UK government workers do with an extra 26 minutes a day?
Best pricing model for AI? Work in progress, says Salesforce
Barclays Bank signs 100k license Copilot deal with Microsoft
The research found that London-based companies said they would allocate a fifth of their tech budgets to AI this year, compared to 13 percent who said the same and were based in North East England, Scotland, and Wales.
Earlier this week,
research by rival consultancy PwC
found that sectors where AI can be readily used for some tasks – including the software industry – are achieving higher productivity and wage growth than others.
Growth in revenue per employee increased during the period when LLMs emerged, from 7 percent annually between 2018 and 2022 to 27 percent between 2018 and 2024. Meanwhile, growth in the same measure fell slightly in industries less affected by AI, such as mining and hospitality, the researchers said. ®
